## Part IX — Operating guide

Parts I–VIII explain what the tool is, how it works and where it breaks. This part is for the person — or the agent — who has to **run** it: what to do every time, what to do when something goes wrong, how to put guard rails around it, how to carry the idea over to other kinds of material, and the questions that come up most.

| Section | Use it when |
|---|---|
| [58. Best practices](#58-best-practices) | before and during a job: rules, checklists, anti-patterns |
| [59. Troubleshooting](#59-troubleshooting) | a message you do not understand, or state that looks wrong — includes a **read-only state auditor** and a helper for the one hand edit the tool allows |
| [60. Driving the tool from an agent](#60-driving-the-tool-from-an-agent) | a model, not a person, types the commands — includes a **guard wrapper** and a tested driver |
| [61. Adapting the methodology to other domains](#61-adapting-the-methodology-to-other-domains) | you want the same discipline for something other than lines of text |
| [62. FAQ](#62-faq) | quick answers |

Three small programs in this part were **written for this guide** and are not in the archive: `state_audit.py` ([§59.2](#592-a-read-only-state-auditor)), `release_lock.py` ([§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch)) and `asm_guard.py` ([§60.3](#603-the-guard-wrapper)). All three use only the Python standard library, all were run against the scenarios of [Appendix D](#appendix-d--how-this-guide-was-verified), and their source is printed in full: read it before you run it.

**References used in this part.** **V***n* are the entries of the [register of deviations](#562-index); **S***n* the [trust findings](#572-findings); **L***n* the [stated limitations](#55-stated-limitations-and-their-verification-status) of the tool's own documentation; **BP***n* the best-practice rules below.

---

### 58. Best practices

Each rule below exists because something in [Part VIII](#part-viii--guarantees-limits-and-verified-caveats) happens without it. They are numbered **BP1 … BP52** so that the checklists, the agent rules of [§60.5](#605-rules-to-give-the-agent) and the FAQ can point at them. Where a rule says "because" and names a V, S or L entry, the entry has the evidence.

#### 58.1 The ten rules that matter most

1. **Version control is the only real undo.** Start from a clean, committed tree; commit after every batch (BP1, BP45).
2. **One command at a time, from the project root, with one spelling per path** (BP3–BP5).
3. **Look before you write.** `show-file` for every ID; read the `line_count` that `register` prints (BP7, BP11).
4. **`validate-plan` is the last thing before applying, and the first thing to repeat after adding anything** (BP25).
5. **Apply one descriptor at a time for work that matters, and read every result** (BP32, BP33).
6. **Treat `undo-descriptor` as final** — never as a redo (BP38).
7. **Declare an independent invariant for what the batch is meant to achieve**: written from the untouched source, with a negative control (BP21).
8. **After any unclean stop, follow the protocol — never "just retry"** (BP35, BP40).
9. **Never type a batch ID or a line ID; copy them from the tool's output** (BP11, BP29).
10. **Treat `.operational-platform/` as part of the project**: commit it, keep it confidential, run the auditor on it (BP46, BP47).

#### 58.2 Setup

| BP | Rule | Because |
|---|---|---|
| **BP1** | Start from a **clean, committed working tree** (`git status`, or your VCS's equivalent) before `new-batch`. | The tool has no whole-batch rollback; per-descriptor undo has holes (V1, V12, V23, V24); a crash can leave a file half-way ([§48](#48-concurrency-atomicity-and-crash-windows)); `register --force` re-mints IDs. Version control is the one recovery that always works — the first rule of the tool's own limitations page ([§48.5](#485-after-an-unclean-stop-a-protocol)). |
| **BP2** | Obtain the skill from a source you trust, keep its directory **read-only**, and run the tool with a sane `PATH`. | The scripts directory is first on `sys.path` (S5); `validate-post` runs whatever `node` resolves to (S6). |
| **BP3** | Start every session **in the project root**: `pwd`, then `cli.py resume`. | State is found by walking *upward* from the current directory, and any command — even a read-only one — creates `.operational-platform/` where none is found ([§43.1](#431-root-discovery-and-the-state-directory), S8). From a subdirectory, relative paths still mean "relative to the root" (V19). |
| **BP4** | Run **one command at a time** per project — also from an agent harness that parallelizes tool calls. | There is no locking: lost updates, and two `apply-next` can both apply ([§48.1](#481-what-is-atomic-and-what-is-not)). |
| **BP5** | **One spelling per file**: relative to the root, no `./`, forward slashes, no `..`, no trailing slash — the same string in `register`, `--file`, `--files`, `--checked-against`, `--src-file`, `--dest-file`, `require-file`. | `file_id` is a hash of the string, so two spellings are two files and the conflict graph cannot see their overlap (V3). |
| **BP6** | Register **every file the job will touch** and every file that may *mention* what is changing, before analysis. | The cascade search sees registered files only ([§30.4](#304-how-the-candidate-search-works)); an invariant on an unregistered file fails only at `validate-post` (V8). |
| **BP7** | Read the `line_count` in the `register` reply. For a file that exists, `0` means the path is wrong. | `register` of a nonexistent path succeeds, and `insert_after START` then creates the file (V19). |
| **BP8** | Normalize line endings, the final newline and unusual separators in a **separate, reviewed commit** before registering. | The line model rewrites bytes the batch never targeted (V7). |
| **BP9** | Keep out of scope: binary and non-UTF-8 files, files that contain form feeds, vertical tabs or U+2028, and anything that needs a file **deleted or renamed**. | Refused or silently rewritten (V7, E10); not supported ([§40.2](#402-choosing-the-right-operation)). |
| **BP10** | Note the Python and Node versions you ran with. | Everything in this guide was observed on CPython 3.13.16 and Node 22.22.0; Python 3.14 changes the default `tarfile` filter (S1). |

#### 58.3 Planning

| BP | Rule | Because |
|---|---|---|
| **BP11** | `show-file` before every `add-descriptor`; copy IDs from its output (or from a descriptor's `created_ids`). Never build an ID by hand or use a line number. | IDs are permanent identities, not positions ([§22](#22-files-and-lines-identity-that-never-changes)); an ID from a stale or second registration can point at the wrong line (V3). |
| **BP12** | Check that `start` lies at or before `end`, by position. | An inverted range is accepted by `add-descriptor` and crashes `validate-plan` — and a descriptor cannot be removed (V6). |
| **BP13** | For `move_range` and `copy_range`: `dest` must lie **outside** the block, be **live** when the move runs, not be deleted or replaced by another descriptor, and not be protected. Use `move_range` — not `copy_range` — for `START`. Add `--depends-on` from the move to anything that touches `dest`. | `dest` is neither claimed, hashed nor checked (V5): the failures arrive at apply time, one of them after the file was already rewritten. |
| **BP14** | Put a block that must stay together in **one** multi-line payload. For several inserts at one anchor (or at `START`), add them in the *reverse* of the order you want, chain them with `--depends-on`, and check with `dry-run`. | Inserts at the same anchor stack in reverse (V17). |
| **BP15** | Check order **semantically**: each descriptor's target must still exist when its turn comes. | The planner obeys `--depends-on` without simulating the batch forward: "replace L2, then insert after L2" passes the plan and aborts mid-apply ([§39.2](#392-conflicts--and-why-a-declared-order-is-obeyed-not-judged), L4). |
| **BP16** | Write `--depends-on d0001,d0002` with **no spaces**. Pass a value that starts with `--` as `--option=value`. | An untrimmed ID fails only at `validate-plan` (V26); argparse mistakes the value for a flag ([§49.3](#493-argument-conventions)). |
| **BP17** | Use `--payload-file` for anything longer than a line or two. Never end `--payload-text` with a newline. An empty payload on `replace_range` writes **one blank line** — use `delete_range` to delete. | V7 (E4, E5, E9); [§40.12](#4012-payloads-and-shell-quoting). |
| **BP18** | Pass `--context` — a short substring of the live target text, at most 120 characters — whenever the target is not obvious. | It is the one check that an ID points where you meant: `context 'x' is not a substring of the live content at this target … likely pasted against the wrong location`. |
| **BP19** | With `add-descriptor-template`: quote the `--find` string, make sure it is not empty, limit it with `--file`, and look at `status` counts and `explain` of the first descriptor before validating. | `--find ''` matches **every** line (V27); a template covers every registered file. |
| **BP20** | `--domino-hint` is a regex: escape metacharacters (`foo\(`) or hint the bare identifier, and test it with `find-pattern`. Run `sync-domino-queue` **last**, right before `validate-plan` (it is idempotent). | An invalid hint wedges `domino-next` and `domino-resolve` (V9); a direct descriptor added after the last sync is never traced (V20). |
| **BP21** | Invariants: begin line-oriented patterns with `(?m)`; compile the pattern yourself first; give every `expected-count 0` a **negative control** (the pattern must match in the pre-state); register every file it names; write it from the **untouched source** and name what you checked with `--checked-against`. | Whole-text regexes with default flags, and errors surfacing only at `validate-post` (V8); the independence rule ([§29.5](#295-the-independence-warnings)). |
| **BP22** | Prefer several small invariants, one per intent, over one clever pattern; add `--type balanced_pairs` where brackets matter. | A failing invariant then names its cause; a clever one fails — or passes — for reasons nobody can read. |
| **BP23** | Declare a category at **project** scope only when every later batch must account for it. | It forces closure in all later batches and nothing removes it (V14). |
| **BP24** | Declare constraints for what must not change **before** the descriptors exist. | A protected range is checked at `validate-plan` ([§28](#28-constraints-and-protected-zones)); project-level ones have no removal command ([§39.4](#394-protected-zones)). |
| **BP25** | `validate-plan` is the **last** planning command: re-run it after every `add-*`, read its `warnings`, and fix one failure at a time. | Descriptors added after a pass are invisible to `apply`, and `apply-all` on an unvalidated batch exits 0 and applies nothing (V4); it reports only the first failing gate ([§32.2](#322-all-gates-in-the-order-validate-plan-runs-them)). |
| **BP26** | Keep batches **small** — tens to a few hundred descriptors — and split by dimension (rename first, then restructure); a breaking change gets its own batch. | Adding descriptors costs time quadratic in their number: 500 → 4.4 s, 1000 → 14.6 s, 2000 → 50.5 s, 4000 → 190.4 s ([§41.5](#415-cost-model-and-measured-scale)); a failed post-condition is easier to diagnose at ten descriptors than at fifty ([§40.9](#409-batch-size-and-several-batches-in-sequence)). |
| **BP27** | Do not add descriptors to a **half-applied** batch; put late additions in a new batch. | Re-validating a half-applied batch fails for descriptors that depend on applied ones (V22). |
| **BP28** | **Export a batch before you apply it**, and treat an import as a *plan*. | A batch exported after apply arrives as `committed` in untouched files, and `validate-post` passes there (V31). |
| **BP29** | Never type a batch ID — copy it from `new-batch` — and never delete a batch directory. | Numbering is *count + 1*, and an unknown ID creates a phantom directory (V13); an ID is a path component (S2). |
| **BP30** | Use `dry-run` and `explain` to *look*, not to *check*; do not parse `dry-run` as JSON. | `dry-run` prints plain text and does not compare hashes (V16). |

#### 58.4 Applying

| BP | Rule | Because |
|---|---|---|
| **BP31** | Run `check <batch> <descriptor>` whenever something may have changed the files since planning — a formatter, a colleague, another tool, a long pause. | `validate-plan` compares no hashes ([§25](#25-hashes-payloads-and-the-compare-and-swap-check)); `check` and an `abort` use the same comparison ([§39.6](#396-abort-the-file-changed-under-the-plan)). |
| **BP32** | For work that matters, loop `apply-next` and **read each result**. Use `apply-all` only for a batch you trust, and never in a pipeline that ignores the exit code and the content of its reply. | `apply-all` prints no progress when it dies on an exception (V30) and applies nothing on an unvalidated batch (V4). |
| **BP33** | Stop on any result other than `applied` or `done`. `recovered` → look at the file before going on. `abort` → [§39.6](#396-abort-the-file-changed-under-the-plan). Anything unrecognized → stop. | `recovered` is also the false result of an undo (V1) and the result of a crash retry that may have duplicated text (V2). |
| **BP34** | After a non-zero exit from `apply-all`, run `status` **before** deciding anything. | V30. |
| **BP35** | After any unclean stop follow the protocol of [§48.5](#485-after-an-unclean-stop-a-protocol) and run the auditor. **Never retry** an `insert_after` or `copy_range` whose text is already in the file. | Two of three crash windows duplicate silently (V2). |
| **BP36** | Do not edit managed files outside the tool while a batch is open. If you must, `check` every pending descriptor afterwards and re-plan whatever fails. | The next descriptor aborts, and an aborted batch can never be closed (V21). |
| **BP37** | **One operator per project at a time** — a person *or* an agent. | No locking of processes; the "locks" guard plans, not processes ([§33](#33-cross-batch-locks), [§48.1](#481-what-is-atomic-and-what-is-not)). |

#### 58.5 Undo and recovery

| BP | Rule | Because |
|---|---|---|
| **BP38** | Treat `undo-descriptor` as an emergency back-out of **one** descriptor, **final**. Do not `apply-next` afterwards; do not re-validate a batch after undoing a `replace_range` or `delete_range`; undo in the reverse order of application; never undo a `delete_range` or `move_range` once another descriptor has touched the neighboring lines. Put the corrected change in a **new** batch. | V1, V12, V23. |
| **BP39** | Assume that a descriptor which came back as `recovered` can never be undone. | V24. |
| **BP40** | After an `abort`, **stop**. Read `detail` and `last_abort`, find what changed the file, then follow [§39.6](#396-abort-the-file-changed-under-the-plan) and [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch). | An aborted batch can never be closed and keeps its locks (V21). |
| **BP41** | Roll a *whole batch* back with version control; then `register --force` any file whose **line structure** changed; then re-plan. | There is no undo for a batch, and `register --force` re-mints a file's IDs (V21). |

#### 58.6 Finishing

| BP | Rule | Because |
|---|---|---|
| **BP42** | Run `validate-post` after **each** batch, not once at the end. | It is the only thing that releases a batch's locks — even on `fail` ([§39.5](#395-cross-batch-locks), [§39.7](#397-a-failed-post-condition)). |
| **BP43** | Read a `pass` for what it proves: the syntax of `.py` and `.js` files, and the invariants you declared. Nothing about behavior. Run the project's own tests. | A batch with no invariants proves syntax at most; the tool knows nothing about your tests ([§45.9](#459-validate_post)). |
| **BP44** | Make `accept-match` the **last** step before the final `validate-post`. | Accepted matches are keyed by line number (L16). |
| **BP45** | Report from `status`, `validate-post` and `report` — not from memory — and **commit** the files and `.operational-platform/` together, naming the batch in the message. | [§35](#35-the-eleven-step-workflow) step 10; the trail is the evidence (S7). |

#### 58.7 Hygiene

| BP | Rule | Because |
|---|---|---|
| **BP46** | Run the **auditor** ([§59.2](#592-a-read-only-state-auditor)) before a session, after every batch, and after any crash, abort or import. | It recognizes the signatures of V1, V2, V3, V21, V25 and V31 that the tool itself never mentions. |
| **BP47** | Treat `.operational-platform/` with the confidentiality of the files it manages. | It keeps every payload and every replaced or deleted text in clear, and an export bundles the **whole** store (S10). |
| **BP48** | Import only archives you exported yourself; inspect others with `tar -tvzf`; prefer Python 3.14 or later; after an import `status` must show the descriptors as `pending`. | S1, V31, V13. |
| **BP49** | In automation, put a **wrapper** between the caller and the tool ([§60.3](#603-the-guard-wrapper)), and build command lines as argument arrays, never as shell strings. | S2–S4, S9, V26, V27. |
| **BP50** | Keep your own log of the decisions the tool does not record: accepted exceptions, why a batch was abandoned, which lock you released. | "Write the decision down: the tool will not" (V21); `inventory-resolve` overwrites with no WAL record (V29). |
| **BP51** | Do not repair state by hand — with the single exception of a stale lock entry (`release_lock.py`, [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch)). | Positions in `registry.json` only mean something together with the text of the files ([§52](#52-the-state-directory)). |
| **BP52** | Put a **timeout** and an output limit around every call made by an automated caller. | User-supplied regexes have no budget (S9). |

#### 58.8 Pre-flight checklists

**Before `validate-plan`**

- [ ] Every file registered, with the canonical spelling; `line_count` as expected (BP5, BP7).
- [ ] Every ID copied from `show-file` or `created_ids`; no inverted ranges (BP11, BP12).
- [ ] Every `move_range` / `copy_range` `dest` checked against BP13.
- [ ] `--depends-on` without spaces; the order is valid *semantically*, not just acyclic (BP15, BP16).
- [ ] Templates previewed with `status` and `explain` (BP19).
- [ ] `sync-domino-queue` run **last**; `domino-status` says `ready_for_plan` (BP20).
- [ ] Invariants have `(?m)` where needed, compile, have a negative control, and name the untouched source (BP21).
- [ ] A commit exists that contains the files as they are now (BP1).

**Before the first `apply`**

- [ ] `validate-plan` passed **after** the last `add-*` (BP25).
- [ ] If time has passed or anything else touched the files: `check` the descriptors (BP31).
- [ ] The batch is exported, if it is going to another project (BP28).
- [ ] The auditor is clean, or every finding is understood (BP46).
- [ ] Nobody — and no other agent — is running commands on this project (BP37).

**After the last `apply`**

- [ ] Every result was read; no unexpected `recovered` (BP33).
- [ ] `validate-post` passed, **with invariants declared**; the project's own tests ran (BP43).
- [ ] Surviving matches reviewed; `accept-match` last (BP44).
- [ ] `report` run; files and `.operational-platform/` committed together (BP45).

**After a crash, an abort or an import**

- [ ] Stopped. Nothing retried (BP35, BP40).
- [ ] `resume`, `status <batch>`, the tail of the WAL and the auditor read ([§48.5](#485-after-an-unclean-stop-a-protocol)).
- [ ] The file compared with version control; the decision taken per [§39.6](#396-abort-the-file-changed-under-the-plan) / [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch).
- [ ] The decision written down (BP50).

#### 58.9 Anti-patterns

| Anti-pattern | What happens | Do instead |
|---|---|---|
| **Apply first, validate later** — `apply-all` on a batch whose plan was never validated | Exit 0, `{"applied": []}`, nothing changed — and a script reads it as success (V4) | Validate last (BP25); treat an empty `applied` as a failure |
| **"Retry until it works"** after an `abort` or a crash | An abort never changes by itself; a retried `insert_after`/`copy_range` duplicates text (V2) | Read the detail; follow [§48.5](#485-after-an-unclean-stop-a-protocol) |
| **Undo, then redo** | `recovered` — a false green: status `applied`, file unchanged (V1) | New batch (BP38) |
| **Patch the plan by adding to a validated batch** | The addition is ignored (V4), or fails for dependents (V22) | Re-run `validate-plan`; late additions → a new batch |
| **One giant batch** | Quadratic cost; a failed post-condition is hard to diagnose | Small batches, split by dimension (BP26) |
| **An invariant counted from your own payload** | It proves the tool did what you told it, not that the job is done (§29.5) | Count from the untouched source; negative control (BP21) |
| **Editing files by hand while a batch is open** | The next descriptor aborts; the batch can never be closed (V21) | `check` first; re-plan (BP36) |
| **Hand-editing the registry to "fix" drift** | Positions no longer match text; every later hash check fails | `register --force` after restoring the files, then re-plan (BP41) |
| **Trusting `recovered`** | It means "the log says it was done" — after an undo or a crash retry that can be false (V1, V2) | Look at the file (BP33) |
| **Parsing `dry-run` as JSON** | It is plain text (V16) | Treat it as a human preview |
| **Parallel tool calls** | Lost updates, double apply (§48.1) | Serialize — the guard does it for you (§60.3) |
| **Typing a batch ID or a path from memory** | Phantom directories, wrong files (V13, V3, S2, S3) | Copy from the tool's output; use the wrapper |
| **Running from a subdirectory** | A stray state directory, or the wrong project's state (S8) | `cd` to the root, then `pwd` (BP3) |
| **Treating a passing `validate-post` as proof** | With no invariants it proves syntax at most (BP43) | Declare invariants; run the real tests |

---

### 59. Troubleshooting

This section answers "I see *this* — what now?" Start with the tables of [§59.1](#591-symptoms-causes-and-fixes), which are keyed by what the tool printed. If the state itself looks wrong, run the auditor of [§59.2](#592-a-read-only-state-auditor) first: it is read-only and tells you in a few seconds what the files, the registry and the logs think. If a batch cannot continue, [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch) says how to leave it properly. Every message is listed verbatim in [Appendix C](#appendix-c--message-catalog).

Three questions settle most cases (the first two are [§39.3](#393-the-two-most-useful-questions-after-any-failure)):

1. **What did the tool actually change?** `status <batch>`, `git diff`, `show-file`. A failed plan and an `abort` write nothing.
2. **Is the state still consistent?** The auditor answers this.
3. **Is the batch still usable?** After an `abort`, an undo of a replace or delete, a broken invariant or hint, or an inverted range, the answer is *no*, and the plan continues in a **new batch** ([§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch)): the tool has no command that removes or edits a descriptor, an invariant, a constraint or a category.

#### 59.1 Symptoms, causes and fixes

Exit codes are those of [§49.2](#492-output-and-exit-codes): `1` is a *reported* failure, `2` an argparse error or an uncaught exception.

##### Setting up

| You see | It means | Do |
|---|---|---|
| `{"error": "'nope.txt' is not registered -- run register_file first"}` | The file was never registered, or it is spelled differently from its registration (V3). The command to run is `register`. | `register` it, using the **same string** everywhere ([BP5](#582-setup)). |
| `register` replies `"line_count": 0` for a file that has content | The path does not lead where you think — wrong directory, a typo, a subdirectory ([§43.1](#431-root-discovery-and-the-state-directory)). The tool registered an empty phantom (V19). | Check `pwd` and the root. The phantom is harmless if nothing uses it; never add descriptors against it. |
| A new `.operational-platform/` appears in a subdirectory, or commands behave as if the project were empty | A command ran where no state exists below your root, or a parent directory holds a different project's state (S8). | Stop. Remove a stray directory that holds only empty `payloads/` and `batches/`; `cd` to the real root; look for `.operational-platform/` in the parents. |
| `IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: …` (exit 2) | `register` was given a directory. | Register the files in it, one by one. |
| `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte` (exit 2) | A file that is not UTF-8 (E10). | Out of scope ([BP9](#582-setup)). |
| `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '…'` from `--payload-file` or `import-batch` | These paths are read relative to the **current directory**, not the project root. | Use a path that resolves from where you are; mind S4. |

##### Planning

| You see | It means | Do |
|---|---|---|
| `{"error": "f_…_l00099 is not in the registry for f.txt"}` | The ID does not exist for that file: mistyped, taken from another file, or minted before a `register --force`. | `show-file` and copy the ID. |
| `replace_range needs payload_text` · `replace_range needs start and end` · ``insert_after needs `after` (a line_id, or the string START)`` · `move_range needs dest (a line_id to move the block after)` | A required option of that operation is missing. | [§24.2](#242-the-five-operations). |
| `unknown op 'frobnicate'; must be one of ['copy_range', 'delete_range', 'insert_after', 'move_range', 'replace_range']` | `--op` is checked by the engine, not by argparse. | Use one of the five. |
| `category 'NAMING' given but this batch has no taxonomy yet -- call add_category first …` | `--category` before any `add-category`. | `add-category` first. |
| `category 'TYPO' is not in this batch's taxonomy: ['NAMING']` | The code was never declared. | Declare it. A declared category can be neither removed nor renamed (L12). |
| `provenance=domino needs --domino-of pointing at the finding it traces back to` | A cascade descriptor without its parent. | Add `--domino-of d0001`. |
| `context 'not there' is not a substring of the live content at this target ('L2') -- likely pasted against the wrong location` | The ID points at other text than you meant. | `show-file`; correct the ID or the context. |
| `context is 130 chars; kept to <=120 …` | The context is too long. | Shorten it. |
| `f_…_l00003..f_…_l00001 resolves to an inverted range (3..1)` from `add-constraint` | `start` lies after `end`. | Swap them. **`add-descriptor` does not make this check** (V6). |
| `category 'NAMING' is already declared for this batch` · `category 'GHOST' was never declared with add_category` · `category 'NAMING' has no scope -- call set_category_scope first` | Taxonomy order of operations. | Nothing to repair; run the missing step. |
| `no invariant on 'f.txt' with pattern 'x' -- add_invariant first` (`accept-match`) | The pattern must equal that of an existing invariant on that file. | Copy it exactly. |
| `transferred_with_edit needs at least one descriptor_id` · `descriptor_ids not found in this batch: ['d0009']` | `inventory-resolve` with a missing or unknown ID. | Give existing descriptor IDs. |
| `no descriptor 'd0009' in this batch` · `no finding 'dm0009' in this batch's domino queue` · `no range 'ri0009' in this batch's inventory` | An unknown ID **in that batch** — check the batch ID too: an unknown batch behaves as an empty planning batch (V13). | `status` / `domino-status` / `inventory-status`. |
| `{"error": "StopIteration: "}` from `check <batch> <id>` | An unknown descriptor (the other commands say `no descriptor …`). | Harmless; use `status`. |
| `{"created": [], "count": 0}` from `add-descriptor-template` | No line matched. Not an error. | Check the text and `--file`. |
| `domino-next` or `domino-resolve` fails with `PatternError` every time | A `--domino-hint` is an invalid regex (V9). The hint cannot be edited. | The batch is wedged: new batch, with an escaped hint ([BP20](#583-planning)). |

##### Validating the plan

`validate-plan` reports **one** failing gate at a time ([§32.2](#322-all-gates-in-the-order-validate-plan-runs-them)); the complete list with every message is in [§51](#51-the-validate-plan-diagnostic-catalog).

| `validate-plan` says | Cause | Do |
|---|---|---|
| `shape_incomplete` · `materials_missing` · `taxonomy_incomplete` · `unit_category_matrix_incomplete` · `inventory_incomplete` · `domino_incomplete` | A declared mechanism is unfinished. The message names it. | Do the named thing — `sync-domino-queue` / `domino-next`, `close-category`, `close-category-file`, `inventory-resolve`, `register` — and run `validate-plan` again. |
| `schema_errors: ["d0001: f_…_l00002 was deleted earlier and is no longer addressable"]` | The target was removed or replaced by another batch, or by an **undo** of this one (V12). | The descriptor can never validate. New batch, with the new IDs from `show-file`. |
| `schema_errors: ["d0001: domino_of references 'd0099', which isn't a descriptor in this batch"]` | A typo in `--domino-of`. Descriptors cannot be edited. | New batch. |
| exit 2: `RangeInvalid: … resolves to an inverted range (3..1)` | An inverted range was accepted when it was added (V6). | New batch. |
| `protected_zone_violations: ["d0001 targets protected lines […] (vendored)"]` | The target lies in a protected range. | Change the target — or, if the zone is stale, [§39.4](#394-protected-zones). |
| `conflicts: ["d0001 and d0002 both target overlapping lines […] with no declared order between them …"]` | Two descriptors claim the same lines. | If both should apply: `--depends-on` in a **new** batch. Otherwise abandon one. |
| `conflicts: ["d0002: depends_on unknown descriptor d0042"]` | A typo — or a space after a comma (V26). | New batch. |
| `dependency_cycle: ["d0001", "d0002"]` | `--depends-on` loops. | New batch. |
| `cross_batch_conflicts: ["batch_0002 overlaps already-locked ranges from batch_0001: […]"]` | A validated, unfinished batch holds those lines. | Finish it (`apply-*`, `validate-post`); if it is abandoned, [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch). |
| `result: "pass"` with a `warnings` list | Not a failure. Typically the independence warning: `invariant on pattern '…' has no --checked-against, and this batch has payload-carrying descriptors -- confirm the expected count came from the untouched source …`. | Read each warning ([§29.5](#295-the-independence-warnings)); do not ignore it. |

##### Applying

| You see | It means | Do |
|---|---|---|
| `apply-next` → `{"error": "no apply_order on this batch -- run validate-plan first"}` | The batch was never validated. | `validate-plan`. |
| `apply-all` → `{"applied": []}` (exit 0) | Nothing was applied: the batch was never validated, or validated *before* its descriptors were added (V4), or nothing was pending. | `status <batch>`; `validate-plan`; apply again. |
| `apply-next` → `"result": "done"` | Every descriptor of `apply_order` is applied. | `validate-post`. |
| `abort` — `live content matches neither the expected pre-state (…) nor a plausible post-state. live hash …. Someone or something changed this file outside the batch -- re-plan rather than retry.` (exit 1) | The file changed since planning, **or** a crash left the file ahead of the registry in window A of a `delete_range` or `move_range` (V2). The file is untouched by this call. | [§39.6](#396-abort-the-file-changed-under-the-plan) and [§48.5](#485-after-an-unclean-stop-a-protocol); `git diff`; the auditor. |
| `abort` — `target no longer exists in the registry (… was deleted earlier and is no longer addressable). This batch needs re-planning, not a retry.` (exit 1) | An earlier descriptor of this batch removed the target — a semantic ordering the planner did not simulate (L4) — or a crash happened in window B of a `replace_range` or `delete_range` (V2). | Look at the file: if the change is already there the work is done. The batch is unfinishable: new batch, [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch). |
| `recovered` — `WAL shows this already completed; status reconciled, nothing re-applied` | The **log**, not the file, says the work was done. After a crash retry it is usually true. After an `undo-descriptor` it is **false** (V1). | Open the file. For `insert_after` and `copy_range` after a crash, look for duplicated text (V2). |
| Duplicated lines after a crash and retry | V2: window A or B of `insert_after` / `copy_range`. | Restore from version control; re-plan. Do not delete lines by hand while a batch is open. |
| exit 2 `LineNotFound: START is not in the registry for a.txt` at `apply-next` | `copy_range --dest START` (V5). | New batch; use `move_range`, or an ID. |
| exit 2 `RangeInvalid: move destination falls inside the block being moved` | `dest` lies in the block (V5). **The file was already rewritten**; the registry was not. | Restore the file from version control; `register <file> --force`; new batch. |
| exit 2 `LineNotFound: … was deleted earlier and is no longer addressable` from a move or copy | Its `dest` was deleted by an earlier descriptor (V5). | The descriptor cannot apply. New batch. |
| `apply-all` exits 2 with only `{"error": …}` | An exception interrupted the loop; the descriptors before it **were** applied but are not listed (V30). | `status`. |
| Several inserts at the same anchor land in the wrong order | V17. | A new batch, in the reverse order; or one multi-line payload. |
| A file's line endings or final newline changed | V7. | Expected for the first write to a file with mixed endings or no final newline. |

##### Undo

| You see | It means | Do |
|---|---|---|
| `d0001 has status 'pending', not 'applied' -- nothing to undo` (also for `'undone'`) | Only an `applied` descriptor can be undone. | Nothing. |
| `d0001: live content no longer matches what this descriptor produced -- something else changed it since, refusing to undo blind` (`replace_range`; for `insert_after` and `copy_range` the text ends at `refusing to undo blind`) | The lines were changed after the apply. | Undo the later change first, or restore from version control. The refused attempt still wrote `undo_start` to the WAL (V25). |
| `d0001: missing created_ids/pre_payload_ref, predates undo support` (also `missing pre_payload_ref …`, `missing created_ids …`) | The descriptor came out of a `recovered` outcome and never recorded what it created (V24). The message blames age, not the cause. | Undo by hand with version control, or write the inverse as a new descriptor in a new batch. |
| After `undo-descriptor`, `apply-next` says `recovered` | V1: the descriptor is `applied` again and the file is **unchanged**. | Treat undo as final ([BP38](#585-undo-and-recovery)); the auditor shows `status applied, yet the WAL records an undo of it`. |
| After undoing a `replace_range` or `delete_range`, `validate-plan` fails with `…was deleted earlier and is no longer addressable` | V12. | New batch. |

##### Validating the result

| You see | It means | Do |
|---|---|---|
| `validate-post` → `fail`, `"error": "1 descriptor(s) not yet applied: ['d0002']"` | A descriptor is `pending` or `undone`. | Finish applying. After an abort, the batch cannot be closed (V21) — [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch). |
| `validate-post` → `fail` with `"syntax": {"…/m.py": "SyntaxError: '(' was never closed at line 2"}` | A touched `.py` file does not parse. | A follow-up batch, or `undo-descriptor` for the one change. |
| `"syntax": {"…/m.js": "Node.js v22.22.0"}` | A `.js` file failed `node --check`; the text is only the last line of Node's stderr (V10). | Run `node --check m.js` yourself. |
| `validate-post` → `fail` with invariants whose `result` is `fail` | Surviving matches or a wrong count. | Read `matches`; `accept-match` for legitimate exceptions; otherwise a small follow-up batch ([§39.7](#397-a-failed-post-condition)). |
| exit 2 `PatternError: missing ), unterminated subpattern at position 1` | An invariant's regex does not compile (V8). The batch stays `validated` with its locks. | It can never be committed: new batch. |
| exit 2 `LineNotFound: file_id 'f_…' is not registered -- register it first` | An invariant names a file that was never registered (V8). | `register` the file and run `validate-post` again — verified: it then passes and commits. |
| `validate-post` passes, and the result is still wrong | Nothing was declared that could fail: no invariants, or vacuous ones (V8); or the descriptor was falsely `recovered` (V1); or the batch was imported already applied (V31). | The auditor; [BP43](#586-finishing). |
| An `expected-count 0` invariant passes, but you can see the text | `^` or `$` without `(?m)` (V8), or a pattern that never matched. | Test the pattern on the pre-state ([BP21](#583-planning)). |

##### State, batches and archives

| You see | It means | Do |
|---|---|---|
| `resume` suggests `validate-post` for a batch that is already `committed` | The checkpoint follows the last batch that *changed phase* (V15). | Read `resume` as a hint; run `status` on the other batches. |
| A batch you imported has been replaced, or its numbering collides | `new-batch` uses *count + 1* (V13). | The auditor reports `the next new-batch would be batch_000N, which already exists`. Never open a batch before `status`-ing the imported ID. |
| `status` shows `applied` for a batch you just imported | The archive was exported **after** the apply (V31). The destination files were never edited. | Do not trust it; re-plan in the destination ([BP28](#583-planning)). |
| `DeprecationWarning: Python 3.14 will, by default, filter extracted tar archives …` on `import-batch` | S1. | Import only your own archives. |
| `.operational-platform/_import_tmp/` left behind | A refused import (V13). | Delete it by hand — the only thing in the state directory that is safe to delete. |
| A lock that will not go away | The batch never reached `validate-post`: aborted, abandoned, or `validated` with an unusable invariant (V21). | [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch). |
| Python `TimeoutExpired` from `validate-post` (exit 2) | `node --check` ran for more than 10 seconds and the exception is not caught (*code-derived, not reproduced*). | Run the check yourself; keep the file out of the batch. |

#### 59.2 A read-only state auditor

**What it is.** `state_audit.py` reads `.operational-platform/` and the managed files, and reports what is inconsistent or about to go wrong. It does two jobs:

- **Consistency.** The registry, the files on disk, the blob store, the two logs, the locks and the checkpoint must agree with each other. The tool never checks this itself, and several of the findings of Part VIII leave exactly such disagreements behind.
- **Plan lint.** Checks on a plan that `validate-plan` does not make, for the failures that otherwise surface late: an inverted range (V6), the `dest` of a move or copy (V5), an invariant that cannot run or cannot fail (V8), an unusable domino hint (V9), descriptors the next apply will ignore (V4, V20), bytes the line model will rewrite (V7), a batch number about to be reused (V13).

It is **read-only**: it opens files only for reading, never imports the skill's modules (their storage layer creates directories as a side effect — even a read of a project with no state would create one), and it **compiles** the regular expressions it finds in the state but never runs them (S9). The read-only property was also checked mechanically — see [Appendix D](#d6-the-guides-own-programs).

**Run it**

```
python3 -I state_audit.py PROJECT_ROOT
```

| Exit | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| `0` | nothing found |
| `1` | findings were printed (ERROR, WARN or INFO) |
| `2` | no `.operational-platform/` under that root (nothing is created) |

Each finding is one line beginning `ERROR`, `WARN ` or `INFO `, sorted by level, followed by a summary line. **ERROR**: the state is inconsistent, or a command is certain to fail or do the wrong thing. **WARN**: a known hazard, an interrupted or abandoned situation. **INFO**: worth knowing, not necessarily wrong.

**What it checks**

| Area | Check | Level | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | live positions of a file are exactly 1…n; line IDs are well-formed; `next_seq` is above every minted sequence | ERROR | — |
| Registry ↔ disk | the file on disk has as many lines as the registry has live ones | ERROR | V2, V5 |
| | a registered file is missing (ERROR if the registry holds live lines for it, INFO if it holds none) | ERROR / INFO | V19 |
| | two registrations resolve to one file | WARN | V3 |
| Blob store | each blob's content hashes to its own name | ERROR | S1, S7 |
| Descriptors | status vocabulary; `payload_ref` / `pre_payload_ref` exist; `depends_on` names exist; every ID named exists in the registry; `apply_order` names descriptors | ERROR | — |
| Descriptors ↔ WAL | `applied` without `op_applied` | WARN | V31 |
| | `pending` with `op_applied` (crash in window C) | WARN | V2 |
| | `op_start` without `op_applied` (an interrupted apply) | WARN | V2 |
| | `op_start` logged more than once (a retried apply) | WARN | V2 |
| | `applied`, yet the WAL records an undo of it (the false `recovered`) | ERROR | V1 |
| | `undone`, with `op_applied` still in the WAL | INFO | V1 |
| | `applied` insert / replace / copy without `created_ids` | WARN | V24 |
| | `undo_start` without `undo_applied` | INFO | V25 |
| Validation log | a `pending` descriptor whose last apply aborted: WARN while the batch still holds locks, INFO once they are released | WARN / INFO | V21 |
| Batches | a `committed` batch with descriptors that are not applied | INFO | V15 |
| | a directory without `descriptors.json` (phantom) | INFO | V13 |
| | the next `new-batch` would reuse an existing batch ID | ERROR | V13 |
| Locks | a lock held by a batch that does not exist, or is `committed` or `failed`; an empty lock entry | WARN / INFO | V21 |
| Checkpoint | points at a batch that has no `descriptors.json` | WARN | V15 |
| Files | unreadable or corrupt JSON / JSONL | ERROR | — |
| **Plan lint** | an inverted range in a pending descriptor | ERROR | V6 |
| | `copy_range` with `dest START`; a `dest` that was deleted; a `move_range` whose `dest` lies inside its own block | ERROR | V5 |
| | a `dest` that puts the block inside a protected range | WARN | V5 |
| | an invariant whose regex does not compile; an invariant on an unregistered file | ERROR | V8 |
| | an invariant with `^` or `$` and without `(?m)` | WARN | V8 |
| | a `domino_hint` that does not compile | ERROR | V9 |
| | a `pending` descriptor missing from `apply_order` of a `validated` batch | WARN | V4 |
| | a direct, pending descriptor missing from the domino queue | WARN | V20 |
| | managed files with mixed endings, bare CR, a form feed or other separators (WARN); with no final newline (INFO) | WARN / INFO | V7 |

**Real output.** The projects below are the scenarios of [Appendix D](#appendix-d--how-this-guide-was-verified); the exit status is the real one. The consistency findings come first.

And the plan lint, on a batch that is full of pitfalls none of which is refused when it is added (`lint1`), on two descriptors that the next `apply` would ignore (`lint2`), on a plan that is clean (`lint4`), and after an import that left the next batch number taken (`numy`):

```
$ python3 -I state_audit.py projects/lint1
ERROR batch_0001/d0001: inverted range (f_e4723ca566_l00004 is line 4, f_e4723ca566_l00002 is line 2) -- validate-plan will crash with RangeInvalid, and a descriptor cannot be removed (V6)
ERROR batch_0001/d0002: copy_range with dest START -- apply will fail with LineNotFound; only move_range accepts START (V5)
ERROR batch_0001/d0003: dest f_e4723ca566_l00003 (line 3) lies inside the block being moved (lines 2-3) -- apply rewrites the file and THEN raises RangeInvalid, leaving the registry stale (V5)
ERROR batch_0001/d0005: domino_hint 'foo(' is not a valid regex (missing ), unterminated subpattern at position 3) -- domino-next and domino-resolve will fail for this batch, and the hint cannot be edited (V9)
ERROR batch_0001/invariant #1 ('a('): not a valid regex (missing ), unterminated subpattern at position 1) -- validate-post will fail with PatternError, and an invariant cannot be edited or removed: the batch can never be committed (V8)
ERROR batch_0001/invariant #2 ('x'): names file f_ef38f77bd0, which is not registered -- validate-post will fail with LineNotFound until that file is registered (V8)
WARN  batch_0001/d0004: the block would land inside the protected range f_e4723ca566_l00004..f_e4723ca566_l00005 (frozen tail) -- dest is not checked against constraints (V5)
WARN  batch_0001/invariant #3 ('^X'): ^ or $ without (?m) means the start or end of the whole TEXT, not of a line -- this passes vacuously (V8)
WARN  mixed.txt: mixed line endings (1 CRLF, 2 LF) -- the first write rewrites every line with one style (V7)
WARN  ff.txt: contains '\x0c' -- the tool treats these as line breaks (the registry counts more lines than an editor shows) and the first write turns them into newlines (V7)
INFO  nofinal.txt: no final newline -- the first write adds one (V7)
-- checked 4 file(s), 5 blob(s), 1 batch(es), 4 WAL record(s), 0 validation record(s): 6 error(s), 4 warning(s), 1 note(s)
[exit=1]

$ python3 -I state_audit.py projects/lint2
WARN  batch_0001/d0002: pending, but not in apply_order -- added after the last validate-plan, so apply-next and apply-all will ignore it (V4)
WARN  batch_0002/d0002: a direct descriptor that is not in the domino queue -- added after the last sync-domino-queue, so it is never traced (V20)
-- checked 1 file(s), 8 blob(s), 2 batch(es), 1 WAL record(s), 1 validation record(s): 0 error(s), 2 warning(s), 0 note(s)
[exit=1]

$ python3 -I state_audit.py projects/lint4
-- checked 1 file(s), 2 blob(s), 1 batch(es), 1 WAL record(s), 1 validation record(s): 0 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 note(s)
[exit=0]

$ python3 -I state_audit.py projects/numy
ERROR the next new-batch would be batch_0003, which already exists -- it would overwrite that batch's descriptors and invariants (V13)
-- checked 1 file(s), 2 blob(s), 2 batch(es), 1 WAL record(s), 0 validation record(s): 1 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 note(s)
[exit=1]
```

**What it cannot see.** The auditor is a set of structural checks, not a proof.

- **Reordering.** Disk and registry are compared by line *count*. A change that only reorders lines — the `RangeInvalid` case of V5 — leaves the counts equal. The auditor sees such a state only through its traces: the `op_start` without `op_applied` in the WAL and, while the descriptor is still pending, the plan lint on its `dest`. Compare with version control.
- **Content.** It never compares the *text* of a file with the registry's idea of it, and it does not know what you meant.
- **Whether an applied descriptor's change is really in the file.** It trusts an `applied` status unless the WAL contradicts it; it does not compare the descriptor's payload with the text.
- **A tampered trail.** The WAL and the validation log are plain text with no signature (S7); the auditor checks their shape, not their honesty.
- **Everything outside `.operational-platform/` and the registered files.**

**Finding → remedy.**

| Finding | First step |
|---|---|
| `ERROR … lines on disk but … live lines in the registry` | A crash or a rewrite left the file ahead of the registry. Stop; [§48.5](#485-after-an-unclean-stop-a-protocol). |
| `WARN … op_start was logged N times` | A retried apply: for `insert_after` / `copy_range` look for duplicated lines (V2). |
| `WARN … op_start without op_applied` | An interrupted apply. Compare the file with version control before any retry. |
| `ERROR … status applied, yet the WAL records an undo of it` | V1: the descriptor *says* applied; the file does not contain its change. Re-plan the change in a new batch. |
| `WARN … the last apply attempt aborted … keeps its locks` | V21: [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch). |
| `WARN … registered N times under different spellings` | V3: stop adding descriptors against either; decide the canonical spelling, restore from version control, `register --force` the right one. |
| `WARN … status applied but no op_applied in the WAL` | Typically an imported batch (V31), or a hand edit. Do not trust the status. |
| `ERROR … names file …, which is not registered` | `register` it; `validate-post` then works. |
| `ERROR … not a valid regex` (invariant or hint) | The batch cannot be finished: new batch. |
| `ERROR … the next new-batch would be batch_000N, which already exists` | Do **not** call `new-batch`. Resolve the numbering first (V13). |

**The program.** 340 lines, standard library only; printed in full so that you can read before you run. A static analysis with `vermin` 1.9.2 reports Python 3.6 as the minimum; it was *run* only on CPython 3.13.16 ([Appendix D](#d6-the-guides-own-programs)).

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""state_audit.py -- a READ-ONLY consistency check and plan lint for an
operational-platform state directory. Written for this guide; it is not part of the
original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I state_audit.py PROJECT_ROOT

Two kinds of finding:
  * consistency -- the registry, the managed files, the blob store, the WAL, the
    validation log, the locks and the checkpoint must agree with each other;
  * plan lint   -- things the tool's own validate-plan does not look at and that
    are known to go wrong later: inverted ranges (V6), the dest of a move or
    copy (V5), invariants that cannot run or cannot fail (V8), unusable domino
    hints (V9), descriptors the next apply will ignore (V4, V20), files whose
    bytes the line model will rewrite (V7), a batch number about to be reused (V13).

It never imports the skill's modules (their storage layer creates directories
as a side effect) and never writes anything; regular expressions found in the
state are compiled but never run. Exit status: 0 = nothing found, 1 = findings
were printed, 2 = no state directory.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

findings = []


def note(level, msg):
    findings.append((level, msg))


def load(path, default=None):
    try:
        return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return default
    except Exception as e:                      # corrupt JSON, bad encoding
        note("ERROR", f"{path.name}: unreadable ({type(e).__name__}: {e})")
        return default


def load_jsonl(path):
    out = []
    if not path.exists():
        return out
    for n, line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            out.append(json.loads(line))
        except Exception as e:
            note("ERROR", f"{path.name} line {n}: not valid JSON ({e}) -- every command that reads this log will fail")
    return out


def main(root):
    root = Path(root).resolve()
    sd = root / ".operational-platform"
    if not sd.is_dir():
        print(f"no .operational-platform directory under {root}")
        return 2

    reg = load(sd / "registry.json", {"files": {}})
    files = reg.get("files", {})

    # ---- 1. registry: shape, permutation of positions, next_seq, disk agreement
    all_ids = set()
    for fid, e in files.items():
        lines = e.get("lines", {})
        all_ids.update(lines)
        live = sorted(p for p in lines.values() if p is not None)
        if live != list(range(1, len(live) + 1)):
            note("ERROR", f"{e.get('path')}: live positions are not exactly 1..{len(live)} (gap or duplicate)")
        seqs = []
        for lid in lines:
            prefix, _, seq = lid.rpartition("_l")
            if prefix != fid or not seq.isdigit():
                note("ERROR", f"{e.get('path')}: malformed line id {lid!r}")
            else:
                seqs.append(int(seq))
        if seqs and e.get("next_seq", 0) <= max(seqs):
            note("ERROR", f"{e.get('path')}: next_seq {e.get('next_seq')} <= highest minted sequence {max(seqs)} -- IDs would be reused")
        p = Path(e["path"])
        p = p if p.is_absolute() else root / p
        if not p.exists():
            if live:
                note("ERROR", f"{e['path']}: registered with {len(live)} live lines but the file does not exist")
            else:
                note("INFO", f"{e['path']}: registered but absent on disk (0 lines) -- a phantom registration?")
        else:
            try:
                disk = len(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines())
            except Exception as ex:
                note("ERROR", f"{e['path']}: cannot be read as UTF-8 ({type(ex).__name__})")
                disk = None
            if disk is not None and disk != len(live):
                note("ERROR", f"{e['path']}: {disk} lines on disk but {len(live)} live lines in the registry -- the file and the registry have drifted")

    # ---- 1b. two registrations that resolve to the same file (a path spelled two ways, V3)
    by_target = {}
    for fid, e in files.items():
        q = Path(e["path"])
        q = q if q.is_absolute() else root / q
        by_target.setdefault(q.resolve(), []).append(e["path"])
    for target, spellings in by_target.items():
        if len(spellings) > 1:
            note("WARN", f"{target.name}: registered {len(spellings)} times under different spellings {spellings} -- each has its own IDs and positions, and editing through one leaves the other stale (V3)")

    # ---- 2. blob store: names are content hashes; references resolve
    blobs = {}
    pdir = sd / "payloads"
    if pdir.is_dir():
        for b in pdir.glob("*.blob"):
            h = hashlib.sha256(b.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
            blobs[b.stem] = h
            if h != b.stem:
                note("ERROR", f"payloads/{b.name}: content hashes to {h}, not to its own name (the store never re-hashes, so nothing else would notice)")

    # ---- 3. logs
    wal = load_jsonl(sd / "wal.jsonl")
    vlog = load_jsonl(sd / "validation_log.jsonl")
    start_counts = {}
    for r in wal:
        if r.get("event") == "op_start":
            k = (r.get("batch_id"), r.get("descriptor_id"))
            start_counts[k] = start_counts.get(k, 0) + 1
    started = set(start_counts)
    done = {(r.get("batch_id"), r.get("descriptor_id")) for r in wal if r.get("event") == "op_applied"}
    undo_s = [(r.get("batch_id"), r.get("descriptor_id")) for r in wal if r.get("event") == "undo_start"]
    undo_d = [(r.get("batch_id"), r.get("descriptor_id")) for r in wal if r.get("event") == "undo_applied"]
    undone_ever = set(undo_d)

    aborted = {}
    for r in vlog:
        if r.get("phase") == "per_op" and r.get("result") == "abort":
            aborted[(r.get("batch_id"), r.get("descriptor_id"))] = r.get("detail", "")

    locks = (load(sd / "active_locks.json", {"batches": {}}) or {}).get("batches", {})

    # ---- 4. batches
    batch_status = {}
    bdir = sd / "batches"
    for b in sorted(bdir.glob("batch_*")) if bdir.is_dir() else []:
        data = load(b / "descriptors.json")
        if data is None:
            note("INFO", f"{b.name}: directory without descriptors.json (a phantom batch created by asking about an unknown ID)")
            continue
        bid = b.name
        batch_status[bid] = data.get("status")
        descs = data.get("descriptors", [])
        ids = {d["descriptor_id"] for d in descs}
        order = data.get("apply_order", [])
        for x in order:
            if x not in ids:
                note("ERROR", f"{bid}: apply_order names {x}, which is not a descriptor")
        if data.get("status") == "committed" and any(d.get("status") != "applied" for d in descs):
            note("INFO", f"{bid}: committed, yet it has descriptors that are not applied (added or undone after the commit)")
        for d in descs:
            did = d["descriptor_id"]
            tag = f"{bid}/{did}"
            if d.get("status") not in ("pending", "applied", "undone"):
                note("ERROR", f"{tag}: unknown status {d.get('status')!r}")
            for ref in ("payload_ref", "pre_payload_ref"):
                if d.get(ref) and d[ref] not in blobs:
                    note("ERROR", f"{tag}: {ref} {d[ref]} is missing from payloads/")
            for dep in d.get("depends_on") or []:
                if dep not in ids:
                    note("ERROR", f"{tag}: depends_on {dep!r} is not a descriptor of this batch")
            for key in ("start", "end", "after", "dest", "undo_anchor"):
                v = d.get(key)
                if v and v != "START" and v not in all_ids:
                    note("ERROR", f"{tag}: {key}={v} is not in the registry at all")
            key = (bid, did)
            st = d.get("status")
            if st == "applied" and key not in done:
                note("WARN", f"{tag}: status applied but no op_applied in the WAL")
            if st == "pending" and key in done:
                note("WARN", f"{tag}: pending, yet the WAL has op_applied (crash after the WAL write: the next apply-next reports 'recovered')")
            if st == "pending" and key in started and key not in done:
                note("WARN", f"{tag}: op_start without op_applied -- an interrupted apply; inspect the file before retrying (insert/copy may double-apply, delete/move abort)")
            if st == "pending" and key in aborted:
                if bid in locks:
                    note("WARN", f"{tag}: the last apply attempt aborted -- the batch cannot be closed and keeps its locks; re-plan in a new batch and remove this batch's entry from active_locks.json (V21)")
                else:
                    note("INFO", f"{tag}: the last apply attempt aborted and the batch's locks are already released -- it stays unfinished for good (V21)")
            if start_counts.get(key, 0) > 1:
                note("WARN", f"{tag}: op_start was logged {start_counts[key]} times -- the apply was retried; for insert_after/copy_range look for DUPLICATED lines (V2)")
            if st == "undone" and key in done:
                note("INFO", f"{tag}: undone, but its op_applied is still in the WAL -- apply-next on it would report a false 'recovered' (V1)")
            if st == "applied" and key in undone_ever:
                note("ERROR", f"{tag}: status applied, yet the WAL records an undo of it -- apply-next after an undo reports a false 'recovered', so the change is not in the file unless something else put it back (V1)")
            if st == "applied" and d.get("op") in ("insert_after", "replace_range", "copy_range") and not d.get("created_ids"):
                note("WARN", f"{tag}: applied without created_ids -- undo will refuse ('predates undo support')")
    for k in undo_s:
        if undo_s.count(k) > undo_d.count(k):
            note("INFO", f"{k[0]}/{k[1]}: undo_start without a matching undo_applied (a crash mid-undo, or a refused undo -- V25)")
            break

    # ---- 4b. plan lint: what validate-plan does not look at
    pos_of = {}
    for e in files.values():
        pos_of.update(e.get("lines", {}))
    protected = list((load(sd / "project_constraints.json", {}) or {}).get("protected_ranges", []))
    registered_ids = set(files)
    text_anchor_free = lambda p: re.sub(r"\[\^?\]?[^\]]*\]", "", re.sub(r"\\.", "", p))
    for b in sorted(bdir.glob("batch_*")) if bdir.is_dir() else []:
        data = load(b / "descriptors.json")
        if data is None:
            continue
        bid = b.name
        descs = data.get("descriptors", [])
        zones = protected + list((load(b / "constraints.json", {}) or {}).get("protected_ranges", []))
        order = data.get("apply_order", [])
        for d in descs:
            if d.get("status") != "pending":
                continue
            did, op = d.get("descriptor_id"), d.get("op")
            tag = f"{bid}/{did}"
            ps, pe = pos_of.get(d.get("start")), pos_of.get(d.get("end"))
            if op in ("replace_range", "delete_range", "move_range", "copy_range") and ps is not None and pe is not None and ps > pe:
                note("ERROR", f"{tag}: inverted range ({d['start']} is line {ps}, {d['end']} is line {pe}) -- validate-plan will crash with RangeInvalid, and a descriptor cannot be removed (V6)")
            if op in ("move_range", "copy_range"):
                dest = d.get("dest")
                if dest == "START" and op == "copy_range":
                    note("ERROR", f"{tag}: copy_range with dest START -- apply will fail with LineNotFound; only move_range accepts START (V5)")
                elif dest in pos_of:
                    pd = pos_of[dest]
                    if pd is None:
                        note("ERROR", f"{tag}: dest {dest} was deleted earlier -- apply will fail with LineNotFound (V5)")
                    else:
                        if op == "move_range" and ps is not None and pe is not None and ps <= pd <= pe:
                            note("ERROR", f"{tag}: dest {dest} (line {pd}) lies inside the block being moved (lines {ps}-{pe}) -- apply rewrites the file and THEN raises RangeInvalid, leaving the registry stale (V5)")
                        for z in zones:
                            zs, ze = pos_of.get(z.get("start")), pos_of.get(z.get("end"))
                            if z.get("file_id") == d.get("file_id") and zs is not None and ze is not None and zs <= pd < ze:
                                note("WARN", f"{tag}: the block would land inside the protected range {z.get('start')}..{z.get('end')} ({z.get('reason') or 'no reason given'}) -- dest is not checked against constraints (V5)")
                                break
            hint = d.get("domino_hint")
            if hint:
                try:
                    re.compile(hint)
                except re.error as ex:
                    note("ERROR", f"{tag}: domino_hint {hint!r} is not a valid regex ({ex}) -- domino-next and domino-resolve will fail for this batch, and the hint cannot be edited (V9)")
            if data.get("status") == "validated" and did not in order:
                note("WARN", f"{tag}: pending, but not in apply_order -- added after the last validate-plan, so apply-next and apply-all will ignore it (V4)")
        dq = load(b / "domino_queue.json")
        if dq is not None:
            queued = {x.get("descriptor_id") for x in dq.get("entries", [])}
            for d in descs:
                if d.get("status") == "pending" and d.get("provenance") == "direct" and d.get("descriptor_id") not in queued:
                    note("WARN", f"{bid}/{d.get('descriptor_id')}: a direct descriptor that is not in the domino queue -- added after the last sync-domino-queue, so it is never traced (V20)")
        inv = load(b / "invariants.json", {"invariants": []}) or {}
        unfinished = data.get("status") != "committed" or any(d.get("status") != "applied" for d in descs)
        for n, v in enumerate(inv.get("invariants", []), 1):
            if not unfinished:
                break
            tag = f"{bid}/invariant #{n} ({v.get('pattern')!r})"
            if v.get("file_id") not in registered_ids:
                note("ERROR", f"{tag}: names file {v.get('file_id')}, which is not registered -- validate-post will fail with LineNotFound until that file is registered (V8)")
            if v.get("type", "occurrence_count") == "occurrence_count":
                pat = v.get("pattern", "")
                try:
                    rx = re.compile(pat)
                except re.error as ex:
                    note("ERROR", f"{tag}: not a valid regex ({ex}) -- validate-post will fail with PatternError, and an invariant cannot be edited or removed: the batch can never be committed (V8)")
                    continue
                bare = text_anchor_free(pat)
                if ("^" in bare or "$" in bare) and not rx.flags & re.MULTILINE:
                    effect = ("this passes vacuously" if v.get("expected_count") == 0
                              else "it can match only at the very start or end of the file")
                    note("WARN", f"{tag}: ^ or $ without (?m) means the start or end of the whole TEXT, not of a line -- {effect} (V8)")

    # ---- 4c. numbering: new-batch uses (number of batch_* entries) + 1
    if bdir.is_dir():
        n_existing = len(list(bdir.glob("batch_*")))
        nxt = f"batch_{n_existing + 1:04d}"
        if (bdir / nxt).exists():
            note("ERROR", f"the next new-batch would be {nxt}, which already exists -- it would overwrite that batch's descriptors and invariants (V13)")

    # ---- 4d. bytes the line model will rewrite (V7), for files not yet normalized
    for e in files.values():
        q = Path(e["path"])
        q = q if q.is_absolute() else root / q
        try:
            raw = q.read_bytes()
        except OSError:
            continue
        try:
            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            continue
        crlf = raw.count(b"\r\n")
        bare_lf = raw.count(b"\n") - crlf
        bare_cr = raw.count(b"\r") - crlf
        odd = [c for c in ("\x0b", "\x0c", "\x1c", "\x1d", "\x1e", "\x85", "\u2028", "\u2029") if c in text]
        name = e["path"]
        if odd or bare_cr:
            what = ", ".join(repr(c) for c in odd) + (", bare CR" if bare_cr else "")
            note("WARN", f"{name}: contains {what.strip(', ')} -- the tool treats these as line breaks (the registry counts more lines than an editor shows) and the first write turns them into newlines (V7)")
        if crlf and bare_lf:
            note("WARN", f"{name}: mixed line endings ({crlf} CRLF, {bare_lf} LF) -- the first write rewrites every line with one style (V7)")
        if raw and not raw.endswith((b"\n", b"\r")):
            note("INFO", f"{name}: no final newline -- the first write adds one (V7)")

    # ---- 5. locks
    for bid, claimed in locks.items():
        st = batch_status.get(bid)
        if st is None:
            note("WARN", f"active_locks: {bid} holds a lock but the batch does not exist")
        elif st in ("committed", "failed"):
            note("WARN", f"active_locks: {bid} is {st} but still holds a lock -- it will block overlapping batches")
        elif not claimed:
            note("INFO", f"active_locks: {bid} holds an empty lock entry")

    # ---- 6. checkpoint
    cp = load(sd / "checkpoint.json")
    if cp and cp.get("active_batch") and cp["active_batch"] not in batch_status:
        note("WARN", f"checkpoint points at {cp['active_batch']}, which has no descriptors.json")

    order = {"ERROR": 0, "WARN": 1, "INFO": 2}
    for level, msg in sorted(findings, key=lambda x: order[x[0]]):
        print(f"{level:5} {msg}")
    n_files = len(files)
    n_batches = len(batch_status)
    print(f"-- checked {n_files} file(s), {len(blobs)} blob(s), {n_batches} batch(es), "
          f"{len(wal)} WAL record(s), {len(vlog)} validation record(s): "
          f"{sum(1 for l, _ in findings if l == 'ERROR')} error(s), "
          f"{sum(1 for l, _ in findings if l == 'WARN')} warning(s), "
          f"{sum(1 for l, _ in findings if l == 'INFO')} note(s)")
    return 1 if findings else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print(__doc__)
        sys.exit(2)
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1]))
```

#### 59.3 Abandoning a batch

**There is no "abandon" command.** A batch that cannot continue stays where it is: its directory, its status, its descriptors and — if it was validated — its **locks** remain. The locks are the only part that harms anyone else, because they block every plan that touches the same lines (V21). Leaving a batch properly is therefore a short, manual procedure.

**When to abandon a batch** — whenever one of these is true:

| Situation | Entry |
|---|---|
| An `abort` — the file changed under the plan, or a crash left a delete or move aborting | [§39.6](#396-abort-the-file-changed-under-the-plan), V2, V21 |
| A descriptor that can never validate: `…was deleted earlier…`, an inverted range, an unknown `domino_of`, a cycle | V6, V12, [§51](#51-the-validate-plan-diagnostic-catalog) |
| An invariant or a hint with an invalid regex | V8, V9 |
| An `undo-descriptor` of a replace or delete, after which you still want to plan the region | V12 |
| A half-applied batch that needs additions | V22 |
| Anything that you decide, on reading the state, is no longer what you meant | — |

**The procedure.**

1. **Stop applying.** Run nothing else on the batch. If an agent is driving, stop it.
2. **Find out what is true.** `status <batch>`; the auditor; `git diff` (or your VCS's equivalent). Which descriptors are applied? Which of the files have the changes, and are they what you want?
3. **Decide the files.** Keep what is right. If an applied part is wrong, or the file drifted, restore the files from version control.
4. **Re-register where the line structure changed.** If you restored a file, or lines were added or removed outside the tool, `register <file> --force`. This **re-mints every ID of that file**, so every descriptor of every batch that names an old ID stops resolving: do it only when you are done with those batches. If only the *text* of lines changed, the IDs still resolve and this step is not needed.
5. **Release the batch's locks** — [`release_lock.py`](#the-helper), below. Run it without `--yes` first.
6. **Plan the replacement in a new batch.** `new-batch` (copy the ID it prints), new descriptors against the **current** IDs from `show-file`.
7. **Write the decision down** — in your log or the commit message: which batch, why, which lock you released. The tool records none of it (BP50).

**Leave the old batch directory in place.** It is the record of what was tried, and deleting it makes the next `new-batch` reuse its number (V13). Its status stays as it was — `validated`, with some descriptors applied and some pending — for good, and the auditor will keep reporting it at INFO level.

##### The helper

The one hand edit the documentation allows — removing a stale batch entry from `active_locks.json` — is easy to get wrong in an editor (the file is the only record of *other* batches' live claims). `release_lock.py` does exactly that edit and nothing else: it validates the batch ID, shows what it is about to remove together with the batch's status and descriptor counts, writes only with `--yes`, and writes the file the way the tool does (temporary file, then rename). It leaves no record in the WAL: that is yours to keep.

```
python3 -I release_lock.py PROJECT_ROOT BATCH_ID           # report only
python3 -I release_lock.py PROJECT_ROOT BATCH_ID --yes     # remove the entry
```

| Exit | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| `0` | done, or there was no lock to release |
| `1` | refused: not a batch ID, or `active_locks.json` is not in the expected shape |
| `2` | bad usage, or no state |

A real run — an `abort` strands `batch_0001`, a replacement plan in `batch_0002` is blocked by its lock, the lock is released, and the replacement validates, applies and commits:

```
$ cli.py apply-next batch_0001
{"result": "abort", "descriptor_id": "d0002", "detail": "d0002: live content matches neither the expected pre-state (4532a463920b) nor a plausible post-state. live hash f9e49c7473ff. Someone or something changed this file outside the batch -- re-plan rather than retry."}
[exit=1]
##### RL1: the state before the release
$ state_audit.py
WARN  batch_0001/d0002: the last apply attempt aborted -- the batch cannot be closed and keeps its locks; re-plan in a new batch and remove this batch's entry from active_locks.json (V21)
-- checked 1 file(s), 4 blob(s), 1 batch(es), 3 WAL record(s), 2 validation record(s): 0 error(s), 1 warning(s), 0 note(s)

$ release_lock.py batch_0009
```
