### 61. Adapting the methodology to other domains

`operational-platform` is the methodology of [Part II](#part-ii--the-methodology) specialized to one kind of unit — a line of UTF-8 text — and one kind of change — five line operations. Almost everything that makes it trustworthy has nothing to do with lines. This section says what carries over to other material, what a port must supply, and what to do differently now that the register of deviations is known.

> **Status of this section.** Everything in Parts I–VIII and in §§58–60 was observed or read from the source and is labeled that way. This section is **design guidance**: nothing in it was built or run, and no tool described here exists. Where it states a fact about `operational-platform` it cites the section that verified it.

#### 61.1 What carries over, and what does not

| Idea | In `operational-platform` | Depends on lines? |
|---|---|---|
| Analysis and correction are separate; nothing is edited while analyzing | no command both analyzes and applies ([§18](#18-anti-patterns)) | no |
| A unit has an identity that outlives its position | line IDs and the registry ([§22](#22-files-and-lines-identity-that-never-changes)) | needs *a* unit |
| The plan is data, and it records the before-state | descriptors with `pre_payload_ref`, `expect_hash`, `payload_ref` ([§24](#24-descriptors-the-five-operations)) | no |
| Reality is compared with the plan immediately before every write | the hash compare-and-swap and `abort` ([§25](#25-hashes-payloads-and-the-compare-and-swap-check), [§39.6](#396-abort-the-file-changed-under-the-plan)) | no |
| Intent and completion are logged around the write | the WAL, `resume` ([§34](#34-the-audit-trail-wal-validation-log-and-checkpoint), [§48](#48-concurrency-atomicity-and-crash-windows)) | no |
| The plan is checked as a whole before anything changes | the eleven gates ([§32.2](#322-all-gates-in-the-order-validate-plan-runs-them)) | partly: the gates are generic; what a descriptor *claims* is not |
| Success is re-derived from the artifact, not from the plan | invariants and `validate-post` ([§29](#29-invariants-and-accepted-matches)) | partly: the *kind* of check is domain-specific |
| Reversal is per unit and needs the recorded before-state | `undo-descriptor` ([§17](#17-requirements-that-building-a-tool-made-explicit), [§44.6](#446-undo_descriptor)) | no |
| Cascades are enumerated and each one is given a disposition | the domino queue ([§30](#30-the-domino-queue)) | the *search* is domain-specific |
| What the engine enforces and what stays judgment | [§20](#20-the-dividing-line-what-is-mechanized-and-what-stays-judgment) | no — and it must be redrawn for each domain |
| Registry positions and tombstones; `splitlines`; the five line operations; regular-expression search; `.py` and `.js` syntax checks | `registry`, `engine`, `validator` | **yes — these are the line-specific parts** |

#### 61.2 The five things a port must supply

1. **A unit with a stable identity.** Something addressable that keeps its identity when its neighbors change — and has a stated rule for when its *own* content changes. In the tool: `f_<hash>_l<seq>`, never reused, never recomputed from a position. *Test:* make three edits elsewhere; does a reference written before them still resolve to the same unit?
2. **A small closed set of operations, each with a defined before-state, a defined after-state and a defined inverse.** What the before-state fingerprint covers decides what the compare-and-swap protects. In the tool the fingerprint of an insert covers the *anchor*, not the insertion — which is why a crash retry can insert twice (V2).
3. **A fingerprint compared at the moment of writing, with three outcomes:** matches the before-state (apply), matches the after-state (already done), matches neither (**refuse** — never guess). The third outcome is the point of the design.
4. **A record of intent and completion, written so that a crash at any point can be classified** as *not started*, *finished* or *ambiguous* — and so that the ambiguous cases are refused rather than retried. The order of the writes (artifact, index, log, status) determines which windows exist ([§48.2](#482-the-crash-harness)).
5. **A check that does not use the plan.** Post-conditions evaluated from the artifact alone, written from the *untouched* source ([§29.5](#295-the-independence-warnings)). A system that verifies its own output against its own plan has verified nothing.

Two further needs depend on the domain: a way to **enumerate cascades** (the candidates of the domino queue need a searchable medium — text, a reference graph, a syntax tree), and a way to **express "must not change"** (protected ranges are claims on units; any port needs the same concept).

#### 61.3 Domain by domain

Starting points, not recipes. For each domain: what the unit and its stable identity are; a closed set of operations; what to fingerprint; what the independent check is; what is particular to the domain.

| Domain | Unit and stable identity | Operations | Before-state fingerprint | Independent check | Particular hazards |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Source code, by symbol** | a function, class or field; identity is a minted ID kept in a side index (the qualified name changes on rename) | replace body, insert member, delete, move, rename | hash of the symbol's source text | the project's tests and type checker; "no reference to the old name" from a parser, not a regex | a rename is a cascade across files: use the language's reference index for the candidates; formatters rewrite untouched code — fingerprint after normalization or refuse |
| **Contracts and policies, by clause** | a clause with a minted ID; the printed number is *derived*, because numbers change when clauses are inserted | replace text, insert, strike (keep a tombstone), move | hash of the clause text | every cross-reference resolves; every defined term is defined and used; no banned phrase; a lawyer's review | the cascade is semantic — a changed definition changes every clause that uses it — and the candidate search finds only *text*; the tool must never be the last reader |
| **Configuration (YAML, JSON, TOML)** | a key path (`a.b[2].c`); list items need a minted ID or a key | set, add, remove, rename key | hash of the value at the path, with its type | schema validation of the whole document; "no key named *old*"; a diff of the *parsed* document against the expected one | comments, anchors and key order do not survive parse-and-serialize (the V7 problem in another form): edit the text surgically, or refuse files that do not round-trip |
| **Database schema migrations** | an object — table, column, index, constraint — by qualified name | add, alter, rename, drop, backfill | hash of the object's **live definition** read from the catalog | the catalog diff against the target; row counts; constraint validation; a restore test | the artifact is live and shared, so the compare-and-swap must read the *live* catalog; the inverse of a drop is a restore, not a text edit; destructive steps need an approval gate |
| **Spreadsheets and models** | a cell or range, addressed by sheet and a **row key**, not a row number | set value or formula, insert or delete a row or column, move | hash of the formula and value | independent recomputation of the totals; no error values; formula consistency down a column | inserting a row shifts references — the drift of line numbers again, inside formulas; named ranges and hidden sheets are cascades with no shared text |
| **Documentation sets** | a section, by a stable anchor rather than its heading text | replace, insert, delete, move | hash of the section's text | every link and anchor resolves; terminology absent; tables of contents regenerated | renaming a heading breaks inbound links: the anchor *is* the identity, so it must survive a title change |
| **Localization catalogs** | a message key | add key, change source text, mark translations stale, remove | hash of the **source** text — what the translations were made from | every locale has every key; placeholders and plural forms preserved | a changed source must *invalidate* translations, not overwrite them; plural rules differ by language |
| **Infrastructure as code** | a resource address (`aws_s3_bucket.logs`) | change attribute, add, remove, move | the **deployed** state of the resource, not only the file | the platform's own plan shows exactly the expected changes and no others; policy checks | the artifact has a state that drifts on its own; some changes destroy and recreate; an undo may not exist — approval before any destructive step |
| **Datasets (CSV, JSON Lines, tables)** | a record, by primary key (create a key first if none exists) | update field, insert, delete, merge duplicates | hash of the record | row counts reconcile; uniqueness; referential integrity; distribution statistics against the source | scale: the quadratic planning cost of [§41.5](#415-cost-model-and-measured-scale) would dominate — partition the work; a bulk change needs a sampled review, not 100,000 descriptors |
| **Slide decks and designs** | a slide or an element, by minted ID | change text, restyle, move, delete | hash of the element's serialized state | render and compare; overflow, contrast and link checks | most checks are visual, so the independent check is a rendering plus a human; keep the mechanized part to text and structure |

#### 61.4 What to reuse and what to rebuild

| Component | Reuse? | Note |
|---|---|---|
| The six phases and the anti-patterns ([§7](#7-core-philosophy-three-stages-six-phases)–[§18](#18-anti-patterns)) | as they are | domain-free |
| The dividing line ([§20](#20-the-dividing-line-what-is-mechanized-and-what-stays-judgment)) | redraw it | the more semantic the unit, the more is judgment |
| The process model: a fresh process per command, all state on disk ([§41.3](#413-the-process-model)) | the design | add locking from the start |
| The storage design: temporary file and rename for JSON, append-only logs, content-addressed payloads | the design | add `fsync`; hash-chain the logs (S7) |
| The registry: positions and tombstones | **rebuild** | for keyed units it becomes a plain dictionary and the position arithmetic disappears |
| The apply algorithm: WAL check, then pre-state, write, index, log, status | the *shape* | fix the crash windows and the false `recovered` (below) |
| The plan gates | the list and its order | what a descriptor *claims* — the basis of conflicts and locks — is domain-specific |
| The domino queue | the discipline (queue plus gate) | rebuild the search for the medium |
| Invariants and `validate-post` | the idea | use the domain's real checkers: schema, referential integrity, tests, render |
| The CLI contract: JSON on stdout, exit codes, a `result` field | yes | add the guard of [§60.3](#603-the-guard-wrapper) from the first day |
| The guard, the auditor and the driver of Part IX | the design | the code is specific to this CLI and these file formats; generate the option table from the parser |

#### 61.5 Design a port that does not repeat the findings

Each row is a finding of the register and a design that would not have it. These are *suggestions*, labeled as such: none was built.

| Finding | A design that avoids it |
|---|---|
| **V2** — a crash retry duplicates an insert or a copy | Mint the new IDs and write them to the descriptor **before** the first write, and make the operation idempotent: "operation *X* is already in the artifact" is a question the artifact can answer. Or make the fingerprint cover the effect (the anchor **and** its successor) |
| **V1** — `recovered` after an undo, with the file unchanged | Version the log by *attempt*: an undo closes the attempt that an `op_applied` belongs to. Report "the log says done" and "the content shows done" as different results |
| **V24** — a recovered descriptor can never be undone | Mint IDs at plan time (see V2), so the record exists whatever happens at apply time |
| **V23** — undoing a delete restores the block in the wrong place | Store the *neighbors'* IDs with the deleted block, not an anchor that can move |
| **V4, V22** — a plan changes after validation | Any addition returns the batch to *planning*; apply refuses a descriptor that is not in the validated order; re-validation understands applied descriptors |
| **V6, V26, V27** — bad input accepted, failing late | Validate everything at the moment it is added: ranges, lists, regular expressions (compile), searches (non-empty) |
| **V8** — invariants with surprising semantics and late errors | Name the semantics in the invariant (per line or whole text); compile and resolve the file at add time |
| **V13, S2** — an unknown or hostile batch ID | IDs are minted only by the tool; an unknown ID is an error; the format is checked |
| **V21** — an aborted batch can never be closed | An explicit `abandon` command that releases the claims and records the decision |
| **V12** — an undo makes the region unplannable | Keep tombstoned IDs addressable for re-planning, or provide `re-plan` |
| **V3** — two spellings, two files | Canonicalize at the boundary (normalize, confine to the root), then hash |
| **V7** — bytes the plan never targeted are rewritten | Record each file's separators and final newline at registration and refuse a file that does not round-trip byte for byte |
| **V5** — the destination of a move is unclaimed | Claim and fingerprint **both** ends of every operation |
| **V17** — inserts at one anchor invert the order you wrote | Order inserts by an explicit, documented key |
| **V4, V30** — exit 0 with nothing applied; no progress on failure | Exit non-zero when nothing was applied; print each result as it happens |
| **V31** — an export taken after apply imports as applied | An export carries a *plan*; an import resets every status to pending |
| **S3, S4** — paths not confined | Resolve and confine every path inside the tool, not in a wrapper |
| **S7** — the trail is not tamper-evident | Hash-chain the log and copy it off the machine after each batch |
| **S9** — regular expressions with no budget | A linear-time engine, or a time limit inside the tool |
| no locking, no `fsync` ([§48.1](#481-what-is-atomic-and-what-is-not)) | A lock per project, taken by the tool itself; `fsync` the file and then the directory |

#### 61.6 Acceptance tests for a port

A port is not finished when its commands run; it is finished when these hold. Each is modeled on a scenario of [Appendix D](#appendix-d--how-this-guide-was-verified), so that a port can be tested the way this tool was.

1. **Identity.** Apply three edits above a target; a reference to the target written *before* them still resolves to the same unit.
2. **Staleness.** Change the target between plan and apply: the apply aborts and writes nothing.
3. **Crash windows.** For every operation, kill the process between every pair of writes; the retry either finishes correctly or **refuses**. It never duplicates. (The tool fails this test for two operations — V2.)
4. **Undo.** For every operation, apply and undo give back the original bytes. After a recovered crash, undo works or refuses *with the true reason*. (The tool fails: V23, V24.)
5. **Independence.** A plan that is internally consistent but wrong — a payload that still contains the old name — is caught by an invariant written from the source.
6. **Overlap.** Two valid plans over the same unit are refused at plan time, and an abandoned plan's claim is neither silently kept nor silently dropped.
7. **Boundary.** Hostile IDs, paths and patterns are refused, and so are empty searches and inverted ranges — **at the moment they are added**.
8. **Round trip.** A batch that applies nothing leaves every artifact byte-identical.
9. **Concurrency.** Two simultaneous commands on one project cannot both apply the same descriptor.

#### 61.7 When not to port

The overhead is justified when changes are numerous, interdependent and checkable. For one obvious change, use the editor and version control — the skill's own advice is the same ("don't reach for it for a single, obvious one-line fix"). And where the medium already has a transactional store with its own history — a database with transactions, a repository with commits — use it, and take from this tool only the *method*: separate analysis from correction, record the before-state, refuse on mismatch, and verify the result from the artifact rather than from the plan.

### 62. FAQ

Each answer is short and points to the entry that has the evidence. The questions are numbered **Q1 … Q41** so that other documents can cite them.

#### 62.1 What it is

**Q1. What is it, in one sentence?** A command-line tool — `scripts/cli.py`, 38 subcommands over seven Python modules, 3,044 lines, standard library only — that applies a *plan* of line-level edits to text files, with each edit addressed by a permanent line ID, compared with a hash of what the plan expected, logged around the write, and verified at the end by conditions re-derived from the files ([§1](#1-what-this-is)).

**Q2. Does it call a model, the network, or git?** No, no and no. The seven modules import only `argparse`, `hashlib`, `json`, `os`, `pathlib`, `re`, `shutil`, `subprocess` (to run `node --check`), `sys`, `tarfile`, `time` and `typing` — nothing that talks to a network — and the only mention of git is a comment ("the same convention as `.git/`"). The model is the *caller*, never something that the tool calls: the tool is built to be driven by one ([§60](#60-driving-the-tool-from-an-agent)). *(Code-derived.)*

**Q3. Which Python version does it need?** A static analysis with `vermin` 1.9.2 finds nothing that *executes* newer than Python 3.7. The source writes annotations such as `list[dict]` that only a 3.9+ interpreter could evaluate, but every module starts with `from __future__ import annotations`, so they never are. This is a *static* result: the only interpreter this guide ran was **CPython 3.13.16**. Known effects of newer versions: on 3.12–3.13 `import-batch` prints a `DeprecationWarning` (m11, S1); on 3.14 the default tar filter changes (S1). The guard of [§60.3](#603-the-guard-wrapper) needs 3.9. Node.js is needed only for the `.js` syntax check; without it the check is `skipped`.

**Q4. Does it run on Windows?** Not tested. One thing to know in advance: a file's ID is a hash of its path *as written*, so `a\b.py` and `a/b.py` would be two files (V3). The guard's lock needs `fcntl` and is skipped where it does not exist.

**Q5. What does it write besides the files I register?** Its state directory `.operational-platform/` — created in the current directory by **any** command, a read-only one included, when no state is found above it (S8, [§43.1](#431-root-discovery-and-the-state-directory)); `export-batch` writes `./<batch_id>.tar.gz` unless told otherwise; a refused `import-batch` leaves `.operational-platform/_import_tmp/`. Nothing else.

**Q6. Can it create, delete or rename files?** It can create one — `register` a path that does not exist, then `insert_after START` ([§40.5](#405-creating-a-new-file)); missing parent directories are created too. It cannot delete or rename: deleting every line leaves an empty file, and a file's identity *is* its path ([§40.2](#402-choosing-the-right-operation)). A typo at `register` silently registers an empty phantom file (V19).

**Q7. Can it edit binary or non-UTF-8 files?** No. `register` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` for non-UTF-8 content (E10). Files that contain form feeds, vertical tabs or U+2028, mixed line endings or no final newline are rewritten in a way you did not ask for (V7, BP8, BP9).

**Q8. Which of the 38 commands do I need?** For a plain job, eleven: `register`, `show-file`, `new-batch`, `add-descriptor`, `add-invariant`, `validate-plan`, `apply-next`, `validate-post`, `status`, `resume`, `report` — plus `check` and `undo-descriptor` when something goes wrong. Taxonomy, constraints, the domino queue, the inventory, templates and the cross-file commands are for jobs that need them; without a `--shape`, nothing is required ([§16](#16-task-shapes), [§35](#35-the-eleven-step-workflow)). The driver of [§60.4](#604-a-reference-driver) runs a complete batch with only those.

#### 62.2 Planning

**Q9. `register` accepted a path I mistyped. Why?** It accepts any path and registers a missing one as an empty file with `line_count: 0` (V19). Read `line_count` every time (BP7).

**Q10. Can I edit or remove a descriptor, an invariant, a constraint or a category?** No command does either ([§56.1](#561-how-to-read-an-entry)). A batch that holds something that can never validate is finished; the remedy is a new batch ([§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch)).

**Q11. Can a descriptor edit text that another descriptor of the *same* batch inserts?** No. The IDs of inserted lines are minted when the descriptor is **applied** (`created_ids`), so they do not exist at plan time. Put the final text in the first payload, or finish the batch and plan the second edit in a new one.

**Q12. How do I change the same text in many places?** `add-descriptor-template --find OLD --replace NEW` writes one `replace_range` per matching *line*, matching literally ([§40.7](#407-mechanical-find-and-replace)); or add one descriptor per occurrence from `find-pattern`. Preview with `status` and `explain` first, and never pass an empty `--find` (V27, BP19). Add an invariant that counts `OLD` in the *untouched* source.

**Q13. I replaced lines with an empty payload and got a blank line.** That is the behavior: an empty payload on `replace_range` writes **one** blank line. To remove lines use `delete_range` (BP17, E5).

**Q14. `validate-plan` demands a taxonomy, a domino trace or an inventory. Can I skip it?** Only if you did not ask for it. Seven of the eleven gates are opt-in: a batch is held to a mechanism if it declared a `--shape` that needs it, or if it used the mechanism (a category, `require-file`, `sync-domino-queue`, `add-source-range`, a protected range). A **project-level** category forces closure in every later batch and cannot be removed (V14). The gate table is [§32.2](#322-all-gates-in-the-order-validate-plan-runs-them).

**Q15. `validate-plan` passed, but `apply-all` did nothing — or `apply-next` aborts.** Nothing: the batch was not validated *after* the last `add-*`, so `apply_order` is empty or short, and `apply-all` exits 0 regardless (V4). Abort: `validate-plan` compares no hashes, so a file that changed after planning only shows up at apply time ([§25](#25-hashes-payloads-and-the-compare-and-swap-check), [§39.6](#396-abort-the-file-changed-under-the-plan)).

**Q16. Why must `validate-plan` be the last planning command?** Because it is the only thing that writes `apply_order`, and anything added afterwards is invisible to `apply` (V4, V20, BP25).

#### 62.3 Applying, undoing, recovering

**Q17. What does `recovered` mean?** "The log, or the file, says this descriptor was already done; the bookkeeping was brought up to date and nothing was applied." It is also the **false** result of an undo followed by an apply (V1), and the result of a crash retry (V2). Look at the file ([§48.4](#484-what-recovered-proves--and-what-it-does-not), BP33).

**Q18. `apply-next` returned `abort`. What now?** Stop. The live content matches neither the expected before-state nor a plausible after-state, so something other than the batch changed the file. Read `detail`, find what changed it, then follow [§39.6](#396-abort-the-file-changed-under-the-plan) and [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch). A retry will not change the outcome, and the batch can never be closed (V21).

**Q19. The process died during `apply-next`.** Do not retry. Run `resume`, `status`, look at the tail of the WAL and the auditor, and compare the file with version control ([§48.5](#485-after-an-unclean-stop-a-protocol)). For an `insert_after` or `copy_range` whose text is already in the file, a retry would add it twice (V2).

**Q20. Can I undo a whole batch?** Not with the tool. `undo-descriptor` is per descriptor and has holes (V1, V12, V23, V24). Restore the files from version control, `register --force` any file whose line structure changed, and plan again (BP41).

**Q21. Can I undo and then apply again?** No. An `apply-next` after an undo reports `recovered`, flips the status to `applied` and leaves the file unchanged (V1). Plan the corrected change in a new batch (BP38).

**Q22. Can I re-run a failed batch?** It depends on how it failed. A failed `validate-plan` changed nothing: fix and run it again. An `abort` can never be closed (V21): new batch. A failed `validate-post` leaves the batch `failed` and the files as they are: a small follow-up batch ([§39.7](#397-a-failed-post-condition)). A crash: [§48.5](#485-after-an-unclean-stop-a-protocol).

**Q23. Everything is applied, but `status` still says `validated`.** The status becomes `committed` only when `validate-post` passes — and that is also what releases the batch's locks (BP42).

**Q24. A lock will not go away.** The batch that holds it never reached `validate-post` (aborted, abandoned, or stuck on an invariant that cannot run). [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch) has the procedure and a helper for the one hand edit that is allowed.

**Q25. Can two people or two agents work at the same time?** Not on one project at the same time: there is no locking of processes, so commands that overlap lose each other's updates (BP37, [§48.1](#481-what-is-atomic-and-what-is-not)). Take turns, or give each its own project copy. Two *plans* over different lines can coexist in separate batches — that is what the cross-batch locks are for ([§33](#33-cross-batch-locks)) — but the commands still have to run one at a time.

#### 62.4 Scale, safety and environment

**Q26. How large a job can it handle?** Measured: a 20,000-line file with 200 replacements applied with `apply-all` in 10.8 s (about 54 ms per descriptor). Adding descriptors costs time quadratic in their number: 500, 1,000, 2,000 and 4,000 descriptors took 4.4, 14.6, 50.5 and 190.4 s ([§41.5](#415-cost-model-and-measured-scale)). Keep batches to tens or a few hundred descriptors (BP26).

**Q27. Does it survive a power loss?** No guarantee. Nothing is `fsync`ed, and the managed files are written by truncate-then-write ([§48.1](#481-what-is-atomic-and-what-is-not)). Version control is the recovery.

**Q28. Is `.operational-platform/` safe to commit? Does it hold secrets?** It holds every payload and every replaced or deleted text **in clear**, and an export bundles the whole store (S10). Commit it with the files it describes (BP45) — and give it the confidentiality of the files it manages (BP47).

**Q29. Can I use it in CI?** Yes, as long as nothing in CI depends on a promise the tool does not make. Start from a clean checkout; run the steps through the guard with a timeout; read exit codes *and* `result` fields; pin the Python version. A cheap and safe check on a committed `.operational-platform/` is the **read-only auditor** ([§59.2](#592-a-read-only-state-auditor)): it needs no tool code and creates nothing.

**Q30. Is it safe to give to an agent?** Not as it is. Three findings are *verified* — a batch ID that is a path component (S2), paths that are not confined to the project root (S3), a payload read from any file the user can read (S4) — and others are read from the code (S1, S5, S6, S7, S9, S10). Put the guard of [§60.3](#603-the-guard-wrapper) between the agent and the tool, and follow the controls of [§57.3](#573-what-to-put-around-the-tool).

**Q31. Does it keep backups?** No. The payload store keeps what descriptors replaced or deleted — enough for `undo-descriptor`, not a backup, and it can be wrong (V23). Use version control.

#### 62.5 The documentation and this guide

**Q32. What are "Set A" and "Set B"?** Two ways of packaging the same content: Set A is one merged document (methodology and implementation phase by phase); Set B keeps the methodology, the tool's instructions and the installable skill apart. They are not sequential ([§2.2](#22-set-a-versus-set-b)).

**Q33. What is "v2.6"?** The documentation's name for its current feature set. The code contains no version constant, so the number cannot be checked against it.

**Q34. Where are the test suite and the "source protocol"?** Not in the archive. The documentation says behaviors have "an automated test backing" them; none is shipped. The "source protocol" it cites for some design decisions is not part of the delivery either ([§2.3](#23-what-is-not-in-the-archive)).

**Q35. The documentation says one thing and the tool does another. Which is right?** Check the register: [§56](#56-verified-behaviors-and-deviations-from-the-documentation) lists every difference found (V1 … V31) with the quotation, the observation, the commands that reproduce it and a workaround. Where this guide says *code-derived*, the behavior was read from the source and not run.

**Q36. How was this guide checked?** [Appendix D](#appendix-d--how-this-guide-was-verified): the scenarios, the environment, the crash harness, the measurements, the tests of the three programs of Part IX, and what was **not** done — no fuzzing, no hostile archive.

**Q37. Which statements are not verified by a run?** Every one labeled *code-derived*: S1, S5, S6, S7 (apart from the auditor's checks), S9 and S10 of [§57.2](#572-findings), the `TimeoutExpired` of m13 and the concurrency analysis of [§48.1](#481-what-is-atomic-and-what-is-not). [§55](#55-stated-limitations-and-their-verification-status) gives the verdict for each of the tool's own stated limitations, and says how each was checked.

#### 62.6 Extending the tool

**Q38. How do I add an operation?** The places that switch on the operation, found by searching the source (adding one was not tried): `engine.BASE_OPS`, and `POSITIVE_CONTENT_OPS` if the result can be recognized in the file afterwards; `engine.add_descriptor` (arguments, and what `expect_hash` and `pre_payload_ref` hash); `engine._check_pre_state` and `_check_post_state` (what "not yet done" and "already done" mean — the heart of crash recovery); `engine._mutate_and_update_registry` (the effect on file and registry); `engine.undo_descriptor` (the inverse); `validator._schema_errors` and `_resolve_ids` (required fields; what the operation *claims*, for conflicts and locks); `cli.py` (the `add-descriptor` options, the `dry-run` replay, `explain`); then the documents and the guard's option table. Define the pre- and post-state **first**, and run the crash harness of [§48.2](#482-the-crash-harness) on every window — that is where V2 came from.

**Q39. How do I add a syntax checker?** Add an entry to `validator.SYNTAX_CHECKERS`, keyed by file suffix (`".yaml"`), whose value is a function `(path) -> (ok, detail)`. `validate-post` calls it for every touched file with that suffix and puts `detail` in the `syntax` map. Keep it fast, never execute the file, catch your own timeouts (the `.js` checker does not — m13), and remember that a checker that starts a program inherits S6.

**Q40. I upgraded the tool. What must I re-check?** There is no version constant, so compare the scripts themselves. Then regenerate the guard's option table with `gen_options.py` (until you do, a new option is refused — that is the point), rerun the scenarios of the guard and the driver, run the auditor on a real project, and re-read the register for entries the new version may have fixed.

**Q41. Can I use the methodology for something other than lines of text?** Yes — that is what it was written for. [§61](#61-adapting-the-methodology-to-other-domains) says what a port must supply and what to do differently.

---

The body of this guide, folded onto a few screens for the reader who already knows what the tool is for. Nothing here is new: every table says where the full explanation is. `cli.py` is `python3 /path/to/operational-platform/scripts/cli.py`, run from the project root; when a model types the commands, each `cli.py` below becomes a call through the guard (`asm`, [§60.3](#603-the-guard-wrapper)).

| Section | What it holds |

| [A.1](#a1-the-loop-on-one-page) | the eleven steps, each with the reply that lets you go on |
| [A.2](#a2-the-38-commands) | the 38 commands, one line each — generated from the tool's own argument parser |
| [A.3](#a3-synopses-operations-and-vocabularies) | the synopses, the five operations, the closed vocabularies |

| [A.8](#a8-when-a-reply-is-not-the-one-you-wanted) | what to do when a reply is not the one you wanted |

### A.1 The loop on one page

The steps are those of [§35](#35-the-eleven-step-workflow) (0–10). The last column is the condition under which the **next** step may start; [§60.2](#602-the-contract-what-to-parse-when-to-continue-when-to-stop) has it for every command.

| # | Step | Commands | Go on only if |
|--:|---|---|---|
| 0 | Look around | `python3 -I state_audit.py PROJECT_ROOT` · `cli.py resume` | the auditor prints no ERROR; `resume` shows no `last_abort`, and the batch it names is one you expect. On a root with no `.operational-platform/` the auditor exits 2 — a fresh start — and `resume` would create the directory |
| 1 | Register | `cli.py register PATH` for every file the job will touch, and every file that may *mention* what changes | `line_count` is above 0 for a file with content; the `file_id` is the same as before for a file you registered earlier (one spelling per path, V3) |
| 2 | Open a batch | `cli.py new-batch [--shape S]` | `batch_id` is the number you expected: count + 1 (V13) |
| 3 | Frame it | `add-category`, `add-constraint`, `require-file`, `add-source-range` — only what the job needs | the echoed entry is what you meant, **at the scope you meant**: `--project` is permanent |
| 4 | Record the edits | `show-file PATH`, then `add-descriptor BATCH --op … --file PATH …` with a `--context` that quotes the live text; `add-descriptor-template` for one literal replacement everywhere; `move-across-files` / `copy-across-files` between files | every reply says `"status": "pending"` and carries the next `descriptor_id`; a template's `count` equals the number of lines `find-pattern` showed |
| 5 | Trace cascades | `sync-domino-queue` · `domino-next` · `add-descriptor … --provenance domino --domino-of dXXXX` · `domino-resolve` … until `domino-status` says `ready_for_plan`; then `sync-domino-queue` once more | you read the candidates yourself and asked what shares no text with the old content; the last `sync` came after the last descriptor was added (BP20) |
| 6 | Say what “complete” means | `add-invariant BATCH --file PATH --pattern REGEX --expected-count N --checked-against PATH` · `close-category` · `set-category-scope` / `close-category-file` · `inventory-resolve` | the pattern compiles and **matches in the pre-state**; the count comes from the untouched source |
| 7 | Validate the plan | `cli.py validate-plan BATCH` — the **last** planning command; `dry-run BATCH --file PATH` to look | exit 0 and `pass`; every warning read; `apply_order` holds every descriptor you added |
| 8 | Apply | `cli.py apply-next BATCH`, again and again | `applied` → call again; `done` → leave the loop; **anything else stops you**: `recovered`, `abort`, an error, a non-zero exit, a reply that is not one JSON object |
| 9 | Check | `cli.py validate-post BATCH` | exit 0, `pass`, at least one invariant listed and every invariant `pass`; each `syntax` value is `syntax OK` or a `skipped` you understand |
| 10 | Report | `cli.py status BATCH` · `cli.py report --batches BATCH` · the project's own tests | the numbers you quote come from these replies, not from memory of composing the batch |

Then commit the files and `.operational-platform/` together (BP45, BP46). Which steps a job needs: the last table of [§35](#35-the-eleven-step-workflow).

> **Note.** The table of step 8 in [§35](#35-the-eleven-step-workflow) repeats the skill's own advice — on `recovered`, keep going. The contract of this guide is stricter, and so is this sheet: after an `undo-descriptor` a `recovered` is false (V1), and after a crash it can hide a duplicated insert (V2).

### A.2 The 38 commands

The table is **generated** by `gen_cheatsheet.py` ([D.6](#d6-the-guides-own-programs)) from the argument parser that `cli.py` builds: the list of commands is the parser's, and the script refuses to run if the parser has a command that the descriptions lack, or the other way round. The purposes and the *Changes* column are written by hand and were checked against [§52.2](#522-who-writes-and-who-reads). The *Changes* column was then checked by running the commands: `changes_check.py` ran all 38 of them, 44 runs in all, each on a fresh copy of one project, and compared the files that each run wrote with the column ([D.7](#d7-mechanical-checks)).

*Changes* names what the command writes under `.operational-platform/`; "WAL" is `wal.jsonl`, "locks" is `active_locks.json`. A dash means nothing is written — with two exceptions that hold for **every** command: on a root with no `.operational-platform/` the first command creates it ([§49.5](#495-the-project-root-and-the-state-directory)), and a command that takes a batch ID creates `batches/<id>/` for an ID that does not exist yet (V13). The managed files themselves change only through `apply-next`, `apply-all` and `undo-descriptor`.

| Command | What it does | Changes | Entry |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Setup and inspection** | | | |
| `register` | bring a file under management: give every line a permanent ID | registry, WAL | [§50.1](#501-register) |
| `show-file` | print every live line with its position and ID (this is what makes a file count as inspected) | WAL | [§50.2](#502-show-file) |
| `find-pattern` | per-line regex search over registered files; positions are the current ones | - | [§50.3](#503-find-pattern) |
| `status` | descriptor counts by status and provenance, the apply order; `--group-by` nests them by any descriptor field | - | [§50.4](#504-status) |
| `explain` | the old text and the new text of one descriptor (which of them exists depends on the operation) | - | [§50.5](#505-explain) |
| `dry-run` | print one file as it would look after all its non-applied descriptors (plain text, no hash checks) | - | [§50.6](#506-dry-run) |
| **Batches and descriptors** | | | |
| `new-batch` | open a batch; optionally declare its shape (which gates it must pass) | batch files | [§50.7](#507-new-batch) |
| `add-descriptor` | add one edit (insert, delete, replace, move, copy) to a batch | blobs, descriptors | [§50.8](#508-add-descriptor) |
| `add-descriptor-template` | one replace descriptor for every line that contains a string | blobs, descriptors | [§50.9](#509-add-descriptor-template) |
| `move-across-files` | move a range to another file: a delete plus an insert, two descriptors | blobs, descriptors | [§50.10](#5010-move-across-files-and-copy-across-files) |
| `copy-across-files` | copy a range to another file: one insert, the source is untouched | blobs, descriptors | [§50.10](#5010-move-across-files-and-copy-across-files) |
| **Taxonomy, constraints, materials** | | | |
| `add-category` | declare a finding category (per batch, or `--project`) | taxonomy | [§50.11](#5011-add-category) |
| `close-category` | record that a category was checked and nothing was found | taxonomy | [§50.12](#5012-close-category) |
| `set-category-scope` | declare which files a category must be checked in | taxonomy | [§50.13](#5013-set-category-scope-and-close-category-file) |
| `close-category-file` | close one file of a scoped category | taxonomy | [§50.13](#5013-set-category-scope-and-close-category-file) |
| `add-constraint` | protect a range of lines from every edit (per batch, or `--project`) | constraints | [§50.14](#5014-add-constraint) |
| `require-file` | declare a file that must be registered before the plan can pass | materials | [§50.15](#5015-require-file) |
| **Invariants** | | | |
| `add-invariant` | declare a post-condition: a regex count over the whole file, or balanced pairs | invariants | [§50.16](#5016-add-invariant) |
| `accept-match` | accept one remaining match of an invariant, by line number, with a note | invariants | [§50.17](#5017-accept-match) |
| **Domino queue** | | | |
| `sync-domino-queue` | put every direct descriptor that is not yet queued into the domino queue | domino queue | [§50.18](#5018-the-domino-commands) |
| `domino-next` | the first pending finding, with the candidate lines its hint still finds (read-only) | - | [§50.18](#5018-the-domino-commands) |
| `domino-resolve` | mark one finding traced; recounts the linked descriptors itself | domino queue, WAL, checkpoint | [§50.18](#5018-the-domino-commands) |
| `domino-status` | counts: pending, traced, traced with candidates left, ready for plan | - | [§50.18](#5018-the-domino-commands) |
| **Region inventory** | | | |
| `add-source-range` | declare a source range that must be accounted for | inventory | [§50.19](#5019-the-inventory-commands) |
| `inventory-next` | the first pending range with its current text (read-only) | - | [§50.19](#5019-the-inventory-commands) |
| `inventory-resolve` | give a range its disposition: transferred as is, with an edit, or excluded | inventory, checkpoint | [§50.19](#5019-the-inventory-commands) |
| `inventory-status` | counts: total, pending, resolved, ready for plan | - | [§50.19](#5019-the-inventory-commands) |
| **Validation and apply** | | | |
| `validate-plan` | run the eleven gates; on pass fix the apply order and take the locks | validation log, checkpoint; on pass also descriptors, locks | [§50.20](#5020-validate-plan) |
| `check` | compare one descriptor's expected hash with the live text — the test apply uses (read-only apart from the log) | validation log | [§50.21](#5021-check) |
| `apply-next` | apply the first descriptor of the order that is not `applied`, then stop | files, registry, descriptors, WAL, checkpoint (validation log on abort) | [§50.22](#5022-apply-next-and-apply-all) |
| `apply-all` | loop of `apply-next` until `done` or the first abort; prints one reply at the very end | files, registry, descriptors, WAL, checkpoint (validation log on abort) | [§50.22](#5022-apply-next-and-apply-all) |
| `validate-post` | needs every descriptor applied; checks syntax and invariants, sets `committed` or `failed`, releases the locks either way | descriptors, locks, validation log, checkpoint | [§50.23](#5023-validate-post) |
| **Reversal** | | | |
| `undo-descriptor` | reverse one applied descriptor through its inverse | files, registry, descriptors, WAL | [§50.24](#5024-undo-descriptor) |
| **Session and reporting** | | | |
| `checkpoint` | print `checkpoint.json` as it is (read-only) | - | [§50.25](#5025-checkpoint-and-resume) |
| `resume` | checkpoint, status of the active batch, applied/total and a suggested next command (read-only) | - | [§50.25](#5025-checkpoint-and-resume) |
| `report` | files touched, issues by severity and the line delta for the listed batches | - | [§50.26](#5026-report) |
| **Transport** | | | |
| `export-batch` | pack the batch directory and the whole payload store into a `.tar.gz` (default `./<batch_id>.tar.gz`) | the archive only | [§50.27](#5027-export-batch-and-import-batch) |
| `import-batch` | unpack an archive; the batch comes back **with the statuses it had when exported** (V31) | batch files, blobs | [§50.27](#5027-export-batch-and-import-batch) |

### A.3 Synopses, operations and vocabularies

**Synopses.** The same 38 commands as the parser spells them — generated by the same script. Square brackets mark an optional argument; a bare `--option VALUE` is required; `{a,b}` is a closed list of choices. The names of the values (`PATH`, `LINE_ID`, `D1,D2`) are display names added by the script; which options exist, which are required and which have choices comes from the parser.

```
# Setup and inspection
cli.py register PATH [--force]
cli.py show-file PATH
cli.py find-pattern --pattern REGEX [--file PATH]
cli.py status BATCH_ID [--group-by FIELD,FIELD]
cli.py explain BATCH_ID DESCRIPTOR_ID
cli.py dry-run BATCH_ID --file PATH

# Batches and descriptors
cli.py new-batch [--shape {conformance,audit,transition,rename,assembly}]
cli.py add-descriptor BATCH_ID --op OP --file PATH [--start LINE_ID] [--end LINE_ID]
      [--after LINE_ID|START] [--dest LINE_ID|START] [--payload-file PATH] [--payload-text TEXT]
      [--depends-on D1,D2] [--category CODE] [--severity {critical,major,minor,cosmetic}]
      [--provenance {direct,domino}] [--domino-hint REGEX] [--domino-of DESCRIPTOR_ID]
      [--context TEXT] [--rule-ref TEXT]
cli.py add-descriptor-template BATCH_ID --find TEXT --replace TEXT [--file PATH]
cli.py move-across-files BATCH_ID --src-file PATH --start LINE_ID --end LINE_ID --dest-file PATH
      --dest-after LINE_ID
cli.py copy-across-files BATCH_ID --src-file PATH --start LINE_ID --end LINE_ID --dest-file PATH
      --dest-after LINE_ID

# Taxonomy, constraints, materials
cli.py add-category BATCH_ID --code CODE [--description TEXT] [--project]
cli.py close-category BATCH_ID --code CODE [--note TEXT]
cli.py set-category-scope BATCH_ID --code CODE --files PATH,PATH
cli.py close-category-file BATCH_ID --code CODE --file PATH [--note TEXT]
cli.py add-constraint BATCH_ID --file PATH --start LINE_ID --end LINE_ID [--reason TEXT]
      [--project]
cli.py require-file BATCH_ID PATH

# Invariants
cli.py add-invariant BATCH_ID --file PATH --pattern REGEX --expected-count N
      [--description TEXT] [--checked-against PATH] [--severity {critical,major,minor,cosmetic}]
      [--exclude-comments] [--type {occurrence_count,balanced_pairs}]
cli.py accept-match BATCH_ID --file PATH --pattern REGEX --line N [--note TEXT]

# Domino queue
cli.py sync-domino-queue BATCH_ID
cli.py domino-next BATCH_ID
cli.py domino-resolve BATCH_ID FINDING_ID
cli.py domino-status BATCH_ID

# Region inventory
cli.py add-source-range BATCH_ID --file PATH --start LINE_ID --end LINE_ID
cli.py inventory-next BATCH_ID
cli.py inventory-resolve BATCH_ID RANGE_ID
      --disposition {transferred_verbatim,transferred_with_edit,excluded} [--note TEXT]
      [--descriptor-ids D1,D2]
cli.py inventory-status BATCH_ID

# Validation and apply
cli.py validate-plan BATCH_ID
cli.py check BATCH_ID DESCRIPTOR_ID
cli.py apply-next BATCH_ID
cli.py apply-all BATCH_ID
cli.py validate-post BATCH_ID

# Reversal
cli.py undo-descriptor BATCH_ID DESCRIPTOR_ID

# Session and reporting
cli.py checkpoint
cli.py resume
cli.py report --batches BATCH_ID,BATCH_ID

# Transport
cli.py export-batch BATCH_ID [--out FILE.tar.gz]
cli.py import-batch FILE.tar.gz
```

Spelling rules that the parser does not enforce for you ([§49.3](#493-argument-conventions)):

- Write the **full** option name. `argparse` accepts any unambiguous prefix (`--payload-f`), and a wrapper that compares option names as text is bypassed by it (m14).
- A value that begins with `--` is written in the `=` form: `--payload-text=--text`.
- Lists have **no spaces** around the commas (V26).
- `--payload-file` wins over `--payload-text` when both are given, and is read relative to the **current directory**, not the project root.
- `--op` is not an `argparse` choice: a wrong value gives an ordinary `{"error": …}`.

**The five operations** ([§24.2](#242-the-five-operations), [§40.2](#402-choosing-the-right-operation)).

| `--op` | Needs | Remember |
|---|---|---|
| `insert_after` | `--after` (a line ID, or `START` for the top) and a payload | several inserts at one anchor land in reverse order (V17) |
| `delete_range` | `--start`, `--end` | `undo` is not an exact inverse (V23) |
| `replace_range` | `--start`, `--end`, a payload | an empty payload writes **one blank line**, not a deletion |
| `move_range` | `--start`, `--end`, `--dest` (a line ID, or `START`) | `dest` must lie outside the block and still be live when the move runs; nothing checks it before apply (V5) |
| `copy_range` | `--start`, `--end`, `--dest` (a line ID) | `--dest START` is accepted but fails at apply (V5) |

There is no operation that creates, renames or deletes a **file** ([§40.5](#405-creating-a-new-file)).

**Closed vocabularies.**

| What | Values |
|---|---|
| `--op` | `insert_after`, `delete_range`, `replace_range`, `move_range`, `copy_range` |
| `--shape` | `conformance`, `audit`, `transition`, `rename`, `assembly` |
| `--severity` | `critical` > `major` > `minor` > `cosmetic` — changes tie-breaking in `apply_order` only |
| `--provenance` | `direct` (default), `domino` |
| `add-invariant --type` | `occurrence_count` (default), `balanced_pairs` |
| `inventory-resolve --disposition` | `transferred_verbatim`, `transferred_with_edit`, `excluded` |
| batch `status` | `planning` → `validated` → `committed` or `failed` |
| descriptor `status` | `pending`, `applied`, `undone` |
| category `status` | `open`, `closed_empty` |
| `line_ending` in the registry | `lf`, `crlf` |

### A.4 Exit statuses and result values

| Exit | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| `0` | the command ran. For `validate-plan`, `check` and `validate-post` it also means `pass`. Not a promise that anything useful happened — `apply-all` on an unvalidated batch exits 0 with `{"applied": []}` |
| `1` | a *reported* failure: `result: "fail"` from `validate-plan`, `check` or `validate-post`, or an `abort` from `apply-next` / `apply-all` |
| `2` | `argparse` rejected the command line (usage on **stderr**, not JSON), or an error object was printed: `{"error": "…"}` |
| `3` | **not the tool**: the guard refused, timed out or could not take its lock — `{"guard_error": "…"}`; nothing ran |

Every command prints one JSON object — except `dry-run`, which prints the file as plain text. Key on `result`, on the exit status and on the documented keys; never on the wording of `detail`, `error` or `warnings` ([§49.2](#492-output-and-exit-codes)).

| `result` | Printed by | Exit | Meaning — and what the caller does |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `pass` · `fail` | `validate-plan` (`phase: plan`), `check` (`per_op`), `validate-post` (`post`) | 0 · 1 | the verdict. After `fail` read the failing key and `detail`. `validate-plan` and `check` change nothing in the batch; `validate-post` sets it `failed` and releases its locks |
| `applied` | `apply-next`; each entry of the list `apply-all` prints | 0 | one descriptor applied — **go on** |
| `done` | `apply-next`; `domino-next`; `inventory-next` | 0 | nothing left to do — **leave the loop** |
| `recovered` | `apply-next`, `apply-all`; `domino-resolve` | 0 | the log, or the live content, says the work was already done and the bookkeeping was reconciled — **stop and look at the file** (V1, V2) |
| `skipped` | `domino-resolve` (the finding is already traced) | 0 | an idempotent no-op. `apply-*` never produces it (V18) |
| `abort` | `apply-next`; the last entry of `apply-all`'s list | 1 | the live text matches neither the pre-state nor a plausible post-state, or the target no longer exists; **the file is untouched** — do not retry |
| `reverted` | `undo-descriptor` | 0 | one descriptor undone — final; never `apply-next` the batch again (V1) |
| `traced` | `domino-resolve` | 0 | a finding closed; the reply carries the number of linked descriptors |

### A.5 Identifiers, hashes and numbers

| Thing | Form | Made by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| batch | `batch_0001` | `new-batch`: the number of existing `batch_*` directories + 1 | an imported batch or a phantom directory shifts the count (V13) |
| descriptor | `d0001` | count + 1 inside the batch | append-only; no command removes or edits one |
| finding | `dm0001` | `sync-domino-queue`: count + 1 | |
| source range | `ri0001` | `add-source-range`: count + 1 | |
| file | `f_` + 10 hex digits | `register`: SHA-256 of the path **string as typed** | `./a.py` and `a.py` are two files (V3) |
| line | `<file_id>_l` + 5 digits | minted at registration and by every insert, replace and copy | never reused; position `null` is a **tombstone** |
| blob | 16 hex digits | SHA-256 of the payload text, lines joined with `\n`, no trailing newline | skip-if-exists; never deleted |
| `expect_hash` | 12 hex digits | the same hash, shortened | of the target's text; for an insert the **anchor line**, for a copy the **source** range |
| `registry_snapshot_hash` | 12 hex digits | SHA-256 of the whole registry, sorted keys | in `checkpoint.json` only |
| `START` | the literal string | — | valid for `--after` and for `--dest` of a **move** |
| `ts`, `updated_at` | float seconds since the epoch | `time.time()` | the only time information anywhere |

Positions are 1-based. A "line" is what `str.splitlines()` finds in the UTF-8 text ([§22.5](#225-what-a-line-is)).

**Numbers** (CPython 3.13.16 on a small cloud VM; the *shape* of the growth is what carries over, [§41.5](#415-cost-model-and-measured-scale)).

| Quantity | Measured |
|---|---|
| applying on a 20,000-line file | about 54 ms per descriptor — 200 descriptors in 10.8 s |
| adding descriptors to one batch | quadratic: 500 → 4.4 s, 1,000 → 14.6 s, 2,000 → 50.5 s, 4,000 → 190.4 s |
| a comfortable batch | a few hundred descriptors; a few thousand are possible but tedious |
| `registry.json` | about 37 bytes per line ever registered, tombstones included, rewritten in full by every apply |
| `descriptors.json` | about 650–730 bytes per descriptor, rewritten in full by every `add-descriptor` |
| `show-file` of a 1,000-line file | 5,006 lines of JSON, 126,856 bytes — read slices, not whole replies |
| `--context` | at most 120 characters, and a substring of the live text at the target **now** |

### A.6 The eleven gates of `validate-plan`

`validate-plan` stops at the **first** failing gate, so a plan with several problems shows them one at a time. Full messages: [§51](#51-the-validate-plan-diagnostic-catalog). Reasoning: [§32.2](#322-all-gates-in-the-order-validate-plan-runs-them).

| # | Failure key | Fails when | Opt-in through |
|--:|---|---|---|
| 1 | `shape_incomplete` | the mechanism the declared shape needs was never used | `new-batch --shape` |
| 2 | `materials_missing` | a `require-file` path is not registered | `require-file` |
| 3 | `taxonomy_incomplete` | a declared category has neither a descriptor nor a closure | `add-category` |
| 4 | `unit_category_matrix_incomplete` | a (file, category) pair of a declared scope is unresolved | `set-category-scope` |
| 5 | `inventory_incomplete` | a source range is still pending | `add-source-range` |
| 6 | `domino_incomplete` | a queued finding is still pending | `sync-domino-queue` |
| 7 | `schema_errors` | a descriptor is malformed or its target cannot be resolved | always |
| 8 | `protected_zone_violations` | a descriptor overlaps a protected range | `add-constraint` |
| 9 | `conflicts` | two descriptors overlap with no declared order, or a dependency is unknown | always |
| 10 | `dependency_cycle` | no descriptor can start | always |
| 11 | `cross_batch_conflicts` | the claimed lines are locked by another validated batch | always |

Not a gate but an error: an **inverted range** escapes as `RangeInvalid`, exit 2 — and the batch is lost, because no descriptor can be removed (V6). On a pass, `warnings` never block: the independence warning, the unverified `--checked-against` claim and the rule-reference drift hint ([§29.5](#295-the-independence-warnings)).

**Shapes** ([§32.1](#321-declaring-a-shape)): a shape commits the batch to *using* a mechanism; the gate checks that it was used, not that it was used well.

| Shape | Required | Satisfied when |
|---|---|---|
| `conformance`, `audit` | taxonomy | the batch or the project has at least one category |
| `transition` | domino, constraints | `domino_queue.json` exists **and** a protected range exists |
| `rename` | domino | `domino_queue.json` exists |
| `assembly` | inventory | `region_inventory.json` exists |

### A.7 The state directory on one screen

Full layout and who writes what: [§52](#52-the-state-directory). Formats: [Appendix B](#appendix-b--state-files-at-a-glance).

```
<project root>/
├── your files …                              the managed files
└── .operational-platform/
    ├── registry.json            line IDs ↔ positions per file; null = tombstone
    ├── payloads/<hash>.blob     text blobs, content-addressed, never deleted
    ├── wal.jsonl                append-only: op_start, op_applied, undo_*, domino_*, file_*
    ├── validation_log.jsonl     append-only: every validator verdict
    ├── checkpoint.json          overwritten: where things stood last
    ├── active_locks.json        lines claimed by validated batches
    ├── project_taxonomy.json    only after add-category --project
    ├── project_constraints.json only after add-constraint --project
    └── batches/batch_0001/
        ├── descriptors.json     the edit queue, status, apply_order, shape
        ├── invariants.json      the post-conditions
        ├── snapshot.json        file and line counts when the batch opened
        ├── taxonomy.json · constraints.json · materials_manifest.json
        └── domino_queue.json · region_inventory.json      (their existence is gate evidence)
```

Never edit anything in it by hand — except removing a stale entry from `active_locks.json`, and for that use `release_lock.py` ([§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch)). Reading it is always safe ([§53.15](#5315-reading-the-state-without-the-tool)). A missing file is silently replaced by an empty default, a corrupt one stops every command that reads it ([§52.4](#524-what-a-missing-file-means)). Litter that is safe to delete: `*.json.tmp`, and `_import_tmp/` after a refused import.

### A.8 When a reply is not the one you wanted

The long version, keyed by what the tool printed, is [§59.1](#591-symptoms-causes-and-fixes); every message is in [Appendix C](#appendix-c--message-catalog). The ones that cost the most if misread:

| The reply | What it means | Do |
|---|---|---|
| exit 3, `{"guard_error": …}` | the guard refused; nothing ran | change the call; do not repeat it unchanged ([§60.3](#603-the-guard-wrapper)) |
| not one JSON object — a traceback, a cut-off reply, nothing | the state is unknown | stop; run the auditor ([§59.2](#592-a-read-only-state-auditor)) |
| `abort` (exit 1) | the file changed under the plan, or the target is gone; this call wrote nothing | **do not retry**; `resume`, `status`, the WAL tail, the auditor, `git diff`; re-plan in a **new** batch ([§48.5](#485-after-an-unclean-stop-a-protocol), [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch)) |
| `recovered` | the **log** says the work was done | open the file. After a crash look for duplicated lines (V2); after an `undo` it is false (V1) |
| `{"applied": []}`, exit 0 | nothing was applied: `validate-plan` was never run, or ran before the last `add-*` (V4) | `status`; `validate-plan`; apply again |
| `apply-all` exits 2 with only an error | the loop was interrupted; the earlier descriptors **were** applied (V30) | `status` |
| `validate-plan` `fail` | exactly one gate failed; the key names it ([A.6](#a6-the-eleven-gates-of-validate-plan)) | do what it names; run it again |
| `validate-plan`, exit 2, `RangeInvalid` | an inverted range was accepted when added (V6) | a new batch |
| `cross_batch_conflicts`; a lock that will not go | another validated batch holds the lines; an abandoned one keeps its lock for good (V21) | finish it, or follow [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch) |
| `validate-post` `fail`: `N descriptor(s) not yet applied` | something is still `pending` or `undone` | finish applying; after an abort the batch cannot be closed ([§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch)) |
| `validate-post`, exit 2, `PatternError`, or a file that is not registered | an invariant cannot run (V8); the batch stays `validated` with its locks | register the file and run it again; a regex that does not compile means a new batch |
| `validate-post` `pass` with no invariants listed | proves syntax at most (BP43) | declare an invariant in a follow-up batch, or say so in the report |
| `register` → `"line_count": 0` for a file that has content | a wrong path; an empty phantom was registered (V19) | check `pwd` and the root; never add descriptors against it |
| `status` says `applied` for a batch you have just imported | it was exported **after** the apply; the files here were never edited (V31) | do not trust it; re-plan in this project |
| `apply-next` after `undo-descriptor` | a false `recovered` (V1); after undoing a replace or delete the batch can no longer validate (V12) | treat undo as final; plan the correction in a new batch |
| a new `.operational-platform/` in a subdirectory | a command ran where no state exists below your root (S8) | stop; `cd` to the real root; remove the stray directory |

---

## Appendix B — State files at a glance

[Part VII](#part-vii--state-file-formats) describes every file the tool keeps, with real samples and the reasons behind the shapes. This appendix is the same material folded into reference tables — every file, every field, its type and when it is present — followed by the result of a **census**: a program that read every state directory the verification scenarios left behind and compared each record with these tables ([B.6](#b6-the-census)). Use it with the sample in hand: [§53](#53-file-by-file-reference) shows what a real value looks like.

### B.1 Notation and conventions

| Notation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `string`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `list`, `object` | JSON types |
| `T or null` | the key is always there; its value may be `null`, which means "not applicable" or "not set yet", never "unknown" |
| `key?` | the key may be **absent** |
| `FILE_ID` | `f_` + 10 hex digits |
| `LINE_ID` | `<FILE_ID>_l` + 5 digits |
| `BATCH_ID`, `DID`, `FID`, `RID` | `batch_0001`, `d0001`, `dm0001`, `ri0001` |
| `H16`, `H12` | the first 16 or 12 hex digits of a SHA-256 |

Every `*.json` file is UTF-8 with `indent=2`, `ensure_ascii=False` and one trailing newline, written to `<name>.tmp` and renamed over the old file. Every `*.jsonl` file holds one JSON object per line, starts each record with `"ts"` (float seconds since the epoch) and is opened in append mode. Nothing is ever pruned: the directory only grows ([§52.3](#523-conventions-shared-by-all-files)).

**Overview.**

| File | Scope | Appears when | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| `registry.json` | project | the first command that saves it (`register`, or any apply or undo) | [B.2](#b2-the-files-of-the-project) · [§53.1](#531-registryjson) |
| `payloads/<H16>.blob` | project | `add-descriptor`, `add-descriptor-template`, `move-across-files`, `copy-across-files` | [§53.2](#532-payloadshashblob) |
| `wal.jsonl` | project | `register` (of a new file), `show-file`, `apply-*`, `undo-descriptor`, `domino-resolve` | [B.2](#b2-the-files-of-the-project) · [§53.13](#5313-waljsonl) |
| `validation_log.jsonl` | project | `validate-plan`, `check`, `validate-post`, an abort | [B.2](#b2-the-files-of-the-project) · [§53.14](#5314-validation_logjsonl) |
| `checkpoint.json` | project | `validate-plan`, `validate-post`, `apply-*`, `domino-resolve`, `inventory-resolve` | [B.2](#b2-the-files-of-the-project) · [§53.12](#5312-checkpointjson) |
| `active_locks.json` | project | a passing `validate-plan` (and its release by `validate-post`) | [B.2](#b2-the-files-of-the-project) · [§53.11](#5311-active_locksjson) |
| `project_taxonomy.json` | project | only after `add-category --project` | [B.2](#b2-the-files-of-the-project) · [§53.5](#535-taxonomyjson-and-project_taxonomyjson) |
| `project_constraints.json` | project | only after `add-constraint --project` | [B.2](#b2-the-files-of-the-project) · [§53.6](#536-constraintsjson-and-project_constraintsjson) |
| `batches/<id>/descriptors.json` | batch | `new-batch` | [B.3](#b3-the-files-of-a-batch) · [§53.3](#533-batchesiddescriptorsjson) |
| `batches/<id>/invariants.json` | batch | `new-batch` (empty) | [B.3](#b3-the-files-of-a-batch) · [§53.4](#534-invariantsjson) |
| `batches/<id>/snapshot.json` | batch | `new-batch` | [B.3](#b3-the-files-of-a-batch) · [§53.10](#5310-snapshotjson) |
| `batches/<id>/taxonomy.json` | batch | once a category was declared or closed in the batch | [B.3](#b3-the-files-of-a-batch) · [§53.5](#535-taxonomyjson-and-project_taxonomyjson) |
| `batches/<id>/constraints.json` | batch | only after `add-constraint` (batch scope) | [B.3](#b3-the-files-of-a-batch) · [§53.6](#536-constraintsjson-and-project_constraintsjson) |
| `batches/<id>/materials_manifest.json` | batch | only after `require-file` | [B.3](#b3-the-files-of-a-batch) · [§53.7](#537-materials_manifestjson) |
| `batches/<id>/domino_queue.json` | batch | only after `sync-domino-queue` — its **existence** is gate evidence | [B.3](#b3-the-files-of-a-batch) · [§53.8](#538-domino_queuejson) |
| `batches/<id>/region_inventory.json` | batch | only after `add-source-range` — its **existence** is gate evidence | [B.3](#b3-the-files-of-a-batch) · [§53.9](#539-region_inventoryjson) |

### B.2 The files of the project

**`registry.json`** — which lines exist, in which order.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `files` | object | `FILE_ID` → entry |
| entry `path` | string | the path **as typed** at registration; also the input of the file ID (V3) |
| entry `lines` | object | `LINE_ID` → position (`int`, 1-based) or `null` (a **tombstone**: the line is gone and its ID is never reused) |
| entry `next_seq` | int | the sequence number the next minted line gets; only ever increases (`--force` resets it) |
| entry `line_ending` | `"lf"` or `"crlf"` | sniffed once, at registration |

**`payloads/<H16>.blob`** — the exact text of a payload, lines joined with `\n`, **no trailing newline**; the name is the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of that text. Written only if absent (not atomically), never re-hashed on read, never deleted.

**`wal.jsonl`** — the write-ahead log; one record per event, `ts` and `event` first.

| `event` | Further keys | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `file_registered` | `file_id`, `path` | `register` — only when something was registered |
| `file_inspected` | `file_id`, `path` | `show-file` |
| `op_start` | `batch_id`, `descriptor_id`, `op` | `apply-*`, just before the file is written |
| `op_applied` | `batch_id`, `descriptor_id`, `note?` (`"backfilled"`) | `apply-*`, after the registry is saved and before the status is saved — **the idempotency key** |
| `undo_start` | `batch_id`, `descriptor_id` | `undo-descriptor`, before any check |
| `undo_applied` | `batch_id`, `descriptor_id` | `undo-descriptor`, after the registry is saved |
| `domino_start` | `batch_id`, `finding_id` | `domino-resolve` |
| `domino_traced` | `batch_id`, `finding_id`, `linked_descriptors` | `domino-resolve` — the idempotency key for it |

**`validation_log.jsonl`** — one record per validator verdict; always `ts`, `phase`, `batch_id`, `result`.

| `phase` · `result` | Further keys |
|---|---|
| `plan` · `fail` | the failing gate's key (a list) — one of the eleven of [A.6](#a6-the-eleven-gates-of-validate-plan) — and, for most gates, `detail` |
| `plan` · `pass` | `apply_order` (list of `DID`), `warnings?` |
| `per_op` · `pass` or `fail` | `descriptor_id`, `detail` (`live hash <H12>`, or `START anchor always matches`) — written by `check` |
| `per_op` · `abort` | `descriptor_id`, `detail` (the abort message) — written by the abort path of `apply-*` |
| `post` · `pass` or `fail` | `syntax` (absolute path → message), `invariants` (the full per-invariant results) |
| `post` · `fail` (descriptors unapplied) | `error: "N descriptor(s) not yet applied: […]"` instead of the two above |

**`checkpoint.json`** — one object, overwritten completely by every writer, so only the keys of the **latest** writer exist.

| Writer | Keys besides `updated_at` (float) and `active_batch` | `last_interrupt_cause` |
|---|---|---|
| `validate-plan` (pass or fail) | — | `plan_check` |
| `apply-next`, `apply-all` and the recovery paths | `queue_position`, `total_descriptors` (int), `registry_snapshot_hash` (H12) | `post_op` |
| `validate-post` (any outcome) | — | `post_check` |
| `inventory-resolve` | `inventory_pending`, `inventory_total` (int) | `inventory_op` |
| `domino-resolve` | `domino_pending`, `domino_total` (int) | `domino_op` |
| an abort in `apply-*` | — | `abort` |

**`active_locks.json`** — `{"batches": {BATCH_ID: [claim, …]}}`; a claim is `{"file_id": FILE_ID, "ids": [LINE_ID, …]}`. One claim per non-applied descriptor at the moment `validate-plan` passed: the range for a replace, delete, move or copy-source; the **anchor line** for an insert; `START` is never claimed. `{"batches": {}}` is the idle state; an empty list for a batch means a plan that passed with nothing left to apply (V31); an entry for a batch that never reached `validate-post` is a stale lock (V21).

**`project_taxonomy.json`** — `{"categories": [category, …]}`; **`project_constraints.json`** — `{"protected_ranges": [range, …]}`. Both have the shape of their batch-level twins, [B.3](#b3-the-files-of-a-batch), without `batch_id`. No command removes anything from either.

### B.3 The files of a batch

**`descriptors.json`** — the batch envelope.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `batch_id` | string | the directory name |
| `status` | string | `planning` → `validated` → `committed` or `failed`; a `committed` or `failed` batch goes back to `validated` if `validate-plan` is run on it again (V31) |
| `apply_order` | list | empty until `validate-plan` passes; then the `DID`s that were **not applied** at that moment, in order; overwritten by every passing `validate-plan` |
| `descriptors` | list | append-only; entries below |
| `shape?`, `required_gates?` | string or null, list | written by `new-batch` only; absent when the file was created by another path |

**The descriptor** — 21 keys, all present in every descriptor. [§24.1](#241-anatomy) explains each; this table says when it has a value.

| Key | Type | Has a value when |
|---|---|---|
| `descriptor_id` | string | always — `d` + (descriptors already in the batch + 1) |
| `op` | string | always — one of the five operations |
| `file_id` | `FILE_ID` | always |
| `start`, `end` | `LINE_ID` or null | every operation except `insert_after` |
| `after` | `LINE_ID`, `"START"` or null | `insert_after` only |
| `dest` | `LINE_ID`, `"START"` or null | `move_range` and `copy_range` only (`START` works for moves) |
| `payload_ref` | H16 or null | `insert_after`, `replace_range`, and `copy_range` (the **source snapshot**) |
| `pre_payload_ref` | H16 or null | `delete_range`, `replace_range` — the text that undo restores |
| `expect_hash` | H12 or `"START"` | always — of the target's text; for an insert the **anchor line**, for a copy the **source** range |
| `depends_on` | list of `DID` | always (possibly empty) |
| `category`, `severity` | string or null | when given; `severity` ∈ `critical`, `major`, `minor`, `cosmetic` |
| `provenance` | string | always — `direct` (default) or `domino` |
| `domino_hint` | string or null | when given — a **regex** (V9) |
| `domino_of` | `DID` or null | required with `provenance: domino` |
| `context`, `rule_ref` | string or null | when given; `context` ≤ 120 characters, checked once, at add time |
| `undo_anchor` | `LINE_ID` or null | `delete_range` and `move_range`: the line above the block; `null` at the top of the file |
| `created_ids` | list or null | set at **apply** time for `insert_after`, `replace_range`, `copy_range`; stays `null` for delete and move, and after a recovery (V24) |
| `status` | string | always — `pending` → `applied` → `undone` |

**`invariants.json`** — `{"batch_id", "invariants": [invariant, …]}`.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | `occurrence_count` or `balanced_pairs` |
| `file_id` | `FILE_ID` | the file whose **whole text** is examined (registered or not — an unregistered file only fails at `validate-post`, V8) |
| `pattern` | string | a regex (`occurrence_count`, default flags, whole text) or the string of open/close characters (`balanced_pairs`) |
| `expected_count` | int | required on the command line; **ignored** for `balanced_pairs` |
| `description`, `severity`, `checked_against` | string or null | free text; the closed severity vocabulary; the path the count was verified against |
| `exclude_comments` | bool | drop matches on lines that begin (after whitespace) with `#`, `//`, `<!--` or `*` before counting |
| `accepted_matches` | list | `{"line": int, "note": string or null}` records added by `accept-match` to the **first** invariant with the same file and identical pattern |

**`taxonomy.json`** — `{"batch_id", "categories": [category, …]}`.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | unique within the file |
| `description` | string | free text; **empty** when the entry is a copy of a project-level category |
| `status` | string | `open` or `closed_empty` |
| `closure_note` | string or null | the note given to `close-category` |
| `scope_files?` | list of `FILE_ID` | the opt-in file × category matrix (`set-category-scope`) |
| `checked_files?` | object | `FILE_ID` → `{"status", "note"}` per-file closures (`close-category-file`) |

A batch sees the **merge** of its own categories and the project's, the batch entry winning on a code clash.

**`constraints.json`** — `{"batch_id", "protected_ranges": [{"file_id", "start", "end", "reason"}, …]}`. A range is stored as two **line IDs**, never as text or positions; it is re-resolved at every `validate-plan`.

**`materials_manifest.json`** — `{"batch_id", "required": [path, …]}`; paths as typed.

**`domino_queue.json`** — `{"batch_id", "entries": [{"finding_id", "descriptor_id", "status", "linked_descriptors", "had_candidates"}, …]}`.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `finding_id` | `dm` + count + 1 |
| `descriptor_id` | the **direct** descriptor being traced |
| `status` | `pending` → `traced` |
| `linked_descriptors` | how many `domino` descriptors with `domino_of` equal to `descriptor_id` existed when `domino-resolve` ran (0 while pending) |
| `had_candidates` | `null` while pending; afterwards `true` if candidate lines remained uncovered at that moment (recomputed on every resolve attempt) |

**`region_inventory.json`** — `{"batch_id", "ranges": [{"range_id", "file_id", "start", "end", "status", "disposition", "note", "descriptor_ids"}, …]}`.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `range_id` | `ri` + count + 1 |
| `file_id`, `start`, `end` | the source range, as IDs |
| `status` | `pending` → `resolved` |
| `disposition` | `null` while pending; `transferred_verbatim`, `transferred_with_edit` or `excluded` |
| `note` | free text (empty string if none) |
| `descriptor_ids` | the descriptors that carry the content across; **required** for `transferred_with_edit`, optional otherwise |

**`snapshot.json`** — `{"files": int, "lines": int}`: the number of registered files and of live lines in the whole registry when `new-batch` ran. Its only reader is `report`.

### B.4 What a missing file means

`storage.py` never raises for a missing state file; it substitutes a default — so the first command in a fresh directory works, and a *deleted* file silently becomes an empty one ([§52.4](#524-what-a-missing-file-means)). A **corrupt** file, unlike a missing one, makes every command that reads it fail with a `JSONDecodeError`.

| File | Default when absent |
|---|---|
| `registry.json` | `{"files": {}}` |
| `descriptors.json` | `{"batch_id": <id>, "status": "planning", "apply_order": [], "descriptors": []}` — no `shape`, no `required_gates` |
| `invariants.json` | `{"batch_id": <id>, "invariants": []}` |
| `taxonomy.json` | `{"batch_id": <id>, "categories": []}` |
| `constraints.json` | `{"batch_id": <id>, "protected_ranges": []}` |
| `domino_queue.json` | `{"batch_id": <id>, "entries": []}` |
| `region_inventory.json` | `{"batch_id": <id>, "ranges": []}` |
| `materials_manifest.json` | `{"batch_id": <id>, "required": []}` |
| `snapshot.json` | `{}` |
| `project_taxonomy.json` | `{"categories": []}` |
| `project_constraints.json` | `{"protected_ranges": []}` |
| `active_locks.json` | `{"batches": {}}` |
| `checkpoint.json` | none — `checkpoint` prints "no checkpoint yet …" |
| `wal.jsonl`, `validation_log.jsonl` | an empty list |

### B.5 What a healthy state satisfies

The rules below are the ones that the tool's behavior implies and that the auditor of [§59.2](#592-a-read-only-state-auditor) tests. The last column says which of them it checks; the others are checkable by reading the files ([§53.15](#5315-reading-the-state-without-the-tool)).

| # | Rule | Auditor |
|---|---|:--:|
| R1 | the live (non-null) positions of a file are exactly `1 … N`, each used once | yes |
| R2 | `N` equals the number of lines `splitlines()` finds in the file on disk right now (blind to reordering) | yes |
| R3 | `next_seq` is greater than every sequence number already minted for the file | yes |
| R4 | every line ID starts with its own file's ID | yes |
| R5 | no ID is ever deleted from `lines` | no — a deleted ID is simply absent |
| R6 | `line_ending` is `lf` or `crlf` | no |
| DS1 | descriptors are numbered `d0001…` contiguously, in list order | no |
| DS2 | every name in `apply_order` is a descriptor ID | yes |
| DS3 | every `payload_ref` and `pre_payload_ref` exists in `payloads/` | yes |
| DS4 | every `applied` descriptor has an `op_applied` record in the WAL — except after an import (V31) | yes |
| BL1 | a blob's content hashes to its own name (nothing in the tool re-hashes it) | yes |
| LK1 | every entry of `active_locks.json` belongs to a batch that exists and is `validated` | yes (V21) |
| CP1 | the checkpoint's `active_batch` has a `descriptors.json` | yes (V15) |
| WL1 | every `op_start` has a later `op_applied` for the same descriptor — otherwise an apply was interrupted | yes (V2) |

### B.6 The census

The rules above are a claim about *every* state the tool produces, so they were tested against all of them. `schema_census.py` ([D.6](#d6-the-guides-own-programs)) reads each state directory under the scenarios' projects — read-only — and checks every record against the key lists of this appendix, written as data in the program: required keys that are missing, keys that appear in no list, and the values of every field that this guide treats as a closed vocabulary. Some of the projects hold states made on purpose to be wrong (a registry that has drifted from its file, a lock with no batch); the census looks at the **shape** of records, which those states keep.

The census read **1,399** state files in **174** state directories and checked **18,300** records against the schema of [Part VII](#part-vii--state-file-formats).
