```python
"""Check Appendix C against reality, in both directions.
(1) Every message the scenarios actually printed must match a template of the catalog (or be one of the known messages
that Python itself writes).  (2) The templates are counted by whether at least one real run produced them: the others are
known from the source only.
Usage: python3 -I check_catalog.py MESSAGES.tsv OUTPUT_DIR"""
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

tsv, outdir = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2])
GENERIC = {("cli", 675), ("validator", 121), ("cli", 493)}        # templates that would match almost anything
SKIP = lambda text: text.startswith(("d{", "dm{", "ri{")) or "    " in text     # ID formats and docstrings: not messages (as in gen_catalog.py)
templates = []
n_skipped = 0
for line in open(tsv, encoding="utf-8"):
    mod, fn, ln, kind, text = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
    if (mod, int(ln)) in GENERIC:
        continue
    text = text.replace("\\n", "\n")
    if SKIP(text.replace("\\n", " ")):                 # an ID format such as d{...} would match every text that starts with a d
        n_skipped += 1
        continue
    parts = re.split(r"(\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\})", text)          # {expr} with one level of nesting
    rx = "".join(".*?" if p.startswith("{") and p.endswith("}") else re.escape(p) for p in parts)
    templates.append((re.compile("^" + rx + "$", re.S), text))

PYTHON = re.compile(r"^(FileNotFoundError|IsADirectoryError|UnicodeDecodeError|StopIteration|PatternError|error|LineNotFound|RangeInvalid): ")
DATA = re.compile(r"^(?:[A-Z]{2,12}|[\w./-]+\.\w+|spec/[\w./-]+|(?:d|dm|ri)\d{4})$")   # category codes, file names and IDs listed in failure keys
pairs = re.compile(r'"(error|detail)":\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"')
items = re.compile(r'"(shape_incomplete|materials_missing|taxonomy_incomplete|unit_category_matrix_incomplete|inventory_incomplete|domino_incomplete|schema_errors|protected_zone_violations|conflicts|cross_batch_conflicts|warnings)":\s*\[((?:[^\]\\]|\\.)*)\]')
strs = re.compile(r'"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"')

found = {}
for f in sorted(outdir.glob("*.txt")):
    text = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    for m in pairs.finditer(text):
        found.setdefault(json.loads('"' + m.group(2) + '"'), set()).add(f.name)
    for m in items.finditer(text):
        for s in strs.finditer(m.group(2)):
            found.setdefault(json.loads('"' + s.group(1) + '"'), set()).add(f.name)

matched, python, data, unmatched = 0, 0, 0, []
hit = [False] * len(templates)
for msg, files in sorted(found.items()):
    hits = [i for i, (rx, _) in enumerate(templates) if rx.match(msg)]
    for i in hits:
        hit[i] = True
    if hits:
        matched += 1
    elif PYTHON.match(msg):
        python += 1
    elif DATA.match(msg):
        data += 1
    else:
        unmatched.append((msg, sorted(files)))
print(f"distinct strings in the error / detail / failure-list fields of the real runs: {len(found)}")
print(f"  matched a template of the catalog : {matched}")
print(f"  Python's own text (C.15)          : {python}")
print(f"  data, not messages (category codes, file names, IDs) : {data}")
print(f"  unexplained                       : {len(unmatched)}")
print(f"templates of the catalog (not counting {len(GENERIC)} that would match almost anything, nor {n_skipped} ID formats and docstrings): {len(templates)}")
print(f"  produced by at least one real run : {sum(hit)}")
print(f"  known from the source only        : {len(templates) - sum(hit)}")
for msg, files in unmatched:
    print("UNMATCHED:", msg[:200].replace("\n", "\\n"), files[:3])
```

#### `check_docs_vs_cli.py`

```python
"""check_docs_vs_cli.py -- are the command names that a document mentions the commands that cli.py has?
Written for this guide; not part of the original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I check_docs_vs_cli.py CLI_PY DOC.md [DOC.md ...]

The files are read as text; nothing is imported or run. For every document the program prints
  * the distinct `cli.py <command>` mentions that name no command of cli.py;
  * backticked kebab-case names that share their first word with a real command but are not one;
  * the commands of cli.py that the document never names.
"""
import re, sys
from pathlib import Path

cli_py, *docs = sys.argv[1:]
src = Path(cli_py).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
commands = set(re.findall(r'sub\.add_parser\("([a-z-]+)"\)', src))
print(f"commands in cli.py: {len(commands)}")

for d in docs:
    text = Path(d).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    mentioned = set(re.findall(r'cli\.py\s+([a-z][a-z-]+)', text))
    # also the backticked kebab-case names that share their first word with a real command but are not one
    ticked = set(re.findall(r'`([a-z]+(?:-[a-z]+)+)`', text))
    unknown = sorted(m for m in mentioned if m not in commands)
    print(f"\n{Path(d).name}")
    print(f"  distinct 'cli.py <cmd>' mentions: {len(mentioned)}; unknown to cli.py: {unknown}")
    cmd_like = sorted(t for t in ticked if t not in commands and t.split('-')[0] in {c.split('-')[0] for c in commands})
    print(f"  backticked kebab-names that look like commands but aren't: {cmd_like}")
    missing = sorted(c for c in commands if c not in text)
    print(f"  cli.py commands never named in this doc: {missing}")
```

#### `check_tool_identity.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check_tool_identity.py -- are the files that were run byte-identical to the files inside the archive?
Written for this guide; not part of the original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I check_tool_identity.py ARCHIVE.zip OUTER_DIR SKILL_PARENT_DIR OUT.md

* ARCHIVE.zip         the archive whose copies were run; it is opened for reading only and nothing is extracted from it.
* OUTER_DIR           the folder into which the five files of the archive were unpacked.
* SKILL_PARENT_DIR    the folder that holds `operational-platform/`, the unpacked nested `operational-platform.skill`.

Every member of the archive, and every member of the nested skill (a zip inside the zip, read in memory), is hashed with
SHA-256 and compared with the file of the same name in the unpacked folders. The report lists the counts, any difference,
and any file in the unpacked folders that the archive does not contain (for instance a `__pycache__` that the Python
interpreter wrote while the tool was being run).
"""
import hashlib
import io
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

archive, outer, skill_parent, out = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]), Path(sys.argv[3]), Path(sys.argv[4])


def sha(b):
    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()


def compare(zf, base, label):
    same, diff, missing = 0, [], []
    names = set()
    for info in zf.infolist():
        if info.is_dir():
            continue
        names.add(info.filename)
        f = base / info.filename
        if not f.is_file():
            missing.append(info.filename)
        elif sha(f.read_bytes()) == sha(zf.read(info)):
            same += 1
        else:
            diff.append(info.filename)
    extra = sorted(str(p.relative_to(base)) for p in base.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and str(p.relative_to(base)) not in names)
    return same, diff, missing, extra


with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as outer_zip:
    s1, d1, m1, e1 = compare(outer_zip, outer, "archive")
    skill = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(outer_zip.read("operational-platform.skill")))
    s2, d2, m2, e2 = compare(skill, skill_parent, "skill")
    arch_sha = sha(archive.read_bytes())
    arch_size = archive.stat().st_size

rows = [
    ("the archive (outer zip)", s1, d1, m1, e1),
    ("the nested `operational-platform.skill`", s2, d2, m2, e2),
]
L = []
L.append(f"Archive: **{arch_size:,} bytes**, SHA-256 `{arch_sha}`.")
L.append("")
L.append("| Compared | Files identical | Files that differ | Files missing from the unpacked copy | Files in the copy that the archive does not contain |")
L.append("|---|---:|---:|---:|---|")
for name, s, d, m, e in rows:
    L.append(f"| {name} | {s} | {len(d)}{' — ' + ', '.join(d) if d else ''} | {len(m)}{' — ' + ', '.join(m) if m else ''} | "
             f"{', '.join('`' + x + '`' for x in e) if e else 'none'} |")
out.write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(f"outer: {s1} identical, {len(d1)} differ, {len(m1)} missing, extra {e1}")
print(f"skill: {s2} identical, {len(d2)} differ, {len(m2)} missing, extra {e2}")
sys.exit(0 if not (d1 or d2 or m1 or m2) else 1)
```

#### `check_guard_table.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check_guard_table.py -- does the OPTIONS table of asm_guard.py say what the real argument parser of cli.py says?
Written for this guide; not part of the original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I check_guard_table.py SCRIPTS_DIR ASM_GUARD.py
        (imports cli.py from SCRIPTS_DIR, so run it only on a copy of the tool that you trust)

The table of the guard is read from the text of ASM_GUARD.py with `ast` -- the guard is not imported. The table of the
parser is built as gen_options.py builds it: `parse_args` is replaced so that `cli.main()` hands over the parser and
runs nothing. For every command the two must agree on the number of positional arguments and on every option
(its first spelling and whether it takes a value). Exit status 0 if they agree, 1 if not.
"""
import argparse
import ast
import sys
from pathlib import Path

scripts_dir, guard = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2])

# the guard's table: the literal assigned to OPTIONS
tree = ast.parse(guard.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
guard_table = None
for node in tree.body:
    if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == "OPTIONS" for t in node.targets):
        guard_table = ast.literal_eval(node.value)
if guard_table is None:
    sys.exit("no OPTIONS table found in " + str(guard))

# the parser's table
sys.path.insert(0, scripts_dir)
captured = {}


def fake_parse(self, *a, **k):
    captured["p"] = self
    raise SystemExit(0)


argparse.ArgumentParser.parse_args = fake_parse
sys.argv = ["cli.py", "status"]
import cli

try:
    cli.main()
except SystemExit:
    pass
parser = captured["p"]
subs = [a for a in parser._actions if isinstance(a, argparse._SubParsersAction)][0].choices
parser_table = {}
for name, sp in subs.items():
    opts, npos = {}, 0
    for a in sp._actions:
        if isinstance(a, argparse._HelpAction):
            continue
        if a.option_strings:
            opts[a.option_strings[0]] = 0 if a.nargs == 0 else 1
        else:
            npos += 1
    parser_table[name] = (npos, opts)

problems = []
for name in sorted(set(guard_table) | set(parser_table)):
    if name not in guard_table:
        problems.append(f"{name}: in the parser, not in the guard's table")
    elif name not in parser_table:
        problems.append(f"{name}: in the guard's table, not in the parser")
    else:
        gn, go = guard_table[name]
        pn, po = parser_table[name]
        if gn != pn:
            problems.append(f"{name}: {gn} positional(s) in the guard, {pn} in the parser")
        for o in sorted(set(go) | set(po)):
            if o not in go:
                problems.append(f"{name} {o}: in the parser, not in the guard's table")
            elif o not in po:
                problems.append(f"{name} {o}: in the guard's table, not in the parser")
            elif go[o] != po[o]:
                problems.append(f"{name} {o}: takes a value = {go[o]} in the guard, {po[o]} in the parser")

n_opts = sum(len(v[1]) for v in parser_table.values())
print(f"commands: guard {len(guard_table)}, parser {len(parser_table)}; options in the parser: {n_opts}")
for p in problems:
    print("DIFFERENCE", p)
print("the two tables agree" if not problems else f"{len(problems)} difference(s)")
sys.exit(1 if problems else 0)
```

#### `check_labels.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check_labels.py -- do the reference labels of the guide agree with each other?
Written for this guide; not part of the original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I check_labels.py GUIDE.md        (the assembled guide; the file is only read)

The guide refers to its findings by short labels: V1.. (deviations from the documentation), S1.. (trust findings),
L1.. (the tool's stated limitations), G1.. (guarantees), BP1.. (best practices), m1.. (minor findings), E1.. (text edge
cases). A label is *defined* by a row of a table or by a heading; this program reads the definitions and checks that

  * the numbers defined are 1, 2, 3 ... without a gap (E has one gap on purpose: there is no E8), and that the index of
    the V register and the headings of the V register define the same numbers;
  * no text mentions a label above the highest one defined (the first number past the last of a family);
  * every range that the text states -- "V1 … V31", "BP1–BP52" -- ends at the highest label defined.

It prints one line per family and, for every problem, `PROBLEM` and the line of the guide. Exit status 0 if there is none.
The output contains no counts of mentions, so it does not change when the output is itself part of the guide.
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

text = Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
lines = text.splitlines()

DEFS = {
    "V": [r"^##### V(\d+) ", r"^\| \*\*V(\d+)\*\* \|"],
    "S": [r"^##### S(\d+) "],
    "L": [r"^\| \*\*L(\d+)\*\* \|"],
    "G": [r"^\| \*\*G(\d+)\*\* \|"],
    "BP": [r"^\| \*\*BP(\d+)\*\* \|"],
    "m": [r"^\| m(\d+) \|"],
    "E": [r"^\| E(\d+) \|"],
}
MEANING = {"V": "deviations from the documentation", "S": "trust findings", "L": "stated limitations", "G": "guarantees",
           "BP": "best practices", "m": "minor findings", "E": "text edge cases"}
EXPECTED_GAPS = {"E": {8}}

problems = []
defined = {}
for fam, patterns in DEFS.items():
    sets = []
    for pat in patterns:
        rx = re.compile(pat)
        sets.append({int(m.group(1)) for line in lines for m in [rx.match(line)] if m})
    allnums = set().union(*sets)
    if not allnums:
        problems.append(f"family {fam}: no definition found")
        continue
    hi = max(allnums)
    gaps = set(range(1, hi + 1)) - allnums
    if gaps != EXPECTED_GAPS.get(fam, set()):
        problems.append(f"family {fam}: numbers missing from 1..{hi}: {sorted(gaps)}")
    if len(sets) > 1 and any(s != sets[0] for s in sets):
        problems.append(f"family {fam}: the definitions disagree: {[sorted(s ^ sets[0]) for s in sets[1:]]}")
    defined[fam] = (hi, len(allnums), gaps)

# mentions above the highest label defined, and stated ranges
for fam, (hi, n, gaps) in defined.items():
    word = re.compile(r"(?<![\w`])" + re.escape(fam) + r"(\d{1,3})(?![\w])")
    rng = re.compile(r"(?<![\w`])" + re.escape(fam) + r"(\d{1,3})\s*(?:…|\.\.\.|–|—)\s*" + re.escape(fam) + r"?(\d{1,3})(?![\w])")
    for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        for m in word.finditer(line):
            if int(m.group(1)) > hi:
                problems.append(f"line {i}: {fam}{m.group(1)} is mentioned, but the highest {fam} label defined is {fam}{hi}")
        for m in rng.finditer(line):
            a, b = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
            if a == 1 and b != hi and b > 9:
                problems.append(f"line {i}: the range {fam}1 … {fam}{b} is stated, but the highest {fam} label defined is {fam}{hi}")

for fam in DEFS:
    if fam in defined:
        hi, n, gaps = defined[fam]
        gap_txt = f" (no {', '.join(fam + str(g) for g in sorted(gaps))})" if gaps else ""
        print(f"{fam}1 … {fam}{hi}{gap_txt}".ljust(26) + MEANING[fam])
for p in problems:
    print("PROBLEM", p)
print("the labels agree" if not problems else f"{len(problems)} problem(s)")
sys.exit(1 if problems else 0)
```

#### `changes_check.py`

Builds one project by running the tool, then, for every command, copies that project, runs the command in the copy, and compares every file of the state directory — content and modification time — before and after.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""changes_check.py -- run each of the 38 commands of operational-platform on a fresh copy of one prepared project and
compare the files that the command changed with the "Changes" column of Appendix A.  Written for this guide; not part
of the original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I changes_check.py SCRIPTS_DIR WORK_DIR OUT.md

* WORK_DIR is created empty (an existing one is removed first) -- give it a throwaway path.
* The base project is built by running the tool itself, through subprocesses (`python3 -I cli.py ...`).
* Every test then copies the base project (copytree, modification times preserved), runs ONE command in the copy, and
  compares the copy before and after. A file is *written* by the command when its bytes differ (changed), when it is
  new (created), or when only its modification time differs (rewritten with the same bytes). The expected sets below
  are sets of written files, which is what the "Changes" column of Appendix A means.
* The archive of `export-batch` is written outside the project, and `import-batch` is run in a second project.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

scripts_dir, work, out_md = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[3])
CLI = scripts_dir / "cli.py"
if work.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(work)
work.mkdir(parents=True)
base, outdir = work / "base", work / "out"
base.mkdir()
outdir.mkdir()


def cli(cwd, *args):
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", str(CLI), *map(str, args)], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r


def ok(cwd, *args):
    r = cli(cwd, *args)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        sys.exit(f"setup step failed: {args}\n{r.stdout}\n{r.stderr}")
    return json.loads(r.stdout) if r.stdout.strip().startswith("{") else r.stdout


# ---- the base project --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
(base / "a.txt").write_text("one\ntwo\nthree\nfour\nfive\nsix\n", encoding="utf-8")
(base / "b.txt").write_text("alpha\nbeta\ngamma\ndelta\n", encoding="utf-8")
(base / "notes.md").write_text("# Notes\nuse old_name here\nend\n", encoding="utf-8")
(base / "c.txt").write_text("not registered yet\n", encoding="utf-8")
fid = {n: ok(base, "register", n)["file_id"] for n in ("a.txt", "b.txt", "notes.md")}
L = lambda name, n: f"{fid[name]}_l{n:05d}"          # the ID of the n-th line as first registered

ok(base, "new-batch")                                                                       # batch_0001: planning
ok(base, "add-category", "batch_0001", "--code", "NAMING")
ok(base, "add-category", "batch_0001", "--code", "STYLE")
ok(base, "set-category-scope", "batch_0001", "--code", "NAMING", "--files", "a.txt,b.txt")
ok(base, "add-descriptor", "batch_0001", "--op", "replace_range", "--file", "a.txt", "--start", L("a.txt", 2),
   "--end", L("a.txt", 2), "--payload-text", "TWO", "--category", "NAMING")
ok(base, "add-invariant", "batch_0001", "--file", "a.txt", "--pattern", "three", "--expected-count", "1",
   "--checked-against", "a.txt")

ok(base, "new-batch")                                                                       # batch_0002: validated
ok(base, "add-descriptor", "batch_0002", "--op", "replace_range", "--file", "a.txt", "--start", L("a.txt", 3),
   "--end", L("a.txt", 3), "--payload-text", "THREE")
ok(base, "add-descriptor", "batch_0002", "--op", "insert_after", "--file", "b.txt", "--after", L("b.txt", 1),
   "--payload-text", "NEW")
ok(base, "validate-plan", "batch_0002")

ok(base, "new-batch")                                                                       # batch_0003: applied
ok(base, "add-descriptor", "batch_0003", "--op", "replace_range", "--file", "a.txt", "--start", L("a.txt", 5),
   "--end", L("a.txt", 5), "--payload-text", "FIVE")
ok(base, "add-invariant", "batch_0003", "--file", "a.txt", "--pattern", "FIVE", "--expected-count", "1",
   "--checked-against", "a.txt")
ok(base, "validate-plan", "batch_0003")
ok(base, "apply-all", "batch_0003")

ok(base, "new-batch")                                                                       # batch_0004: domino
ok(base, "add-descriptor", "batch_0004", "--op", "replace_range", "--file", "notes.md", "--start",
   L("notes.md", 2), "--end", L("notes.md", 2), "--payload-text", "use new_name here", "--domino-hint", "old_name")
ok(base, "sync-domino-queue", "batch_0004")

ok(base, "new-batch", "--shape", "assembly")                                                # batch_0005: inventory
ok(base, "add-source-range", "batch_0005", "--file", "b.txt", "--start", L("b.txt", 2), "--end", L("b.txt", 3))

# an archive of batch_0003 for import-batch, made once, outside every project
ok(base, "export-batch", "batch_0003", "--out", str(outdir / "exp.tar.gz"))


# ---- snapshots ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def snap(root):
    s = {}
    for p in sorted(root.rglob("*")):
        if p.is_file():
            st = p.stat()
            s[str(p.relative_to(root))] = (hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest(), st.st_mtime_ns)
    return s


def label(rel):
    parts = rel.split("/")
    name = parts[-1]
    if parts[0] != ".operational-platform":
        return "files"
    if len(parts) > 1 and parts[1] == "_import_tmp":
        return "_import_tmp (leftover)"
    return {"registry.json": "registry", "wal.jsonl": "WAL", "validation_log.jsonl": "validation log",
            "checkpoint.json": "checkpoint", "active_locks.json": "locks", "descriptors.json": "descriptors",
            "invariants.json": "invariants", "snapshot.json": "snapshot", "taxonomy.json": "taxonomy",
            "constraints.json": "constraints", "materials_manifest.json": "materials",
            "domino_queue.json": "domino queue", "region_inventory.json": "inventory",
            "project_taxonomy.json": "taxonomy (project)",
            "project_constraints.json": "constraints (project)"}.get(name, "blobs" if name.endswith(".blob") else name)


def diff(before, after):
    changed, rewritten, created = set(), set(), set()
    for k, (h, m) in after.items():
        if k not in before:
            created.add(label(k))
        elif before[k][0] != h:
            changed.add(label(k))
        elif before[k][1] != m:
            rewritten.add(label(k))
    return changed, rewritten, created


# ---- the tests -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (display text, argv, expected exit status, expected set of labels that change or are created)
A2, A3, A4 = L("a.txt", 2), L("a.txt", 4), L("a.txt", 6)
B2, B3 = L("b.txt", 2), L("b.txt", 3)
N = set()
TESTS = [
    ("register c.txt  (a new file)", ["register", "c.txt"], 0, {"registry", "WAL"}),
    ("register a.txt  (already registered)", ["register", "a.txt"], 0, N),
    ("show-file a.txt", ["show-file", "a.txt"], 0, {"WAL"}),
    ("find-pattern --pattern one", ["find-pattern", "--pattern", "one"], 0, N),
    ("status batch_0001 --group-by file_id,category", ["status", "batch_0001", "--group-by", "file_id,category"], 0, N),
    ("explain batch_0002 d0001", ["explain", "batch_0002", "d0001"], 0, N),
    ("dry-run batch_0002 --file a.txt", ["dry-run", "batch_0002", "--file", "a.txt"], 0, N),
    ("new-batch", ["new-batch"], 0, {"descriptors", "invariants", "snapshot"}),
    ("new-batch --shape rename", ["new-batch", "--shape", "rename"], 0, {"descriptors", "invariants", "snapshot"}),
    ("add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range …", ["add-descriptor", "batch_0001", "--op", "replace_range", "--file",
     "a.txt", "--start", A4, "--end", A4, "--payload-text", "FOUR"], 0, {"blobs", "descriptors"}),
    ("add-descriptor-template batch_0001 --find six --replace SIX", ["add-descriptor-template", "batch_0001", "--find",
     "six", "--replace", "SIX"], 0, {"blobs", "descriptors"}),
    ("move-across-files batch_0001 …", ["move-across-files", "batch_0001", "--src-file", "a.txt", "--start", A4, "--end",
     A4, "--dest-file", "b.txt", "--dest-after", B2], 0, {"blobs", "descriptors"}),
    ("copy-across-files batch_0001 …", ["copy-across-files", "batch_0001", "--src-file", "a.txt", "--start", A4, "--end",
     A4, "--dest-file", "b.txt", "--dest-after", B2], 0, {"blobs", "descriptors"}),
    ("add-category batch_0001 --code DOCS", ["add-category", "batch_0001", "--code", "DOCS"], 0, {"taxonomy"}),
    ("add-category batch_0001 --code DOCS --project", ["add-category", "batch_0001", "--code", "DOCS", "--project"], 0,
     {"taxonomy (project)"}),
    ("close-category batch_0001 --code STYLE", ["close-category", "batch_0001", "--code", "STYLE", "--note", "none"], 0,
     {"taxonomy"}),
    ("set-category-scope batch_0001 --code STYLE --files a.txt", ["set-category-scope", "batch_0001", "--code", "STYLE",
     "--files", "a.txt"], 0, {"taxonomy"}),
    ("close-category-file batch_0001 --code NAMING --file b.txt", ["close-category-file", "batch_0001", "--code", "NAMING",
     "--file", "b.txt", "--note", "none"], 0, {"taxonomy"}),
    ("add-constraint batch_0001 --file b.txt …", ["add-constraint", "batch_0001", "--file", "b.txt", "--start", B3, "--end",
     B3, "--reason", "frozen"], 0, {"constraints"}),
    ("add-constraint batch_0001 --file b.txt … --project", ["add-constraint", "batch_0001", "--file", "b.txt", "--start",
     B3, "--end", B3, "--reason", "frozen", "--project"], 0, {"constraints (project)"}),
    ("require-file batch_0001 notes.md", ["require-file", "batch_0001", "notes.md"], 0, {"materials"}),
    ("add-invariant batch_0001 --file b.txt --pattern beta …", ["add-invariant", "batch_0001", "--file", "b.txt",
     "--pattern", "beta", "--expected-count", "1"], 0, {"invariants"}),
    ("accept-match batch_0001 --file a.txt --pattern three --line 3", ["accept-match", "batch_0001", "--file", "a.txt",
     "--pattern", "three", "--line", "3", "--note", "ok"], 0, {"invariants"}),
    ("sync-domino-queue batch_0001  (no queue yet)", ["sync-domino-queue", "batch_0001"], 0, {"domino queue"}),
    ("sync-domino-queue batch_0004  (nothing new to add)", ["sync-domino-queue", "batch_0004"], 0, {"domino queue"}),
    ("domino-next batch_0004", ["domino-next", "batch_0004"], 0, N),
    ("domino-resolve batch_0004 dm0001", ["domino-resolve", "batch_0004", "dm0001"], 0,
     {"domino queue", "WAL", "checkpoint"}),
    ("domino-status batch_0004", ["domino-status", "batch_0004"], 0, N),
    ("add-source-range batch_0005 --file a.txt …", ["add-source-range", "batch_0005", "--file", "a.txt", "--start",
     L("a.txt", 1), "--end", A2], 0, {"inventory"}),
    ("inventory-next batch_0005", ["inventory-next", "batch_0005"], 0, N),
    ("inventory-resolve batch_0005 ri0001 --disposition excluded", ["inventory-resolve", "batch_0005", "ri0001",
     "--disposition", "excluded", "--note", "not needed"], 0, {"inventory", "checkpoint"}),
    ("inventory-status batch_0005", ["inventory-status", "batch_0005"], 0, N),
    ("validate-plan batch_0001  (a gate fails)", ["validate-plan", "batch_0001"], 1, {"validation log", "checkpoint"}),
    ("validate-plan batch_0002  (passes)", ["validate-plan", "batch_0002"], 0,
     {"validation log", "checkpoint", "descriptors", "locks"}),
    ("check batch_0002 d0001", ["check", "batch_0002", "d0001"], 0, {"validation log"}),
    ("apply-next batch_0002", ["apply-next", "batch_0002"], 0, {"files", "registry", "descriptors", "WAL", "checkpoint"}),
    ("apply-all batch_0002", ["apply-all", "batch_0002"], 0, {"files", "registry", "descriptors", "WAL", "checkpoint"}),
    ("validate-post batch_0003", ["validate-post", "batch_0003"], 0,
     {"descriptors", "locks", "validation log", "checkpoint"}),
    ("undo-descriptor batch_0003 d0001", ["undo-descriptor", "batch_0003", "d0001"], 0,
     {"files", "registry", "descriptors", "WAL"}),
    ("checkpoint", ["checkpoint"], 0, N),
    ("resume", ["resume"], 0, N),
    ("report --batches batch_0001,batch_0002", ["report", "--batches", "batch_0001,batch_0002"], 0, N),
    ("export-batch batch_0003 --out <outside>/x.tar.gz", ["export-batch", "batch_0003", "--out", str(outdir / "x.tar.gz")],
     0, N),
]

rows = []
n_pass = 0
for text, argv, want_exit, expected in TESTS:
    proj = work / "run"
    if proj.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(proj)
    shutil.copytree(base, proj, copy_function=shutil.copy2)
    before = snap(proj)
    r = cli(proj, *argv)
    changed, rewritten, created = diff(before, snap(proj))
    written = changed | created | rewritten
    good = written == expected and r.returncode == want_exit
    n_pass += good
    rows.append((text, r.returncode, changed | created, rewritten - (changed | created), good, argv[0]))

# import-batch: into a second, tiny project
dst = work / "dst"
dst.mkdir()
(dst / "z.txt").write_text("z\n", encoding="utf-8")
ok(dst, "register", "z.txt")
before = snap(dst)
r = cli(dst, "import-batch", str(outdir / "exp.tar.gz"))
changed, rewritten, created = diff(before, snap(dst))
written = changed | created | rewritten
good = written == {"descriptors", "invariants", "snapshot", "blobs"} and r.returncode == 0
n_pass += good
rows.append(("import-batch <archive of batch_0003>  (second project)", r.returncode, changed | created,
             rewritten - (changed | created), good, "import-batch"))
total = len(TESTS) + 1
archive_ok = (outdir / "x.tar.gz").exists()

cmds = {r_[5] for r_ in rows}

lines = []
lines.append(f"**{total} runs** of **{len(cmds)}** different commands (some twice, to cover a variant such as `--project`), "
             f"each in a fresh copy of the same prepared project; **{n_pass} matched** the expectation, "
             f"{total - n_pass} did not.")
lines.append("")
lines.append("| Run | Exit | Bytes changed, or file created | Rewritten with the same bytes | As expected |")
lines.append("|---|---:|---|---|:--:|")
for text, code, obs, rew, good, _ in rows:
    lines.append(f"| `{text}` | {code} | {', '.join(sorted(obs)) or '—'} | {', '.join(sorted(rew)) or '—'} | "
                 f"{'yes' if good else '**NO**'} |")
lines.append("")
lines.append(f"`export-batch` wrote its archive outside the project: {'yes' if archive_ok else 'NO'}.")
out_md.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(f"{total} runs, {len(cmds)} commands, {n_pass} as expected")
missing = sorted({"register", "show-file", "find-pattern", "status", "explain", "dry-run", "new-batch", "add-descriptor",
                  "add-descriptor-template", "move-across-files", "copy-across-files", "add-category", "close-category",
                  "set-category-scope", "close-category-file", "add-constraint", "require-file", "add-invariant",
                  "accept-match", "sync-domino-queue", "domino-next", "domino-resolve", "domino-status",
                  "add-source-range", "inventory-next", "inventory-resolve", "inventory-status", "validate-plan", "check",
                  "apply-next", "apply-all", "validate-post", "undo-descriptor", "checkpoint", "resume", "report",
                  "export-batch", "import-batch"} - cmds)
print("commands not covered:", missing or "none")
sys.exit(0 if n_pass == total and not missing else 1)
```

#### `schema_census.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""schema_census.py -- compare the state-file formats documented in Part VII with every state directory that the
verification scenarios of this guide left behind.  Written for this guide; not part of the original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I schema_census.py PROJECTS_DIR OUT.md

For every `.operational-platform/` directory found under PROJECTS_DIR the script reads each state file (read-only) and
checks every record against the schema below, which is the schema of section 53 written as data:
  * REQUIRED keys that are missing from a record, and keys that are in no list, are reported;
  * OPTIONAL keys are counted;
  * the values of the closed-vocabulary fields are tallied and compared with the documented vocabulary.
Unreadable files (a scenario corrupted them on purpose) are listed, never guessed at.
It never imports the skill's modules and never writes anywhere but OUT.md.
"""
import json
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

root, out_path = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])

DESCRIPTOR = {"descriptor_id", "op", "file_id", "start", "end", "after", "dest", "payload_ref", "pre_payload_ref",
              "expect_hash", "depends_on", "category", "severity", "provenance", "domino_hint", "domino_of",
              "context", "rule_ref", "undo_anchor", "created_ids", "status"}
INVARIANT = {"type", "file_id", "pattern", "expected_count", "description", "checked_against", "severity",
             "exclude_comments", "accepted_matches"}
CATEGORY_REQ = {"code", "description", "status", "closure_note"}
CATEGORY_OPT = {"scope_files", "checked_files"}
CHECKPOINT_REQ = {"updated_at", "active_batch", "last_interrupt_cause"}
CHECKPOINT_OPT = {"queue_position", "total_descriptors", "registry_snapshot_hash", "inventory_pending",
                  "inventory_total", "domino_pending", "domino_total"}

# kind -> (required keys, optional keys)
SCHEMA = {
    "registry.json": ({"files"}, set()),
    "registry.json: file entry": ({"path", "lines", "next_seq", "line_ending"}, set()),
    "descriptors.json": ({"batch_id", "status", "apply_order", "descriptors"}, {"shape", "required_gates"}),
    "descriptor": (DESCRIPTOR, set()),
    "invariants.json": ({"batch_id", "invariants"}, set()),
    "invariant": (INVARIANT, set()),
    "accepted match": ({"line", "note"}, set()),
    "taxonomy.json": ({"batch_id", "categories"}, set()),
    "project_taxonomy.json": ({"categories"}, set()),
    "category": (CATEGORY_REQ, CATEGORY_OPT),
    "category: checked_files value": ({"status", "note"}, set()),
    "constraints.json": ({"batch_id", "protected_ranges"}, set()),
    "project_constraints.json": ({"protected_ranges"}, set()),
    "protected range": ({"file_id", "start", "end", "reason"}, set()),
    "materials_manifest.json": ({"batch_id", "required"}, set()),
    "domino_queue.json": ({"batch_id", "entries"}, set()),
    "domino entry": ({"finding_id", "descriptor_id", "status", "linked_descriptors", "had_candidates"}, set()),
    "region_inventory.json": ({"batch_id", "ranges"}, set()),
    "inventory range": ({"range_id", "file_id", "start", "end", "status", "disposition", "note",
                         "descriptor_ids"}, set()),
    "snapshot.json": ({"files", "lines"}, set()),
    "active_locks.json": ({"batches"}, set()),
    "lock claim": ({"file_id", "ids"}, set()),
    "checkpoint.json": (CHECKPOINT_REQ, CHECKPOINT_OPT),
    "wal: file_registered": ({"ts", "event", "file_id", "path"}, set()),
    "wal: file_inspected": ({"ts", "event", "file_id", "path"}, set()),
    "wal: op_start": ({"ts", "event", "batch_id", "descriptor_id", "op"}, set()),
    "wal: op_applied": ({"ts", "event", "batch_id", "descriptor_id"}, {"note"}),
    "wal: undo_start": ({"ts", "event", "batch_id", "descriptor_id"}, set()),
    "wal: undo_applied": ({"ts", "event", "batch_id", "descriptor_id"}, set()),
    "wal: domino_start": ({"ts", "event", "batch_id", "finding_id"}, set()),
    "wal: domino_traced": ({"ts", "event", "batch_id", "finding_id", "linked_descriptors"}, set()),
    "vlog: plan fail": ({"ts", "phase", "batch_id", "result"}, {"detail", "shape_incomplete", "materials_missing",
                        "taxonomy_incomplete", "unit_category_matrix_incomplete", "inventory_incomplete",
                        "domino_incomplete", "schema_errors", "protected_zone_violations", "conflicts",
                        "dependency_cycle", "cross_batch_conflicts"}),
    "vlog: plan pass": ({"ts", "phase", "batch_id", "result", "apply_order"}, {"warnings"}),
    "vlog: per_op": ({"ts", "phase", "batch_id", "result", "descriptor_id", "detail"}, set()),
    "vlog: post": ({"ts", "phase", "batch_id", "result"}, {"syntax", "invariants", "error"}),
}

VOCAB = {
    "descriptor.op": {"insert_after", "delete_range", "replace_range", "move_range", "copy_range"},
    "descriptor.status": {"pending", "applied", "undone"},
    "descriptor.provenance": {"direct", "domino"},
    "descriptor.severity": {None, "critical", "major", "minor", "cosmetic"},
    "descriptors.json.status": {"planning", "validated", "committed", "failed"},
    "descriptors.json.shape": {None, "conformance", "audit", "transition", "rename", "assembly"},
    "invariant.type": {"occurrence_count", "balanced_pairs"},
    "invariant.severity": {None, "critical", "major", "minor", "cosmetic"},
    "category.status": {"open", "closed_empty"},
    "domino entry.status": {"pending", "traced"},
    "inventory range.status": {"pending", "resolved"},
    "inventory range.disposition": {None, "transferred_verbatim", "transferred_with_edit", "excluded"},
    "registry file entry.line_ending": {"lf", "crlf"},
    "checkpoint.last_interrupt_cause": {"plan_check", "post_op", "post_check", "inventory_op", "domino_op", "abort"},
    "wal.event": {"file_registered", "file_inspected", "op_start", "op_applied", "undo_start", "undo_applied",
                  "domino_start", "domino_traced"},
    "vlog.phase": {"plan", "per_op", "post"},
    "vlog.result": {"pass", "fail", "abort"},
}

records = defaultdict(lambda: {"files": set(), "n": 0, "missing": Counter(), "extra": Counter(), "opt": Counter()})
vocab_seen = defaultdict(Counter)
unreadable = []
dirs = sorted(p for p in root.rglob(".operational-platform") if p.is_dir())
n_files = 0


def feed(kind, rec, proj):
    if not isinstance(rec, dict):
        unreadable.append((proj, f"{kind}: record is not an object"))
        return
    req, opt = SCHEMA[kind]
    r = records[kind]
    r["files"].add(proj)
    r["n"] += 1
    keys = set(rec)
    for k in req - keys:
        r["missing"][k] += 1
    for k in keys - req - opt:
        r["extra"][k] += 1
    for k in keys & opt:
        r["opt"][k] += 1


def load(path):
    global n_files
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        n_files += 1
        return data
    except Exception as e:                                   # corrupt on purpose, or not JSON at all
        unreadable.append((str(path.parent.parent.relative_to(root)), f"{path.name}: {type(e).__name__}"))
        return None


def load_jsonl(path):
    global n_files
    out = []
    try:
        for ln in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if ln.strip():
                out.append(json.loads(ln))
        n_files += 1
    except Exception as e:
        unreadable.append((str(path.parent.parent.relative_to(root)), f"{path.name}: {type(e).__name__}"))
    return out


def tally(field, value):
    vocab_seen[field][value if not isinstance(value, (list, dict)) else "<structure>"] += 1


for d in dirs:
    proj = str(d.parent.relative_to(root))
    p = d / "registry.json"
    if p.exists():
        data = load(p)
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            feed("registry.json", data, proj)
            for e in (data.get("files") or {}).values():
                feed("registry.json: file entry", e, proj)
                if isinstance(e, dict):
                    tally("registry file entry.line_ending", e.get("line_ending"))
    for name, kind in (("project_taxonomy.json", "project_taxonomy.json"),
                       ("project_constraints.json", "project_constraints.json"),
                       ("active_locks.json", "active_locks.json"), ("checkpoint.json", "checkpoint.json")):
        p = d / name
        if p.exists():
            data = load(p)
            if data is None:
                continue
            feed(kind, data, proj)
            if name == "project_taxonomy.json":
                for c in data.get("categories", []):
                    feed("category", c, proj)
                    tally("category.status", c.get("status"))
            elif name == "project_constraints.json":
                for r in data.get("protected_ranges", []):
                    feed("protected range", r, proj)
            elif name == "active_locks.json":
                for claims in (data.get("batches") or {}).values():
                    for c in claims:
                        feed("lock claim", c, proj)
            elif name == "checkpoint.json":
                tally("checkpoint.last_interrupt_cause", data.get("last_interrupt_cause"))
    for fn, kind in (("wal.jsonl", "wal"), ("validation_log.jsonl", "vlog")):
        p = d / fn
        if not p.exists():
            continue
        for rec in load_jsonl(p):
            if kind == "wal":
                ev = rec.get("event")
                tally("wal.event", ev)
                k = f"wal: {ev}"
                if k in SCHEMA:
                    feed(k, rec, proj)
                else:
                    unreadable.append((proj, f"wal record with unknown event {ev!r}"))
            else:
                ph, res = rec.get("phase"), rec.get("result")
                tally("vlog.phase", ph)
                tally("vlog.result", res)
                k = {("plan", "fail"): "vlog: plan fail", ("plan", "pass"): "vlog: plan pass",
                     ("per_op", "pass"): "vlog: per_op", ("per_op", "fail"): "vlog: per_op",
                     ("per_op", "abort"): "vlog: per_op", ("post", "pass"): "vlog: post",
                     ("post", "fail"): "vlog: post"}.get((ph, res))
                if k:
                    feed(k, rec, proj)
                else:
                    unreadable.append((proj, f"validation record with phase={ph!r} result={res!r}"))
    bdir = d / "batches"
    for b in sorted(bdir.iterdir()) if bdir.is_dir() else []:
        if not b.is_dir():
            continue
        bproj = f"{proj}:{b.name}"
        p = b / "descriptors.json"
        if p.exists():
            data = load(p)
            if isinstance(data, dict):
                feed("descriptors.json", data, bproj)
                tally("descriptors.json.status", data.get("status"))
                tally("descriptors.json.shape", data.get("shape"))
                for x in data.get("descriptors", []):
                    feed("descriptor", x, bproj)
                    if isinstance(x, dict):
                        for f in ("op", "status", "provenance", "severity"):
                            tally(f"descriptor.{f}", x.get(f))
        p = b / "invariants.json"
        if p.exists():
            data = load(p)
            if isinstance(data, dict):
                feed("invariants.json", data, bproj)
                for i in data.get("invariants", []):
                    feed("invariant", i, bproj)
                    if isinstance(i, dict):
                        tally("invariant.type", i.get("type"))
                        tally("invariant.severity", i.get("severity"))
                        for m in i.get("accepted_matches") or []:
                            feed("accepted match", m, bproj)
        p = b / "taxonomy.json"
        if p.exists():
            data = load(p)
            if isinstance(data, dict):
                feed("taxonomy.json", data, bproj)
                for c in data.get("categories", []):
                    feed("category", c, bproj)
                    if isinstance(c, dict):
                        tally("category.status", c.get("status"))
                        for v in (c.get("checked_files") or {}).values():
                            feed("category: checked_files value", v, bproj)
        p = b / "constraints.json"
        if p.exists():
            data = load(p)
            if isinstance(data, dict):
                feed("constraints.json", data, bproj)
                for r in data.get("protected_ranges", []):
                    feed("protected range", r, bproj)
        p = b / "materials_manifest.json"
        if p.exists():
            data = load(p)
            if isinstance(data, dict):
                feed("materials_manifest.json", data, bproj)
        p = b / "domino_queue.json"
        if p.exists():
            data = load(p)
            if isinstance(data, dict):
                feed("domino_queue.json", data, bproj)
                for e in data.get("entries", []):
                    feed("domino entry", e, bproj)
                    if isinstance(e, dict):
                        tally("domino entry.status", e.get("status"))
        p = b / "region_inventory.json"
        if p.exists():
            data = load(p)
            if isinstance(data, dict):
                feed("region_inventory.json", data, bproj)
                for r in data.get("ranges", []):
                    feed("inventory range", r, bproj)
                    if isinstance(r, dict):
                        tally("inventory range.status", r.get("status"))
                        tally("inventory range.disposition", r.get("disposition"))
        p = b / "snapshot.json"
        if p.exists():
            data = load(p)
            if isinstance(data, dict):
                feed("snapshot.json", data, bproj)

# ---- which files exist at all ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TOP_KNOWN = {"registry.json", "wal.jsonl", "validation_log.jsonl", "checkpoint.json", "active_locks.json",
             "project_taxonomy.json", "project_constraints.json"}
BATCH_KNOWN = {"descriptors.json", "invariants.json", "snapshot.json", "taxonomy.json", "constraints.json",
               "materials_manifest.json", "domino_queue.json", "region_inventory.json"}
BLOB = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{16}\.blob$")
by_kind = Counter()
unknown_files = []
for d in dirs:
    for f in sorted(d.rglob("*")):
        if f.is_dir():
            continue
        parts = f.relative_to(d).parts
        if len(parts) == 1 and parts[0] in TOP_KNOWN:
            by_kind["state files of the project"] += 1
        elif len(parts) == 2 and parts[0] == "payloads" and BLOB.match(parts[1]):
            by_kind["payload blobs"] += 1
        elif len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "batches" and parts[2] in BATCH_KNOWN:
            by_kind["batch files"] += 1
        elif f.name.endswith(".tmp"):
            by_kind["`*.tmp` files left by a crashed write"] += 1
        elif parts[0] == "_import_tmp":
            by_kind["files in a leftover `_import_tmp/`"] += 1
        else:
            unknown_files.append(str(f.relative_to(root)))

# ---- report ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
lines = []
total_records = sum(r["n"] for r in records.values())
lines.append(f"The census read **{n_files:,}** state files in **{len(dirs)}** state directories and checked "
             f"**{total_records:,}** records against the schema of [Part VII](#part-vii--state-file-formats).")
lines.append("")
kinds = "; ".join(f"{n:,} {k}" for k, n in sorted(by_kind.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))
lines.append(f"**Files.** {kinds}. Files that the layout of [§52.1](#521-layout) does not describe: "
             + (", ".join(f"`{u}`" for u in unknown_files) if unknown_files else "**none**") + ".")
lines.append("")
lines.append("| Record | In directories | Records | Required keys missing | Keys in no list | Optional keys present (records) |")
lines.append("|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|")
problems = 0
for kind in SCHEMA:
    r = records.get(kind)
    if not r:
        lines.append(f"| {kind} | 0 | 0 | — | — | not observed |")
        continue
    miss = ", ".join(f"`{k}` ×{n}" for k, n in sorted(r["missing"].items())) or "none"
    extra = ", ".join(f"`{k}` ×{n}" for k, n in sorted(r["extra"].items())) or "none"
    opt = ", ".join(f"`{k}` {n}" for k, n in sorted(r["opt"].items())) or "—"
    problems += len(r["missing"]) + len(r["extra"])
    ndirs = len({f.split(":")[0] for f in r["files"]})
    lines.append(f"| {kind} | {ndirs} | {r['n']:,} | {miss} | {extra} | {opt} |")
lines.append("")
lines.append("**Closed vocabularies.** Every value of a field that the documentation lists as a closed set, as it was "
             "found. A value outside the documented set would be marked **outside**.")
lines.append("")
lines.append("| Field | Documented | Found (records) | Outside the set |")
lines.append("|---|---|---|---|")
outside_total = 0
for field, allowed in VOCAB.items():
    seen = vocab_seen.get(field, Counter())
    doc = ", ".join(f"`{v}`" if v is not None else "`null`" for v in sorted(allowed, key=lambda x: (x is None, str(x))))
    found = ", ".join(f"`{v}` {n:,}" if v is not None else f"`null` {n:,}"
                      for v, n in sorted(seen.items(), key=lambda kv: (kv[0] is None, str(kv[0])))) or "—"
    out = [v for v in seen if v not in allowed]
    outside_total += len(out)
    lines.append(f"| `{field}` | {doc} | {found} | {', '.join(map(str, out)) if out else 'none'} |")
lines.append("")
bad = sorted({(p, why) for p, why in unreadable})
if bad:
    lines.append(f"**Files that could not be read or classified ({len(bad)}):** deliberate corruptions of the scenarios "
                 "that test the auditor, listed so that they are not mistaken for omissions.")
    lines.append("")
    for p, why in bad:
        lines.append(f"- `{p}` — {why}")
    lines.append("")
verdict = ("**Result:** every record of every readable file has all the keys the documentation lists as required, "
           "no key that no list mentions, every closed-vocabulary field holds only documented values, and no file exists "
           "that the layout does not describe."
           if problems == 0 and outside_total == 0 and not unknown_files else
           f"**Result:** {problems} record-schema difference(s), {outside_total} value(s) outside a documented set and {len(unknown_files)} undescribed file(s) — see above.")
lines.append(verdict)
out_path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(f"{len(dirs)} state directories, {n_files} files, {total_records} records, "
      f"{problems} schema differences, {outside_total} out-of-vocabulary values, {len(unknown_files)} undescribed files, {len(bad)} unreadable")
```

#### `audit_sweep.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""audit_sweep.py -- run the read-only auditor (state_audit.py) over every project that the verification scenarios left
behind, and prove by comparison that it wrote nothing.  Written for this guide; not part of the original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I audit_sweep.py PROJECTS_DIR STATE_AUDIT.py OUT.md

For every directory that holds a `.operational-platform/` -- and for every directory *directly* under PROJECTS_DIR that does
not, which is where the auditor must answer "no state" and create nothing -- the script
  1. records a digest of the whole tree (every path, size, SHA-256 and modification time in nanoseconds);
  2. runs `python3 -I state_audit.py ROOT`;
  3. records the digest again and compares it with the first.
It reports the exit statuses, the number of findings by level, any traceback, and any difference between the digests.
"""
import hashlib
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

projects, auditor, out_md = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[3])


def digest(root):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    n_files = 0
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        dirnames.sort()
        rel = os.path.relpath(dirpath, root)
        h.update(f"D {rel}\n".encode())
        for fn in sorted(filenames):
            p = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
            st = os.lstat(p)
            with open(p, "rb") as f:
                body = hashlib.sha256(f.read()).hexdigest()
            h.update(f"F {os.path.join(rel, fn)} {st.st_size} {body} {st.st_mtime_ns}\n".encode())
            n_files += 1
    return h.hexdigest(), n_files


roots = sorted({p.parent for p in projects.rglob(".operational-platform") if p.is_dir()})
no_state = sorted(p for p in projects.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and not (p / ".operational-platform").is_dir())

exit_codes = Counter()
levels = Counter()
tracebacks = []
changed = []
created_state = []
audited = 0
files_covered = 0
for kind, group in (("state", roots), ("no state", no_state)):
    for root in group:
        before, nf = digest(root)
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", str(auditor), str(root)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
        after, _ = digest(root)
        audited += 1
        files_covered += nf
        exit_codes[(kind, r.returncode)] += 1
        if "Traceback" in r.stdout or "Traceback" in r.stderr:
            tracebacks.append(str(root.relative_to(projects)))
        for ln in r.stdout.splitlines():
            m = re.match(r"^(ERROR|WARN|INFO)\b", ln)
            if m:
                levels[m.group(1)] += 1
        if before != after:
            changed.append(str(root.relative_to(projects)))
        if kind == "no state" and (root / ".operational-platform").exists():
            created_state.append(str(root.relative_to(projects)))

lines = []
lines.append(f"The auditor was run **{audited}** times — once in each of the **{len(roots)}** projects that hold a "
             f"state directory and once in each of the **{len(no_state)}** directories that hold none — over "
             f"**{files_covered:,}** files in all.")
lines.append("")
lines.append("| Directories | Exit 0 (nothing found) | Exit 1 (findings printed) | Exit 2 (no state) | Other |")
lines.append("|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|")
for kind, group in (("with a state directory", roots), ("without one", no_state)):
    k = "state" if kind.startswith("with a") else "no state"
    other = sum(n for (kk, c), n in exit_codes.items() if kk == k and c not in (0, 1, 2))
    lines.append(f"| {kind} ({len(group)}) | {exit_codes[(k, 0)]} | {exit_codes[(k, 1)]} | {exit_codes[(k, 2)]} | {other} |")
lines.append("")
lines.append(f"Findings printed, by level: **{levels['ERROR']} ERROR**, **{levels['WARN']} WARN**, **{levels['INFO']} INFO** "
             "(the scenarios deliberately leave crashes, aborts, stale locks and falsely recovered descriptors behind; "
             "the findings are what the auditor is for).")
lines.append("")
lines.append(f"Tracebacks or Python errors: **{len(tracebacks)}**" + (f" — {', '.join(tracebacks)}" if tracebacks else "") + ".")
lines.append("")
lines.append(f"Trees that differ after the run (any path, size, content or modification time): **{len(changed)}**"
             + (f" — {', '.join(changed)}" if changed else "") + ".")
lines.append("")
lines.append(f"A `.operational-platform/` created by the auditor where there was none: **{len(created_state)}**"
             + (f" — {', '.join(created_state)}" if created_state else "") + ".")
out_md.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(f"audited {audited}; exit codes {dict(exit_codes)}; levels {dict(levels)}; "
      f"tracebacks {len(tracebacks)}; changed trees {len(changed)}; created state {len(created_state)}")
sys.exit(0 if not tracebacks and not changed and not created_state else 1)
```

#### `repro_check.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""repro_check.py -- run every scenario script again, in a new place, and compare what it prints with the transcript
that this guide quotes.  Written for this guide; not part of the original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I repro_check.py SCRIPTS_DIR TOOL_DIR OUTPUTS_DIR WORK_DIR OUT.md

* SCRIPTS_DIR   the guide's scripts (`lib.sh`, `sc_*.sh`, `crash_sim.py`).
* TOOL_DIR      the folder `operational-platform-skill-extracted`, which holds the unpacked skill. It is copied; the copy is run.
* OUTPUTS_DIR   the recorded transcripts, `sc_NAME.txt` (and `audit_samples.txt` for `sc_audit_samples.sh`).
* WORK_DIR      created empty (an existing one is removed first) -- give it a throwaway path.
  The scripts name their root in a line `S=...`; in the copies of `lib.sh` and `sc_audit_samples.sh` that line is
  changed to WORK_DIR, so nothing of the original projects is touched.

Each script runs as `bash WORK_DIR/scripts/NAME.sh` with standard output and standard error joined. `sc_audit_samples.sh`
looks at projects that other scripts and `crash_sim.py` leave behind, so it runs last, after `crash_sim.py`.
Before the comparison four things are normalized, in both texts: the root directory (to `<root>`), the time stamps that
the tool writes (`"ts": 1234.5` and `"updated_at": 1234.5`, to `<t>`), the dates that `ls -l` prints, and the size that
`ls -l` prints for `wal.jsonl` (the file holds floating-point time stamps, and their printed length is not the same in
every run); they differ from run to run by design -- and the six lines `run N: ...` of `sc_lockorder.sh`, whose point is
that the order differs. A script that still differs is compared again in two weaker ways -- with every file ID masked
(an ID is a hash of the path as it was typed, and a path that names the root changes it), and with the lines sorted (the
order of items that the tool takes from a set is not the same in every process) -- and the report says which. It lists,
for every script that does not reproduce exactly, the first line that differs.
"""
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

args = [Path(a) for a in sys.argv[1:6]]
scripts, tool, outputs, work = (a.resolve() for a in args[:4])
out_md = args[4]

if work.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(work)
(work / "scripts").mkdir(parents=True)
(work / "projects").mkdir()
(work / "outputs").mkdir()                      # sc_showsize.sh writes a scratch file there
shutil.copytree(tool, work / tool.name)
for f in scripts.iterdir():
    if f.suffix in (".sh", ".py"):
        shutil.copy2(f, work / "scripts" / f.name)
for name in ("lib.sh", "sc_audit_samples.sh"):
    p = work / "scripts" / name
    text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    new = re.sub(r"(?m)^S=.*$", f"S={work}", text)
    p.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")

TS = re.compile(r'"(ts|updated_at)": [0-9.eE+-]+')
LSDATE = re.compile(r"\b(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) +\d{1,2} +\d\d:\d\d\b")
FID = re.compile(r"\bf_[0-9a-f]{10}\b")
WALSIZE = re.compile(r"(?m)^(\S+ +\d+ +\S+ +\S+ +)\d+( +<date> +wal\.jsonl)$")     # an `ls -l` line, its date already masked


RUN_LINE = re.compile(r"(?m)^(run \d+): .*$")         # sc_lockorder.sh: the orders it prints are random on purpose


def norm(text, root):
    text = TS.sub(r'"\1": <t>', text.replace(str(root), "<root>"))
    text = RUN_LINE.sub(r"\1: <order>", text)
    return WALSIZE.sub(r"\1<size>\2", LSDATE.sub("<date>", text))


# the root that the recorded transcripts name: the one in the original lib.sh
orig_root = re.search(r"(?m)^S=(.*)$", (scripts / "lib.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8")).group(1).strip()

names = sorted(p.stem for p in (work / "scripts").glob("sc_*.sh"))
names.remove("sc_audit_samples")
rows = []


def run_script(name):
    r = subprocess.run(["bash", str(work / "scripts" / f"{name}.sh")], cwd=work, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                       stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, errors="replace", timeout=900)
    return r.stdout


def compare(name, got, rec_path):
    if not rec_path.exists():
        rows.append((name, "no recorded transcript", ""))
        return
    want = norm(rec_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), orig_root)
    got = norm(got, work)
    if got == want:
        rows.append((name, "identical", ""))
        return
    if FID.sub("f_<id>", got) == FID.sub("f_<id>", want):
        rows.append((name, "identical apart from file IDs", "an ID hashes a path that contains the root"))
        return
    if sorted(x.rstrip(",") for x in got.splitlines()) == sorted(x.rstrip(",") for x in want.splitlines()):
        gl0, wl0 = got.splitlines(), want.splitlines()
        i = next(k for k in range(len(gl0)) if gl0[k] != wl0[k])
        rows.append((name, "identical apart from the order of lines", f"the first line that differs is line {i + 1}"))
        return
    gl, wl = got.splitlines(), want.splitlines()
    for i in range(max(len(gl), len(wl))):
        a = gl[i] if i < len(gl) else "<end of output>"
        b = wl[i] if i < len(wl) else "<end of transcript>"
        if a != b:
            rows.append((name, "differs", f"line {i + 1}: now `{a[:90]}` / recorded `{b[:90]}`"))
            return


for name in names:
    compare(name, run_script(name), outputs / f"{name}.txt")

# the projects that sc_audit_samples.sh audits and that no scenario script makes
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", str(work / "scripts" / "crash_sim.py"), str(work / tool.name / "operational-platform" / "scripts"),
                str(work / "projects" / "crash")], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, check=False)
compare("sc_audit_samples", run_script("sc_audit_samples"), outputs / "audit_samples.txt")

n_same = sum(1 for r in rows if r[1] == "identical")
n_weak = sum(1 for r in rows if r[1].startswith("identical apart"))
n_bad = len(rows) - n_same - n_weak
L = [f"**{len(rows)}** scenario scripts were run again in a new directory. **{n_same}** printed exactly what the recorded transcript says "
     "(after the root directory, the time stamps, the dates of `ls -l` and the size of `wal.jsonl` were normalized); "
     f"**{n_weak}** printed the same text apart from the point named below; **{n_bad}** differ."]
bad = [r for r in rows if r[1] != "identical"]
if bad:
    L += ["", "| Script | Result | Where |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for name, res, why in bad:
        L.append(f"| `{name}.sh` | {res} | {why.replace('|', chr(92) + '|')} |")
out_md.write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(f"{len(rows)} scripts, {n_same} identical, {n_weak} identical apart from one point, {n_bad} differ")
for name, res, why in bad:
    print(f"  {name}: {res} {why}")
sys.exit(1 if n_bad else 0)
```

#### `conflict_runs.py`

Runs `sc_conflict.sh` again a number of times in the directory that `repro_check.py` made, and says for each run whether it printed its transcript exactly, with the same lines in another order, or something else ([D.3](#do-the-transcripts-reproduce)).

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""conflict_runs.py -- how often does sc_conflict.sh print exactly what its transcript says?
Written for this guide; not part of the original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I conflict_runs.py WORK_DIR TRANSCRIPT RUNS ORIGINAL_ROOT

* WORK_DIR        the throwaway directory that `repro_check.py` made: it holds `scripts/` (with `lib.sh` pointed at WORK_DIR)
                  and a copy of the tool. `scripts/sc_conflict.sh` is run RUNS times in it, one run after the other.
* TRANSCRIPT      the recorded transcript, `sc_conflict.txt`.
* RUNS            how many times to run the script.
* ORIGINAL_ROOT   the root directory that the recorded transcript names (the `S=` line of the original `lib.sh`).

`sc_conflict.sh` prints `active_locks.json`, and the order in which that file lists the IDs of a claimed range depends on
the hash seed of the process: the tool builds the list from a set of strings, and Python randomizes the hashes of strings
per process. Each run is compared with the transcript after the same normalization that `repro_check.py` makes (the root
directory and the time stamps). The program prints, for every run, whether the text is identical, identical apart from the
order of lines, or different -- and then the counts.
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

work, recorded, runs, orig_root = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4]

TS = re.compile(r'"(ts|updated_at)": [0-9.eE+-]+')


def norm(text, root):
    return TS.sub(r'"\1": <t>', text.replace(str(root), "<root>"))


def lines(text):
    return sorted(x.rstrip(",") for x in text.splitlines())


want = norm(recorded.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), orig_root)
exact = reordered = 0
for i in range(1, runs + 1):
    r = subprocess.run(["bash", str(work / "scripts" / "sc_conflict.sh")], cwd=work, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                       stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, errors="replace", timeout=300)
    got = norm(r.stdout, work)
    if got == want:
        exact += 1
        verdict = "identical"
    elif lines(got) == lines(want):
        reordered += 1
        verdict = "same lines, another order"
    else:
        verdict = "DIFFERENT"
    print(f"run {i:2d}: {verdict}")
print(f"{runs} runs: {exact} identical, {reordered} with the same lines in another order, {runs - exact - reordered} different")
```

#### `rename_package.py`

Makes the renamed archive from the delivered one ([D.2](#how-the-package-was-renamed)): the rules of the rename, the proof that the code did not change, and — in its `carry-over` mode — what the renamed tool does with a project that holds the state of the delivered one. It is the one program of this guide that contains the delivered names, because it has to find them.

````python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""rename_package.py -- give the delivered package one name, in its file names and in its text.
Written for this guide; not part of the original archive.

The package as delivered used several names for one thing: the tool `llm-assembler` (the skill, its folder, the state
directory `.llm-assembler/`), the project "LLM Operational Platform", and file names that carry them. This program turns the
delivered archive into a copy in which all of them are the single name **Operational Platform**; the delivered archive is
only read.

Usage
  python3 -I rename_package.py build ORIGINAL.zip DIST_DIR EXTRACT_ROOT REPORT.md
        writes DIST_DIR/operational-platform-a-2a.zip (which holds operational-platform.skill), unpacks the archive into
        EXTRACT_ROOT/operational-platform-extracted/ (five files, the .skill among them) and the .skill into
        EXTRACT_ROOT/operational-platform-skill-extracted/ (neither folder may exist), and writes REPORT.md: what was
        renamed, the proof that the code did not change, and the lines of a program that differ (all of them strings).
  python3 -I rename_package.py map FILE_IN FILE_OUT
        applies the same rules to one file (the guide's own scripts and transcripts are renamed with this).
  python3 -I rename_package.py carry-over ORIGINAL.zip RENAMED_CLI WORKDIR REPORT.md
        what happens to a project that already holds the state of the delivered tool (WORKDIR must not exist). The delivered
        tool is unpacked from ORIGINAL.zip into WORKDIR and run on a small project; the renamed tool, RENAMED_CLI (its cli.py),
        is run on copies of that project, before and after the state directory is renamed, and imports a batch that the
        delivered tool exported. Writes REPORT.md.

The rules
  * File names:  llm-assembler -> operational-platform;  llm-operational-platform-task-execution-methodology ->
                 operational-platform-task-execution-methodology;  llm-os -> operational-platform.
  * Text:  `.llm-assembler` (the state directory) -> `.operational-platform`;  `llm-assembler` -> `operational-platform` in
           code, in code spans and in link targets, and -> "Operational Platform" in running text;  "LLM Operational
           Platform" -> "Operational Platform".  A few paragraphs that explained the difference between the old names are
           replaced as a whole (PATCHES): after the rename there is nothing left to distinguish.
  * Words such as "assembly" and "assembled" are not names and are not touched.

The proof that the code did not change: each Python module of the original and of the copy is parsed, every string constant
(docstrings included) is blanked, and the two syntax trees must be equal; the strings that differ are listed.
"""
import ast
import difflib
import hashlib
import io
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

NEW_ZIP = "operational-platform-a-2a.zip"
OLD_RESIDUE = re.compile(r"(?i)llm[-_ ]?assembler|llm[-_ ]os\b|llm[ -]operational")

# ---- file names ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NAME_RULES = [
    ("llm-operational-platform-task-execution-methodology", "operational-platform-task-execution-methodology"),
    ("llm-assembler", "operational-platform"),
    ("llm-os", "operational-platform"),
]


def rename_name(name):
    for old, new in NAME_RULES:
        name = name.replace(old, new)
    return name


# ---- paragraphs that are replaced as a whole -----------------------------------------------------------------------
INTRO_OLD = """**LLM Operational Platform** — or simply **Operational Platform** — is
the name of this project: a six-phase task-execution methodology and a
tested implementation of it (`llm-assembler`, a skill for line-precise
batch editing of text and code)."""
INTRO_NEW = """**Operational Platform** is the name of this project: a six-phase
task-execution methodology and a tested implementation of it
(`operational-platform`, a skill for line-precise batch editing of text
and code)."""

NAME_NOTE_OLD = """`llm-assembler` is a specific tool's name, not the project's — it keeps
its own identity (the skill's `name:` field, its filenames) unchanged, the
same way a specific application keeps its own name on a platform. **LLM
Operational Platform** is the project both files above answer to: the
merged document in Set A opens with it, the standalone methodology
document in Set B opens with it, and `llm-assembler.md`'s own opening
line points back to both as the methodology it implements."""
NAME_NOTE_NEW = """**Operational Platform** is the one name of everything in this delivery:
the project, the methodology and the tool. The merged document in Set A
opens with it, the standalone methodology document in Set B opens with
it, and `operational-platform.md`'s own opening line points back to both
as the methodology it implements. In file names and in the skill's
`name:` field the name is written `operational-platform`, and the tool
keeps its state in a `.operational-platform/` directory."""

SKILL_HEAD_OLD = """# llm-assembler

*Part of the **LLM Operational Platform** (Operational Platform for
short) -- the tool that implements its task-execution methodology.
`references/methodology-mapping.md` maps the methodology's phases onto
the commands below; the full methodology on its own, with no mention of
this tool, lives in `llm-operational-platform-task-execution-methodology.md`.*"""
SKILL_HEAD_NEW = """# Operational Platform

*The tool of the **Operational Platform** project -- it implements the
project's task-execution methodology. `references/methodology-mapping.md`
maps the methodology's phases onto the commands below; the full
methodology on its own, with no mention of this tool, lives in
`operational-platform-task-execution-methodology.md`.*"""

FULL_INTRO_OLD = """**LLM Operational Platform** — or simply **Operational Platform** — is
the name of this project: a six-phase task-execution methodology and,
inline, phase by phase, exactly which command, field, and file of a real
working implementation (`llm-assembler`, a skill for line-precise batch
editing of text and code) satisfies each requirement. Reading only this
document is enough to use the system."""
FULL_INTRO_NEW = """**Operational Platform** is the name of this project: a six-phase
task-execution methodology and, inline, phase by phase, exactly which
command, field, and file of a real working implementation
(`operational-platform`, a skill for line-precise batch editing of text
and code) satisfies each requirement. Reading only this document is
enough to use the system."""

ABSTRACT_INTRO_OLD = """**LLM Operational Platform** — or simply **Operational Platform** — is
the name of the project this document belongs to: a six-phase
task-execution methodology, and, separately, a tested implementation of
it (`llm-assembler`, a skill for line-precise batch editing of text and
code). This document covers the methodology alone."""
ABSTRACT_INTRO_NEW = """**Operational Platform** is the name of the project this document
belongs to: a six-phase task-execution methodology, and, separately, a
tested implementation of it (`operational-platform`, a skill for
line-precise batch editing of text and code). This document covers the
methodology alone."""

FRONT_OLD, FRONT_NEW = "name: llm-assembler\n", "name: operational-platform\n"

# member name (as delivered) -> list of (old, new); a patch that does not match is an error
PATCHES = {
    "README.md": [(INTRO_OLD, INTRO_NEW), (NAME_NOTE_OLD, NAME_NOTE_NEW)],
    "llm-assembler.md": [(FRONT_OLD, FRONT_NEW), (SKILL_HEAD_OLD, SKILL_HEAD_NEW)],
    "llm-assembler/SKILL.md": [(FRONT_OLD, FRONT_NEW), (SKILL_HEAD_OLD, SKILL_HEAD_NEW)],
    "llm-operational-platform-task-execution-methodology-full-in-one-file-md.md": [(FULL_INTRO_OLD, FULL_INTRO_NEW)],
    "llm-operational-platform-task-execution-methodology.md": [(ABSTRACT_INTRO_OLD, ABSTRACT_INTRO_NEW)],
    "llm-assembler/scripts/storage.py": [("for llm-assembler lives here", "for Operational Platform lives here")],
}

# ---- text -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FENCE = re.compile(r"^\s*(`{3,}|~{3,})")
SPAN = re.compile(r"(`+)(?!`)(.+?)(?<!`)\1(?!`)")
LINK_TARGET = re.compile(r"\]\([^)\s]*\)")
GENERIC = [
    ("llm-operational-platform-task-execution-methodology", "operational-platform-task-execution-methodology"),
    ("llm-assembler-skill-extracted", "operational-platform-skill-extracted"),
    ("llm-os-extracted", "operational-platform-extracted"),
    ("llm-os-a-2a", "operational-platform-a-2a"),
    ("how-work-llm-assembler", "how-work-operational-platform"),
    (".llm-assembler", ".operational-platform"),
]


def identifier_form(text, counts):
    for old, new in GENERIC + [("llm-assembler", "operational-platform"), ("LLM Operational Platform", "Operational Platform")]:
        n = text.count(old)
        if n:
            counts[old] = counts.get(old, 0) + n
            text = text.replace(old, new)
    return text


def prose_form(text, counts):
    for old, new in GENERIC + [("LLM Operational Platform", "Operational Platform"), ("llm-assembler", "Operational Platform")]:
        n = text.count(old)
        if n:
            counts[old] = counts.get(old, 0) + n
            text = text.replace(old, new)
    return text


def rename_markdown(text, counts):
    out, fence = [], None                                   # fence = (character, length) while inside a fenced block
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        m = FENCE.match(line)
        if fence is None and m:
            fence = (m.group(1)[0], len(m.group(1)))
            out.append(identifier_form(line, counts))
        elif fence is not None:
            if m and m.group(1)[0] == fence[0] and len(m.group(1)) >= fence[1] and line.strip() == m.group(1):
                fence = None
            out.append(identifier_form(line, counts))
        else:
            pieces, pos = [], 0
            protected = [m.span() for m in SPAN.finditer(line)] + [m.span() for m in LINK_TARGET.finditer(line)]
            for a, b in sorted(protected):
                if a < pos:
                    continue
                pieces.append(prose_form(line[pos:a], counts))
                pieces.append(identifier_form(line[a:b], counts))
                pos = b
            pieces.append(prose_form(line[pos:], counts))
            out.append("".join(pieces))
    return "\n".join(out)


def rename_text(name, text, counts=None):
    """name is the member's name as delivered (it selects the patches); returns the text of the renamed member."""
    counts = {} if counts is None else counts
    for old, new in PATCHES.get(name, []):
        if text.count(old) != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"{name}: a patch does not match exactly once: {old[:60]!r}")
        text = text.replace(old, new)
        counts["(a paragraph)"] = counts.get("(a paragraph)", 0) + 1
    if name.endswith(".md"):
        return rename_markdown(text, counts)
    return identifier_form(text, counts)


# ---- the proof that no program changed ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
class Blank(ast.NodeTransformer):
    def visit_Constant(self, node):
        return ast.copy_location(ast.Constant(value=""), node) if isinstance(node.value, str) else node


def strings(tree):
    return [n.value for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.Constant) and isinstance(n.value, str)]


def same_tree(old_src, new_src):
    a, b = ast.parse(old_src), ast.parse(new_src)
    same = ast.dump(Blank().visit(ast.parse(old_src))) == ast.dump(Blank().visit(ast.parse(new_src)))
    differing = [(x, y) for x, y in zip(strings(a), strings(b)) if x != y] if same else []
    return same, differing


# ---- build ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build(original, dist, extract_root, report):
    outer = zipfile.ZipFile(original)
    rows, counts_by_member, modules = [], {}, []
    new_outer = io.BytesIO()
    members_new = {}                                        # new path under extract_root -> bytes
    with zipfile.ZipFile(new_outer, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zo:
        for info in outer.infolist():
            data = outer.read(info)
            if info.filename.endswith(".skill"):
                start = len(rows)
                inner, inner_out = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)), io.BytesIO()
                with zipfile.ZipFile(inner_out, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zi:
                    for member in inner.infolist():
                        old = inner.read(member)
                        c = {}
                        new = rename_text(member.filename, old.decode("utf-8"), c).encode("utf-8")
                        newname = rename_name(member.filename)
                        zinfo = zipfile.ZipInfo(newname, member.date_time)
                        zinfo.compress_type, zinfo.external_attr, zinfo.create_system = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, member.external_attr, member.create_system
                        zi.writestr(zinfo, new)
                        members_new["operational-platform-skill-extracted/" + newname] = new
                        rows.append((info.filename + " : " + member.filename, rename_name(info.filename) + " : " + newname,
                                     len(old), len(new), sum(c.values())))
                        if member.filename.endswith(".py"):
                            modules.append((member.filename, old.decode("utf-8"), new.decode("utf-8")))
                new = inner_out.getvalue()
                members_new["operational-platform-extracted/" + rename_name(info.filename)] = new
                rows.insert(start, (info.filename, rename_name(info.filename), len(data), len(new), None))
            else:
                c = {}
                new = rename_text(info.filename, data.decode("utf-8"), c).encode("utf-8")
                members_new["operational-platform-extracted/" + rename_name(info.filename)] = new
                rows.append((info.filename, rename_name(info.filename), len(data), len(new), sum(c.values())))
            zinfo = zipfile.ZipInfo(rename_name(info.filename), info.date_time)
            zinfo.compress_type, zinfo.external_attr, zinfo.create_system = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, info.external_attr, info.create_system
            zo.writestr(zinfo, new)
    Path(dist).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_zip = Path(dist) / NEW_ZIP
    out_zip.write_bytes(new_outer.getvalue())
    for rel, content in members_new.items():                # the unpacked copies, which the scenarios run
        target = Path(extract_root) / rel
        if target.exists():
            raise SystemExit(f"{target} exists")
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target.write_bytes(content)
    # the .skill is also written beside the archive, the way it is delivered inside it
````
