````python
    Path(dist, "operational-platform.skill").write_bytes(zipfile.ZipFile(out_zip).read("operational-platform.skill"))

    residue = [r[1] for r in rows if OLD_RESIDUE.search(r[1])]
    for rel, content in members_new.items():
        if rel.endswith(".skill"):                          # a zip: its members were scanned one by one
            continue
        if OLD_RESIDUE.search(content.decode("utf-8")):
            residue.append(rel)
    L = [f"The delivered archive ({Path(original).stat().st_size:,} bytes, SHA-256 `{hashlib.sha256(Path(original).read_bytes()).hexdigest()}`) "
         f"holds {len([r for r in rows if ' : ' not in r[0]])} files, one of which (the package) holds {len([r for r in rows if ' : ' in r[0]])} more. "
         f"The renamed archive `{NEW_ZIP}` is {out_zip.stat().st_size:,} bytes, SHA-256 `{hashlib.sha256(out_zip.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}`.", "",
         "| Delivered as | Renamed to | Bytes before | Bytes after | Names replaced in the text |", "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|"]
    for old, new, a, b, n in rows:
        L.append(f"| `{old}` | `{new}` | {a:,} | {b:,} | {'—' if n is None else n} |")
    L += ["", f"**The code did not change; strings did.** {len(modules)} Python modules were parsed before and after; the syntax tree of each, with every "
          "string constant (docstrings included) blanked, is the same:", "", "| Module | Syntax trees equal | Strings that differ | Lines that differ |", "|---|:--:|---:|---:|"]
    all_same, diffs = True, []
    for name, old, new in modules:
        same, differing = same_tree(old, new)
        all_same &= same
        d = list(difflib.unified_diff(old.splitlines(), new.splitlines(), fromfile=name, tofile=rename_name(name), lineterm="", n=0))
        nlines = sum(1 for x in d if x[:1] in "+-" and x[:3] not in ("+++", "---")) // 2
        L.append(f"| `{rename_name(name)}` | {'yes' if same else '**NO**'} | {len(differing)} | {nlines} |")
        if nlines:
            diffs.append((rename_name(name), d))
    for name, d in diffs:                                   # the lines themselves: `-` as delivered, `+` renamed
        L += ["", f"The lines of `{name}` that differ (`-` as delivered, `+` renamed):", "", "```diff", *d, "```"]
    L += ["", "**Residue.** " + ("None of the old names is left in a file name or in a text of the renamed archive." if not residue
                                else "Old names are left in: " + ", ".join(residue))]
    Path(report).write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(rows)} members renamed; trees equal: {all_same}; residue: {residue or 'none'}; {out_zip}")
    sys.exit(0 if all_same and not residue else 1)


# ---- a project that already holds the state of the delivered tool ---------------------------------------------------------
def carry_over(original, renamed_cli, workdir, report):
    """The renamed tool looks for `.operational-platform/`, the delivered one for `.llm-assembler/`. Is the old directory
    recognized, is renaming it enough, and does a batch that the delivered tool exported still import?"""
    work = Path(workdir)
    if work.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"{work} exists")
    work.mkdir(parents=True)
    outer = zipfile.ZipFile(original)
    skill = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(outer.read(next(n for n in outer.namelist() if n.endswith(".skill")))))
    skill.extractall(work / "delivered-tool")               # a folder of its own; nothing in it is imported, the tool is only run (with -I, through its cli.py)
    old_cli = next((work / "delivered-tool").glob("*/scripts/cli.py"))

    def call(cli, cwd, *args):                              # (exit code, reply), with the paths of the tool, the project and the work folder masked
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", str(cli), *args], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return r.returncode, (r.stdout + r.stderr).replace(str(cli), "<cli.py>").replace(str(cwd), "<project>").replace(str(work), "<work>")

    def must(cli, cwd, *args):
        rc, out = call(cli, cwd, *args)
        if rc:
            raise SystemExit(f"{args[0]} failed: {out}")
        return out

    proj = work / "project"
    proj.mkdir()
    (proj / "list.txt").write_text("".join(f"item {i}\n" for i in range(1, 7)), encoding="utf-8")
    fid = json.loads(must(old_cli, proj, "register", "list.txt"))["file_id"]
    receiving_a, receiving_b = work / "receiving_delivered", work / "receiving_renamed"
    for d in (receiving_a, receiving_b):                    # two copies that hold the registered file and no batch yet
        shutil.copytree(proj, d)
    (receiving_b / ".llm-assembler").rename(receiving_b / ".operational-platform")

    must(old_cli, proj, "new-batch")
    must(old_cli, proj, "add-descriptor", "batch_0001", "--op", "replace_range", "--file", "list.txt",
         "--start", f"{fid}_l00002", "--end", f"{fid}_l00002", "--payload-text", "item 2, edited")
    must(old_cli, proj, "validate-plan", "batch_0001")
    exported = work / "batch_0001.tar.gz"
    must(old_cli, proj, "export-batch", "batch_0001", "--out", str(exported))
    must(old_cli, proj, "apply-all", "batch_0001")
    state = [p for p in (proj / ".llm-assembler").rglob("*") if p.is_file()]
    named = [p for p in state if OLD_RESIDUE.search(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))]

    delivered, moved, unmoved = (work / n for n in ("project_delivered", "project_moved", "project_unmoved"))
    for d in (delivered, moved, unmoved):
        shutil.copytree(proj, d)
    (moved / ".llm-assembler").rename(moved / ".operational-platform")

    def pairs(args_list, cli_a, dir_a, cli_b, dir_b):       # the same commands, one tool in each directory
        out = []
        for args in args_list:
            a, b = call(cli_a, dir_a, *args), call(cli_b, dir_b, *args)
            out.append((" ".join(args).replace(str(exported), "batch_0001.tar.gz"), a[0], b[0], a[1] == b[1]))
        return out

    moved_rows = pairs([("status", "batch_0001"), ("show-file", "list.txt"), ("validate-post", "batch_0001"), ("status", "batch_0001")],
                       old_cli, delivered, renamed_cli, moved)
    import_rows = pairs([("import-batch", str(exported)), ("status", "batch_0001"), ("validate-plan", "batch_0001"),
                         ("apply-all", "batch_0001"), ("validate-post", "batch_0001"), ("show-file", "list.txt")],
                        old_cli, receiving_a, renamed_cli, receiving_b)
    rc, out = call(renamed_cli, unmoved, "status", "batch_0001")
    reply = json.loads(out)
    new_dir = unmoved / ".operational-platform"
    made = sorted(str(q.relative_to(unmoved)) for q in new_dir.rglob("*")) if new_dir.exists() else []

    L = ["| Step | Result |", "|---|---|",
         f"| The delivered tool registers a file, opens a batch, adds one descriptor, plans, exports the batch and applies it | {len(state)} files of state under `.llm-assembler/` |",
         f"| Files of that state that contain the old name | **{len(named)}** of {len(state)} |",
         f"| The renamed tool is asked for the batch in a copy that still has `.llm-assembler/` | `status` `{reply.get('status')}`, `counts` `{json.dumps(reply.get('counts'))}` — "
         f"the answer for a batch that does not exist; and a new `.operational-platform/` appears, holding {', '.join('`' + m + '`' for m in made) or 'nothing'} |",
         "", "After `mv .llm-assembler .operational-platform` in another copy, the same four commands were run by the delivered tool on the copy that kept its "
         "directory and by the renamed tool on the copy whose directory was renamed (the path of the project is masked as `<project>`, that of the tool as `<cli.py>`):", "",
         "| Command | Exit codes | Same reply |", "|---|:--:|:--:|"]
    L += [f"| `{cmd}` | {ca} and {cb} | {'yes' if same else '**NO**'} |" for cmd, ca, cb, same in moved_rows]
    L += ["", "The batch that the delivered tool exported before it applied it (the archive holds the batch's files and the payloads, and no name of the tool) "
          "was then imported into two more copies of the project, which held the registered file and no batch — by the delivered tool in the copy that kept its "
          "directory, and by the renamed tool in the copy whose directory was renamed:", "",
          "| Command | Exit codes | Same reply |", "|---|:--:|:--:|"]
    L += [f"| `{cmd}` | {ca} and {cb} | {'yes' if same else '**NO**'} |" for cmd, ca, cb, same in import_rows]
    Path(report).write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    ok = not named and all(r[3] for r in moved_rows + import_rows)
    print(f"state files: {len(state)}; naming the old tool: {len(named)}; replies identical after the move: {all(r[3] for r in moved_rows)}; "
          f"after the import: {all(r[3] for r in import_rows)}; phantom: {made}")
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)


def main(argv):
    if len(argv) == 6 and argv[1] == "build":
        build(*argv[2:6])
    elif len(argv) == 4 and argv[1] == "map":
        src = Path(argv[2])
        Path(argv[3]).write_text(rename_text(src.name, src.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), encoding="utf-8")
    elif len(argv) == 6 and argv[1] == "carry-over":
        carry_over(*argv[2:6])
    else:
        sys.exit(__doc__)


main(sys.argv)
````

#### `gen_scenarios.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gen_scenarios.py -- list the scenario scripts of this guide's verification, from the scripts themselves.
Written for this guide; not part of the original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I gen_scenarios.py SCRIPTS_DIR OUTPUTS_DIR OUT.md

For every `sc_*.sh` it reads: the headings that the script echoes (`echo "##### CODE: title"`) -- taken from the recorded
transcript in OUTPUTS_DIR when there is one (so that a heading inside a loop shows once per pass, with its real values),
otherwise from the script text --, the names of the projects it creates (`newproj NAME`, or `mk NAME` where a script
wraps it), and the number of commands whose reply was recorded (lines of the transcript that start with `$ `).
Each script name in the table links to the heading of that name in the listing of the scripts (appendix D.11).
Read-only: it opens files for reading and writes OUT.md.
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

scripts, outputs, out = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]), Path(sys.argv[3])

head = re.compile(r'echo\s+"(#{5,})\s*([^"]*)"')
tx_head = re.compile(r"^#{5,}\s*(.*)$")
newproj = re.compile(r'\bnewproj\s+("?)([^\s;"]+)\1')
mk = re.compile(r'\bmk\s+(\w+)\s*;')

# scripts that do not announce their scenarios with a heading
DESCRIBED = {
    "sc_alias.sh": "ALIAS: the same file registered as `app.py` and as `./app.py` (V3)",
    "sc_export.sh": "EXP: export-batch in one project, import-batch into another, a second import, validate-plan and apply-all there",
    "sc_showsize.sh": "SIZE: the reply of show-file for a file of 1,000 lines (count of lines and bytes)",
}
var = re.compile(r"\$\{?(\w+)\}?")


def show(t):
    return var.sub(lambda m: f"<{m.group(1)}>", t)


rows = []
tot_head = tot_cmds = tot_proj = 0
for sh in sorted(scripts.glob("sc_*.sh")):
    text = sh.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    heads = []
    for m in head.finditer(text):
        t = show(m.group(2).strip().rstrip("."))
        if t and t not in heads:
            heads.append(t)
    names = []
    for m in newproj.finditer(text):
        n = m.group(2)
        if n == "$1":                                  # inside the helper `mk`; the names come from its callers
            continue
        n = show(n)
        if n not in names:
            names.append(n)
    for m in mk.finditer(text):
        if m.group(1) not in names:
            names.append(m.group(1))
    o = next((c for c in (outputs / (sh.stem + ".txt"), outputs / (sh.stem[3:] + ".txt")) if c.exists()), None)
    cmds = lines = 0
    if o is not None:
        body = o.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
        lines = len(body)
        cmds = sum(1 for ln in body if ln.startswith("$ "))
        tx = []
        for ln in body:
            m = tx_head.match(ln)
            if m:
                t = m.group(1).strip().rstrip(".")
                if t and t not in tx:
                    tx.append(t)
        if tx:
            heads = tx
    first_comment = DESCRIBED.get(sh.name, "")
    if not heads and not first_comment:
        for ln in text.splitlines():
            if ln.startswith("#") and not ln.startswith("#!"):
                first_comment = ln.lstrip("# ").strip()
                break
    rows.append((sh.name, names, heads, first_comment, cmds, lines))
    tot_head += len(heads)
    tot_cmds += cmds
    tot_proj += len(names)

L = []
L.append(f"**{len(rows)}** scenario scripts; **{tot_head}** scenarios that announce themselves with a heading; "
         f"**{tot_cmds:,}** commands whose reply is recorded in a transcript (a script may run more commands "
         "silently, to set a state up).")
L.append("")
L.append("| Script | Projects it creates | Scenarios (as the transcript titles them) | Replies recorded |")
L.append("|---|---|---|---:|")
for name, names, heads, fc, cmds, lines in rows:
    proj = ", ".join(f"`{n}`" for n in names) or "—"
    if heads:
        scen = " · ".join(h.replace("|", "\\|") for h in heads)
    else:
        scen = fc.replace("|", "\\|") if fc else "—"
    anchor = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", name.lower())              # the anchor of the heading `name` in the listing of the scripts
    L.append(f"| [`{name}`](#{anchor}) | {proj} | {scen} | {cmds or '—'} |")
out.write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(f"{len(rows)} scripts, {tot_head} headings, {tot_cmds} recorded commands")
```

#### `gen_program_table.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gen_program_table.py -- tabulate the Python programs written for this guide.
Written for this guide; not part of the original archive.

Usage:  python3 -I gen_program_table.py SCRIPTS_DIR VERMIN OUT.md

For every `*.py` in SCRIPTS_DIR the file is parsed with `ast` -- it is never imported and never run -- and the script
reports: its number of lines; the modules it imports, and whether each belongs to the standard library
(`sys.stdlib_module_names`); whether it imports a module of the tool itself; whether it starts another process; and the
lowest Python version that `vermin` (run once per file, the path passed as an argument) says the file needs.
`vermin` looks at names it knows (modules, functions, syntax); it cannot see a method called on an object, so the
script also scans for the few methods newer than 3.7 that the guide's programs could have used, and adds them.
"""
import ast
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

scripts, vermin, out = Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], Path(sys.argv[3])

TOOL = {"cli", "engine", "registry", "storage", "validator", "domino", "inventory"}
# methods that vermin cannot attribute to a type, with the version that introduced them
LATE_METHODS = {"is_relative_to": "3.9", "removeprefix": "3.9", "removesuffix": "3.9", "with_stem": "3.9",
                "bit_count": "3.10", "readlink": "3.9"}
method_re = re.compile(r"\.(" + "|".join(LATE_METHODS) + r")\(")
ver_re = re.compile(r"Minimum required versions:\s*([0-9.]+)")


def key(v):
    return tuple(int(x) for x in v.split("."))


rows = []
for path in sorted(scripts.glob("*.py")):
    src = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    mods = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            mods.update(a.name.split(".")[0] for a in node.names)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module and node.level == 0:
            mods.add(node.module.split(".")[0])
    non_std = sorted(m for m in mods if m not in sys.stdlib_module_names and m not in TOOL)
    tool = sorted(m for m in mods if m in TOOL)
    r = subprocess.run([vermin, "--no-tips", str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    m = ver_re.search(r.stdout)
    need = m.group(1) if m else "?"
    extra = sorted({(LATE_METHODS[x], x) for x in method_re.findall(src)}, key=lambda t: key(t[0]))
    need_txt = need
    if extra and key(extra[-1][0]) > key(need):
        need_txt = f"{extra[-1][0]} (`.{extra[-1][1]}()`; vermin says {need})"
    rows.append({
        "name": path.name,
        "lines": len(src.splitlines()),
        "mods": sorted(mods - TOOL),
        "non_std": non_std,
        "tool": tool,
        "proc": "subprocess" in mods,
        "need": need_txt,
    })

n = len(rows)
tot = sum(r["lines"] for r in rows)
bad = [r["name"] for r in rows if r["non_std"]]
L = []
L.append(f"**{n}** programs, **{tot:,}** lines in all. Every import is from the standard library"
         + ("." if not bad else f" — except in {', '.join(bad)}.")
         + f" **{sum(1 for r in rows if r['tool'])}** of them import modules of the tool itself (so they run the tool's code: "
         "use them only on a copy of the tool that you trust); "
         f"**{sum(1 for r in rows if r['proc'])}** start other processes; the rest only read and write files.")
L.append("")
L.append("| Program | Lines | Standard-library modules imported | Imports the tool's modules | Starts processes | Python needed (static estimate) |")
L.append("|---|---:|---|---|---|---|")
for r in rows:
    mods = ", ".join(f"`{m}`" for m in r["mods"]) or "—"
    tool = ", ".join(f"`{m}`" for m in r["tool"]) or "—"
    L.append(f"| `{r['name']}` | {r['lines']} | {mods} | {tool} | {'yes' if r['proc'] else 'no'} | {r['need']} |")
out.write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(f"{n} programs, {tot} lines; non-stdlib: {bad or 'none'}")
```

#### `assemble.py`

The program that joins the parts of this guide into one file. It expands the `INCLUDE` markers (a program or a transcript as a code block, a generated table as Markdown), fills in the counts that must not be typed (the fixtures, the lines of a program, the links, the headings), builds the contents, and checks every internal link and every link label that cites a section number.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Assemble the guide from guide/p[0-9]*.md, expand INCLUDE markers, build the TOC and
check every internal link.  Usage: python3 -I assemble.py SCRATCHPAD OUT_FILE

INCLUDE markers (one per line):
  <!-- INCLUDE:python:REL_PATH -->                 file as a fenced python block
  <!-- INCLUDE:sh:REL_PATH -->                     file as a fenced shell block
  <!-- INCLUDE:text:REL_PATH -->                   file as a fenced plain block
  <!-- INCLUDE:md:REL_PATH -->                     file inserted as raw Markdown (generated tables)
  <!-- INCLUDE:text:REL_PATH:name1,name2 -->       audit_samples.txt only: the named blocks
REL_PATH is relative to SCRATCHPAD.
Other placeholders: @@NPROJECTS@@ (number of project fixtures), @@LINES:REL_PATH@@ (line count of a file) and, filled in
last, once the document is complete: @@NLINKS@@ (internal links checked), @@NHEADS@@ (headings of all levels) and
@@NINCLUDES@@ (INCLUDE markers expanded).
A listing or a transcript is shown as it is: the "@@" inside an included file is held back while the placeholders are
filled in, and put back at the end, so that this program's own listing reads like the file.
"""
import re
import sys
import unicodedata
from pathlib import Path

scratch = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
out_path = Path(sys.argv[2])
guide = scratch / "guide"

PREFIXES = [str(scratch) + "/projects/", str(scratch) + "/operational-platform-skill-extracted/", str(scratch) + "/"]
errors, warnings = [], []
HOLD = "\ue000"                                           # stands for "@@" inside an included file, until the end


def shorten(text):
    for p in PREFIXES:
        text = text.replace(p, "…/projects/" if p.endswith("/projects/") else "…/")
    return text.replace(str(scratch), "/path/to/work")        # what is left is the bare directory itself, e.g. `S=...`


def fence_for(body):
    n = 3
    while "`" * n in body:
        n += 1
    return "`" * n


def audit_blocks(text):
    """Split audit_samples.txt into {project name: block text}."""
    blocks, cur, name = {}, [], None
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"\$ python3 -I state_audit\.py projects/(\S+)", line)
        if m:
            if name is not None:
                blocks[name] = "\n".join(cur).rstrip()
            name, cur = m.group(1), [line]
        elif name is not None:
            cur.append(line)
    if name is not None:
        blocks[name] = "\n".join(cur).rstrip()
    return blocks


def expand_include(kind, rel, names):
    path = scratch / rel
    if not path.is_file():
        errors.append(f"INCLUDE: missing file {rel}")
        return f"<!-- MISSING INCLUDE {rel} -->"
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("@@", HOLD)
    if kind in ("text", "sh", "md"):
        text = shorten(text)
    if kind == "md":
        return text.rstrip("\n")                   # raw Markdown: tables generated by a script
    if names:
        blocks = audit_blocks(text)
        picked = []
        for n in names.split(","):
            if n not in blocks:
                errors.append(f"INCLUDE: no block {n!r} in {rel}")
                continue
            picked.append(blocks[n])
        text = "\n\n".join(picked)
    text = "\n".join(l.rstrip() for l in text.rstrip("\n").splitlines())
    lang = {"python": "python", "sh": "bash", "text": ""}[kind]
    f = fence_for(text)
    return f"{f}{lang}\n{text}\n{f}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. concatenate
parts = sorted(p for p in guide.glob("p[0-9]*.md"))
raw = []
for p in parts:
    t = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if not t.endswith("\n"):
        t += "\n"
    raw.append(t)
doc = "".join(raw)

inc_re = re.compile(r"^<!-- INCLUDE:(python|sh|text|md):([^:>\s]+?)(?::([^>\s]+))? -->$", re.M)
n_inc = len(inc_re.findall(doc))
doc = inc_re.sub(lambda m: expand_include(m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)), doc)

n_proj = len({q.parent for q in (scratch / "projects").rglob(".operational-platform") if q.is_dir()})
doc = doc.replace("@@NPROJECTS@@", str(n_proj))


def _lines(m):
    p = scratch / m.group(1)
    if not p.is_file():
        errors.append(f"@@LINES: missing file {m.group(1)}")
        return "?"
    return str(len(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()))


doc = re.sub(r"@@LINES:([^@\s]+)@@", _lines, doc)      # line count of a program, so the text cannot go stale

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. structure scan
FENCE_OPEN = re.compile(r"^(\s*)(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$")


def scan(lines):
    """yield (index, line, in_fence) while tracking fences; report imbalance."""
    in_f, ch, ln, start = False, "", 0, 0
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = FENCE_OPEN.match(line)
        if not in_f:
            if m:
                in_f, ch, ln, start = True, m.group(2)[0], len(m.group(2)), i
                yield i, line, True
                continue
            yield i, line, False
        else:
            yield i, line, True
            if m and m.group(2)[0] == ch and len(m.group(2)) >= ln and m.group(3).strip() == "":
                in_f = False
    if in_f:
        errors.append(f"unbalanced code fence opened at line {start + 1}")


lines = doc.split("\n")
scanned = list(scan(lines))


def slugify(title):
    t = re.sub(r"`", "", title)
    t = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", t)         # links -> text
    t = re.sub(r"[*]", "", t)
    t = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", t).lower()
    t = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", t, flags=re.UNICODE)       # keep letters, digits, _, -, space
    return t.replace(" ", "-")


heads, slugs, seen = [], {}, {}
for i, line, infence in scanned:
    if infence:
        continue
    m = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$", line)
    if not m:
        continue
    level, title = len(m.group(1)), m.group(2)
    base = slugify(title)
    k = seen.get(base, 0)
    seen[base] = k + 1
    slug = base if k == 0 else f"{base}-{k}"
    heads.append((level, title, slug, i))
    slugs.setdefault(slug, i)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. TOC
toc = ["## Contents", ""]
for level, title, slug, i in heads:
    if level == 2 and not title.startswith(("About this guide", "Contents")):
        toc.append(f"- **[{title}](#{slug})**")
    elif level == 3 and not title.startswith(("How to read it", "Conventions")):
        toc.append(f"  - [{title}](#{slug})")
toc_text = "\n".join(toc)
if "## Contents

- **[Part I — Orientation](#part-i--orientation)**
  - [1. What this is](#1-what-this-is)
  - [2. What is in the archive](#2-what-is-in-the-archive)

lines = doc.split("\n")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4. link check (outside code)
text_no_code = []
for i, line, infence in list(scan(lines)):
    text_no_code.append("" if infence else re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", "", line))
link_re = re.compile(r"\]\(#([^)\s]+)\)")
n_links, bad = 0, []
for i, line in enumerate(text_no_code):
    for m in link_re.finditer(line):
        n_links += 1
        if m.group(1) not in slugs:
            bad.append((i + 1, m.group(1)))
for ln, a in bad:
    errors.append(f"line {ln}: dangling link #{a}")

# link labels that cite a section number must agree with the target's number
label_re = re.compile(r"\[((?:§|[Ss]ection\s+)\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)[^\]]*)\]\(#([^)\s]+)\)")
for i, line in enumerate(text_no_code):
    for m in label_re.finditer(line):
        want = m.group(2).replace(".", "")
        got = re.match(r"(\d+)", m.group(3))
        if got and got.group(1) != want:
            warnings.append(f"line {i + 1}: label {m.group(1)!r} points to #{m.group(3)}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. write + report
final = "\n".join(lines)
final = re.sub(r"\n{4,}", "\n\n\n", final)
final = (final.replace("@@NLINKS@@", f"{n_links:,}").replace("@@NHEADS@@", f"{len(heads):,}")
         .replace("@@NINCLUDES@@", f"{n_inc:,}").replace(HOLD, "@@"))
out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
out_path.write_text(final, encoding="utf-8")
n_h = {lv: sum(1 for h in heads if h[0] == lv) for lv in range(1, 7)}
print(f"parts: {len(parts)}   includes: {n_inc}   lines: {final.count(chr(10)) + 1}   bytes: {len(final.encode('utf-8'))}")
print(f"headings by level: {n_h}   internal links checked: {n_links}   TOC entries: {len(toc) - 2}")
for w in warnings:
    print("WARN ", w)
for e in errors:
    print("ERROR", e)
print("OK" if not errors else f"{len(errors)} error(s)")
sys.exit(1 if errors else 0)
```

### D.7 Mechanical checks

A reader checks a document by reading it; a program checks it by comparing it with the thing it describes. These are the comparisons that programs made. Each program is in [D.6](#d6-the-guides-own-programs).

#### Is the tool the one in the archive?

`check_tool_identity.py` hashed every member of the archive of this edition, and every member of the nested skill, and compared each with the file that was run: the table in [D.2](#d2-the-environment). Nothing differs. The only files in the unpacked copy that the archive lacks are the seven `__pycache__` files of the interpreter. The archive itself was derived from the delivered one, and that step has a report of its own ([D.2](#how-the-package-was-renamed)).

#### Do the documents name the commands that exist?

`check_docs_vs_cli.py` takes the commands from `cli.py` and looks in each of the five documents of the archive for every `cli.py <command>` that it mentions, for backticked names that look like commands but are not, and for commands the document never names.

```
commands in cli.py: 38

SKILL.md
  distinct 'cli.py <cmd>' mentions: 15; unknown to cli.py: []
  backticked kebab-names that look like commands but aren't: []
  cli.py commands never named in this doc: ['close-category', 'close-category-file', 'dry-run', 'explain', 'export-batch', 'find-pattern', 'import-batch', 'inventory-status', 'set-category-scope']

cli-reference.md
  distinct 'cli.py <cmd>' mentions: 19; unknown to cli.py: []
  backticked kebab-names that look like commands but aren't: []
  cli.py commands never named in this doc: []

file-formats.md
  distinct 'cli.py <cmd>' mentions: 0; unknown to cli.py: []
  backticked kebab-names that look like commands but aren't: []
  cli.py commands never named in this doc: ['accept-match', 'add-descriptor-template', 'add-invariant', 'add-source-range', 'apply-all', 'close-category', 'close-category-file', 'copy-across-files', 'domino-next', 'dry-run', 'explain', 'export-batch', 'find-pattern', 'import-batch', 'inventory-next', 'inventory-status', 'move-across-files', 'require-file', 'set-category-scope', 'undo-descriptor']

limitations.md
  distinct 'cli.py <cmd>' mentions: 0; unknown to cli.py: []
  backticked kebab-names that look like commands but aren't: []
  cli.py commands never named in this doc: ['add-invariant', 'add-source-range', 'apply-all', 'close-category-file', 'domino-resolve', 'domino-status', 'explain', 'export-batch', 'find-pattern', 'inventory-next', 'inventory-resolve', 'inventory-status', 'new-batch', 'require-file', 'set-category-scope', 'show-file', 'status']

methodology-mapping.md
  distinct 'cli.py <cmd>' mentions: 0; unknown to cli.py: []
  backticked kebab-names that look like commands but aren't: []
  cli.py commands never named in this doc: ['add-descriptor-template', 'apply-all', 'checkpoint', 'copy-across-files', 'dry-run', 'explain', 'export-batch', 'find-pattern', 'import-batch', 'inventory-next', 'inventory-status', 'move-across-files']
```

No document names a command that does not exist, and none writes a near-miss. Two things follow from the last line of each block. `cli-reference.md` contains the name of every one of the 38 commands (a plain text search, so a short name that is also an English word proves little). **`SKILL.md`** — the page an agent reads first — does not name nine of them: `close-category`, `close-category-file`, `dry-run`, `explain`, `export-batch`, `find-pattern`, `import-batch`, `inventory-status` and `set-category-scope`. The other documents are references for one subject each and are not expected to name them all. The same check was run over this guide. Of the words that follow the file name `cli.py` in it, 38 are commands — all 38 of them — and nine are not, and each of the nine is understood: seven are English words in a sentence (*builds*, *has*, *says*, *from*, *that*, *directly* and *commands*); `newproj` is the shell function that `lib.sh` defines on the line after the assignment of `CLI`; and `nosuchcommand` is the wrong command that the error scenario types on purpose, to see what the tool answers. So the guide writes no command that does not exist.

#### Does the cheat sheet say what the parser says?

The command table and the synopses of [Appendix A](#appendix-a--cheat-sheet) are produced by `gen_cheatsheet.py` from the parser that `cli.py` builds, and the program refuses to run when the parser and its hand-written entries disagree. It did not refuse: 38 commands on both sides.

#### Does the guard's table of options say what the parser says?

The guard of [§60.3](#603-the-guard-wrapper) refuses any option that is not in a table, so the table must be right. `check_guard_table.py` reads the table out of the text of `asm_guard.py`, builds the same table from the parser, and compares them command by command: the number of positional arguments, and every option — its first spelling and whether it takes a value.

```
commands: guard 38, parser 38; options in the parser: 70
the two tables agree
```

A check that cannot fail proves nothing, so it was tested on a copy of the guard from whose table one option had been deleted:

```
$ # the same check, on a copy of the guard from whose table the option --note of accept-match was deleted
commands: guard 38, parser 38; options in the parser: 70
DIFFERENCE accept-match --note: in the parser, not in the guard's table
1 difference(s)
[exit=1]
```

#### Does the "Changes" column say what the commands do?

[A.2](#a2-the-38-commands) says, for each command, which state files it writes. `changes_check.py` builds one project, and for each command copies it, runs the command in the copy, and compares every file of the state directory before and after — content and modification time. A file counts as *written* if its bytes changed, if it is new, or if only its modification time changed (it was rewritten with the same bytes, which is what `sync-domino-queue` does when there is nothing to add). The set of written files is compared with the column, and the exit status with the expected one. The first version of the program counted only changed bytes and found two disagreements; both were rewrites with identical bytes, and the definition of *written* was fixed, not the column.

**44 runs** of **38** different commands (some twice, to cover a variant such as `--project`), each in a fresh copy of the same prepared project; **44 matched** the expectation, 0 did not.

#### Do the state files have the documented formats?

`schema_census.py` reads every state file of every fixture — read-only, and without importing the tool — and checks every record against the schema of Part VII written as data: required keys present, no key in no list, optional keys counted, closed vocabularies tallied. The result is the table of [B.6](#b6-the-census): no required key missing and no unlisted key anywhere. The rules of [B.5](#b5-what-a-healthy-state-satisfies) are those that the auditor tests — the table says which — and the next check runs the auditor over the same fixtures.

#### Is the auditor read-only, and does it survive every state the scenarios left?

`audit_sweep.py` runs `state_audit.py` in every fixture that holds a state directory and in every directory directly under `projects/` that holds none. Before and after each run it hashes the whole tree — every path, size, SHA-256 and modification time in nanoseconds — and compares the two digests.

The auditor was run **180** times — once in each of the **174** projects that hold a state directory and once in each of the **6** directories that hold none — over **32,698** files in all.

| Directories | Exit 0 (nothing found) | Exit 1 (findings printed) | Exit 2 (no state) | Other |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| with a state directory (174) | 96 | 78 | 0 | 0 |
| without one (6) | 0 | 0 | 6 | 0 |

Findings printed, by level: **33 ERROR**, **53 WARN**, **33 INFO** (the scenarios deliberately leave crashes, aborts, stale locks and falsely recovered descriptors behind; the findings are what the auditor is for).

Tracebacks or Python errors: **0**.

Trees that differ after the run (any path, size, content or modification time): **0**.

A `.operational-platform/` created by the auditor where there was none: **0**.

The findings are the point: the scenarios leave crashes, aborts, stale locks and falsely recovered descriptors behind on purpose, and the auditor reports them. What the sweep proves is what the other lines say — no traceback on any of those states, and nothing written: no changed byte, no changed modification time, and no state directory created where there was none.

#### Does the message catalog match the real replies?

[Appendix C](#appendix-c--message-catalog) was built from the source, not from the runs; the check below compares the two in both directions (a real reply that the catalog does not explain, and a catalog entry that no real reply has produced).

```
distinct strings in the error / detail / failure-list fields of the real runs: 118
  matched a template of the catalog : 96
  Python's own text (C.15)          : 9
  data, not messages (category codes, file names, IDs) : 13
  unexplained                       : 0
templates of the catalog (not counting 3 that would match almost anything, nor 5 ID formats and docstrings): 100
  produced by at least one real run : 60
  known from the source only        : 40
```

#### Do the labels of the guide agree with each other?

The guide refers to its findings by labels, and a label that is mentioned must be defined. `check_labels.py` reads the finished guide: it collects the definitions — a table row or a heading per label — and checks that the numbers run without a gap, that the V register's index and its headings define the same numbers, that nothing mentions a label above the highest one defined, and that every range the text states ends where the definitions end.

```
V1 … V31                  deviations from the documentation
S1 … S10                  trust findings
L1 … L23                  stated limitations
G1 … G12                  guarantees
BP1 … BP52                best practices
m1 … m15                  minor findings
E1 … E10 (no E8)          text edge cases
the labels agree
```

#### Are the links of the guide intact?

`assemble.py` expanded 111 listings and transcripts into this file and checked 1,027 internal links to 548 headings: none dangles, and no link whose label cites a section number (`§48.3`) points to a heading of another number. The same program reports a code fence that is opened and not closed. It caught dangling anchors and wrong section labels several times while the guide was being written; the build that produced this file reports none.

### D.8 Tests of the programs of Part IX

The four programs of [Part IX](#part-ix--operating-guide) are advice that runs, so each was tested the way the tool was: by scenarios, with the transcript read. The codes are the scenarios' own; the scripts are in [D.11](#d11-the-scenario-scripts).

| Program | Scenarios | What they show | Shown in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state_audit.py` | **LINT-A … LINT-D** (`sc_lint.sh`): four plans, three of them full of pitfalls that the tool does not refuse when they are added, one clean; the report on 18 fixture projects and on a directory with no state (`sc_audit_samples.sh`); the sweep of [D.7](#d7-mechanical-checks) | every finding is a state that a scenario created on purpose; a clean plan draws no finding (LINT-D); on a root with no state it answers *no state*, exit 2, and creates nothing; it never writes | [§59.2](#592-a-read-only-state-auditor) |
| `release_lock.py` | **RL1 … RL4** (`sc_release_lock.sh`): the state before; refusals, and a report without `--yes`; the release, then a new plan; the state afterwards | the single hand edit that the tool's documentation allows, done without opening the file in an editor and only with `--yes` | [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch) |
| `asm_guard.py` | **GD1 … GD5** (`sc_guard.sh`): a normal flow with the guard's remarks; refusals; the strict parser (abbreviations, unknown options, argument counts); the lock held by another command; a root inside another project; the timeout. **AB-A, AB-B** (`sc_abbrev.sh`): `argparse` accepts `--payload-f`; the guard refuses it. The table check of [D.7](#d7-mechanical-checks) | what a refusal looks like (`guard_error` on standard output, exit 3), that a refusal changes nothing, that two commands cannot overlap, and why the table of options must come from the real parser | [§60.3](#603-the-guard-wrapper) |
| `driver.py` | **DR1 … DR4** (`sc_driver.sh`): a clean run, plan then apply; somebody edits the file between the two and the driver stops at the abort; an invariant that does not hold, so that `validate-post` fails and the driver says so; refusals — a mistyped path and an inverted range | that the driver reads every reply, stops where it must, and reports the reason in words | [§60.4](#604-a-reference-driver) |

What these tests cannot show is the guard under real concurrency — two long commands started at once by two callers — beyond the single case of GD3, in which the lock is already held; and the driver against any model: it is a reference, and the contract it implements ([§60.2](#602-the-contract-what-to-parse-when-to-continue-when-to-stop)) is what a port should be tested against ([§61.6](#616-acceptance-tests-for-a-port)).

### D.9 Measurements

Every timing here is one run on the machine of [D.2](#d2-the-environment): two virtual CPUs, shared with other work. Read the numbers as orders of magnitude and as ratios between rows.

**One batch of 200 descriptors on a file of 20,000 lines.** `bench.sh` makes a file of 20,000 lines, registers it, opens a batch, adds 200 `replace_range` descriptors — one command each, so 200 processes — and then runs `validate-plan`, `apply-all` and `validate-post`, timing each with `date`.

```
file: 20000 lines, 788894 bytes
register:
   -> 0.13s
registry.json: 749044 bytes
add 200 replace_range descriptors (separate process each):
   -> 13.58s total, 0.068s per call
validate-plan:
   -> 0.30s
apply-all:
   -> 10.77s
validate-post:
   -> 0.08s
sizes: registry.json 756444 B, descriptors.json 134943 B, wal.jsonl 45000 B (401 lines), payloads: 400 blobs
file after: 20000 lines; edited lines: 200

real	0m25.114s
user	0m21.181s
sys	0m2.963s
```

| Step | Time | Per descriptor |
|---|---:|---:|
| `register` of the file | 0.13 s | — |
| 200 × `add-descriptor`, each in its own process | 13.58 s | 68 ms |
| `validate-plan` | 0.30 s | 1.5 ms |
| `apply-all` | 10.77 s | 54 ms |
| `validate-post` | 0.08 s | — |

`registry.json` was 749,044 bytes for the 20,000 lines — about 37 bytes per line — and every apply loads it and writes it back whole; that is the 54 ms ([§41.5](#415-cost-model-and-measured-scale)). `descriptors.json` ended at 134,943 bytes and the WAL at 401 lines.

**Adding descriptors is quadratic.** `bench_plan.py` adds *D* descriptors to a batch **in one process** — so that the cost of starting Python does not hide the trend — on a file of 5,000 lines, and then times `validate-plan`.

```
D=  500: add (in-process)    4.4s, validate-plan   0.27s -> pass, descriptors.json 0.32 MB
D= 1000: add (in-process)   14.6s, validate-plan   0.54s -> pass, descriptors.json 0.64 MB
D= 2000: add (in-process)   50.5s, validate-plan   1.69s -> pass, descriptors.json 1.28 MB
D= 4000: add (in-process)  190.4s, validate-plan   6.11s -> pass, descriptors.json 2.56 MB

real	4m28.464s
user	3m59.891s
sys	0m14.052s
```

Each doubling of *D* multiplied the time to add by 3.3, 3.5 and 3.8: towards the factor 4 of a quadratic cost, because every `add_descriptor` loads and rewrites the whole `descriptors.json`, which grows with *D*. `validate-plan` grew by 2.0, 3.1 and 3.6 — linearly at first, then faster, and not yet quadratic in this range. The guidance of [BP26](#583-planning) follows: keep a batch to a few hundred descriptors.

**The size of a reply.** `show-file` prints every line as a five-line JSON object, so that what an agent reads is large ([§60.1](#601-what-changes-when-the-caller-is-a-model)). `sc_showsize.sh` ([D.11](#sc_showsizesh)) measured one file:

```
show-file of a 1000-line file: 5006 lines of JSON, 126856 bytes
{
  "file_id": "f_ffa9d0dd71",
  "path": "big.txt",
  "lines": [
    {
      "pos": 1,
      "line_id": "f_ffa9d0dd71_l00001",
      "text": "line 1: some typical source text here"
    },
    {
      "pos": 2,
      "line_id": "f_ffa9d0dd71_l00002",
keys: ['file_id', 'lines', 'path'] | first entry: {'pos': 1, 'line_id': 'f_ffa9d0dd71_l00001', 'text': 'line 1: some typical source text here'}
```

#### `bench.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
LINES=${1:-20000}; N=${2:-200}
newproj bench_${LINES}_${N}
python3 -I -c "
import sys
n=int(sys.argv[1])
open('big.txt','w').write(''.join(f'line {i} some filler text for realism\n' for i in range(1,n+1)))
" $LINES
echo "file: $(wc -l < big.txt) lines, $(wc -c < big.txt) bytes"
t() { local s=$(date +%s.%N); "$@"; local e=$(date +%s.%N); printf '   -> %.2fs\n' "$(echo "$e - $s" | bc)"; }
echo "register:";        t quiet register big.txt
F=$(python3 -I "$CLI" register big.txt | python3 -I -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["file_id"])')
echo "registry.json: $(wc -c < .operational-platform/registry.json) bytes"
quiet new-batch
echo "add $N replace_range descriptors (separate process each):"
s=$(date +%s.%N)
STEP=$(( LINES / N ))
for i in $(seq 1 $N); do
  pos=$(( (i-1)*STEP + 1 ))
  id=$(printf '%s_l%05d' "$F" "$pos")
  python3 -I "$CLI" add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file big.txt --start "$id" --end "$id" --payload-text "EDITED $i" >/dev/null
done
e=$(date +%s.%N); printf '   -> %.2fs total, %.3fs per call\n' "$(echo "$e - $s" | bc)" "$(echo "($e - $s)/$N" | bc -l)"
echo "validate-plan:";   t quiet validate-plan batch_0001
echo "apply-all:";       t quiet apply-all batch_0001
echo "validate-post:";   t quiet validate-post batch_0001
echo "sizes: registry.json $(wc -c < .operational-platform/registry.json) B, descriptors.json $(wc -c < .operational-platform/batches/batch_0001/descriptors.json) B, wal.jsonl $(wc -c < .operational-platform/wal.jsonl) B ($(wc -l < .operational-platform/wal.jsonl) lines), payloads: $(ls .operational-platform/payloads | wc -l) blobs"
echo "file after: $(wc -l < big.txt) lines; edited lines: $(grep -c '^EDITED' big.txt)"
```

#### `bench_plan.py`

```python
"""validate-plan scaling: in-process, D distinct replace_range descriptors on a 5,000-line file.
Usage: python3 -I bench_plan.py <scripts_dir> <work_dir>"""
import sys, os, time, pathlib, shutil
scripts_dir, base = sys.argv[1], pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve()
sys.path.insert(0, scripts_dir)
import engine, registry, storage, validator
for D in (500, 1000, 2000, 4000):
    p = base / f"plan_{D}"; shutil.rmtree(p, ignore_errors=True); p.mkdir(parents=True); os.chdir(p)
    (p / "f.txt").write_text("".join(f"line {i}\n" for i in range(1, 5001)))
    registry.register_file("f.txt"); fid = registry.file_id_for("f.txt")
    b = engine.new_batch()
    t0 = time.time()
    for i in range(D):
        lid = f"{fid}_l{i+1:05d}"
        engine.add_descriptor(b, "replace_range", "f.txt", start=lid, end=lid, payload_text=f"E{i}")
    t1 = time.time()
    r = validator.validate_plan(b)
    t2 = time.time()
    print(f"D={D:5d}: add (in-process) {t1-t0:6.1f}s, validate-plan {t2-t1:6.2f}s -> {r['result']}, descriptors.json {os.path.getsize(p/'.operational-platform/batches'/b/'descriptors.json')/1e6:.2f} MB", flush=True)
```

### D.10 What was not verified

An appendix about verification owes the reader the other list. What follows was **not** checked — and each item says what the guide does instead.

| Not verified | What the guide does |
|---|---|
| **Two processes at once.** No two commands were ever run concurrently on one project. | The lost updates and the double apply of [§48.1](#481-what-is-atomic-and-what-is-not) are *code-derived*. The advice — one command at a time — is enforced only by the guard ([§60.3](#603-the-guard-wrapper)), and only among those who use it. |
| **A kill in the middle of a write.** The crash harness stops *between* two writes; it never interrupts one. Two crashes in a row, a crash during `undo`, `import-batch` or any command but an apply, and a crash before the first or after the last step of an apply were not simulated. | A torn managed file ([§43.5](#435-reading-and-writing-managed-files)) is *code-derived*. The auditor looks for the trace — an `op_start` with no `op_applied` — and [§48.5](#485-after-an-unclean-stop-a-protocol) gives the protocol. |
| **Power loss, a full disk, a read-only file, a permission error.** | That there is no `fsync` was found by searching the source for the word; what a power cut does is *code-derived* ([§43.2](#432-the-json-writer)). |
| **Any platform but one.** CPython 3.13.16 on Linux x86-64. No other interpreter, no Windows, no macOS, no case-insensitive or network file system. | The "Python needed" column of [D.6](#d6-the-guides-own-programs) is a static estimate, not a run. `asm_guard.py` imports `fcntl` and works only where it exists. A path spelled with a backslash is refused by the guard and untested in the tool. |
| **Unusual objects in the file system.** No scenario created a symbolic link, a hard link or a device file, or changed a permission. A directory given where a file was expected was tried once (`register .`: `IsADirectoryError`, [C.15](#c15-messages-that-are-not-the-tools-own)). | Not claimed. |
| **Scale beyond what was measured.** The largest runs: a file of 20,000 lines with 200 descriptors, and 4,000 descriptors in one batch added in one process. No file of hundreds of thousands of lines; no measurement of memory. | [§41.5](#415-cost-model-and-measured-scale) says so beside the numbers. |
| **Hostile input.** No fuzzing. No hostile archive was offered to `import-batch`, and no adversarial payload to the guard beyond the tests of [D.8](#d8-tests-of-the-programs-of-part-ix). | The trust findings S1–S10 ([§57.2](#572-findings)) mark each as verified or code-derived; four were run — S2, S3, S4 and S8 — and the guard's tests refuse the inputs of S2, S3 and S4. |
| **Every message the tool can print.** Of the templates of [Appendix C](#appendix-c--message-catalog) that can be tested, the real runs produced only some; the others are read from the source ([D.7](#d7-mechanical-checks)). | The catalog is complete for the source and verified for the messages that were produced. |
| **The documents' claim of "an automated test" behind each stated behavior.** The archive ships no tests. | [§2.3](#23-what-is-not-in-the-archive). |
| **Another version of the archive.** Everything here holds for the archive of [D.2](#d2-the-environment) — identified by its SHA-256 — and, because its code is the delivered code ([D.2](#how-the-package-was-renamed)), for the delivered archive too; the code has no version constant. | Compare the checksum before you rely on a line number of the catalog. |
| **Projects that hold state under the delivered name.** The carry-over check of [D.2](#how-the-package-was-renamed) ran one small project: one file, one batch, one descriptor, ten state files — not a crashed apply, not a project with several batches. | The check looked for the old name in every state file and found none; renaming the directory is the whole change, but make the first trial on a copy. |

**Statements labeled *code-derived*** are the ones the guide could not run. The exact list is the answer to [Q37](#625-the-documentation-and-this-guide) and the entries marked *(code-derived)* in [§56.9](#569-minor-findings) (m8, m9, m12, m13); [§55](#55-stated-limitations-and-their-verification-status) gives the verdict, with its basis, for each of the tool's own stated limitations.

**The guide's own programs** were tested on the states that the scenarios produce — a large set, but one that a single reader made. The auditor sees structure, not content ([§59.2](#592-a-read-only-state-auditor)); the guard is a wrapper, and anyone who runs `cli.py` directly goes around it.

**What would strengthen the verification** is cheap, and is why the scripts are printed: run `repro_check.py` on your platform and your interpreter and read the table of differences; run the crash harness on the version of the tool you will use; and, if you port the methodology, test the port with the scenarios of [§61.6](#616-acceptance-tests-for-a-port), which are these scenarios made abstract.

### D.11 The scenario scripts

Every script that produced a transcript of this guide, in full: the helpers first, then the scenario scripts in alphabetical order. The table in [D.3](#d3-the-scenarios) says what each one is about and links here. To run them, set `S` in `lib.sh` (and in `sc_audit_samples.sh`, which sets its own) to a directory of your choice, unpack the skill at `$S/operational-platform-skill-extracted/` (so that `cli.py` is at `$S/operational-platform-skill-extracted/operational-platform/scripts/cli.py`), put the scripts in `$S/scripts/`, and run `bash $S/scripts/sc_NAME.sh`; each script makes its own project directories under `$S/projects/`. `repro_check.py` ([D.6](#repro_checkpy)) does all of this in a new directory and compares what each script prints with the transcript.

#### `lib.sh`

```bash
# shared helpers for scenario scripts (sourced, not executed)
S=/path/to/work
CLI=$S/operational-platform-skill-extracted/operational-platform/scripts/cli.py
newproj() { P="$S/projects/$1"; rm -rf "$P"; mkdir -p "$P"; cd "$P" || exit 1; }
run() { echo "\$ cli.py $*"; python3 -I "$CLI" "$@"; echo "[exit=$?]"; echo; }
quiet() { python3 -I "$CLI" "$@" >/dev/null; }
# file id for a relative path (does a register, idempotent)
fid() { python3 -I "$CLI" register "$1" | python3 -I -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["file_id"])'; }
show() { echo "--- $1"; cat -A "$1" | sed 's/\$$/⏎/'; echo; }
```

#### `sc_abbrev.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
G=$S/scripts/asm_guard.py; SK=$(dirname "$CLI")
newproj abbrev; printf 'alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n' > a.txt; printf 'SECRET-FROM-OUTSIDE\n' > ../abbrev_secret.txt; P=$PWD
F=$(fid a.txt); quiet new-batch
echo "##### AB-A: argparse accepts an unambiguous prefix of a long option (here --payload-f for --payload-file)"
run add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-f ../abbrev_secret.txt
echo "##### AB-B: the guard refuses the abbreviated spelling"
echo "\$ asm_guard -- add-descriptor ... --payload-f ../abbrev_secret.txt"
python3 -I "$G" "$P" "$SK" -- add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-f ../abbrev_secret.txt 2>&1 | head -8
echo "[exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}]"
echo "\$ asm_guard -- add-descriptor ... --fil ../x.txt   (an abbreviated --file)"
python3 -I "$G" "$P" "$SK" -- add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --fil ../abbrev_secret.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text X 2>&1 | head -6
echo "[exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}]"
```

#### `sc_abort.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
r1() { echo "\$ cli.py $*"; python3 -I "$CLI" "$@" 2>&1 | python3 -I -c "import sys,json;print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin),ensure_ascii=False))" 2>/dev/null || true; echo "[exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}]"; }
newproj abort
printf 'def old_name(x):\n    return x + 1\n\nprint(old_name(1))\n' > app.py
F=$(fid app.py); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file app.py --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text 'def new_name(x):'
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file app.py --start ${F}_l00004 --end ${F}_l00004 --payload-text 'print(new_name(1))'
r1 validate-plan batch_0001
r1 apply-next batch_0001
echo "##### AB1: somebody edits line 4 outside the tool"
sed -i 's/old_name(1)/old_name(999)/' app.py; show app.py
r1 apply-next batch_0001
r1 resume
r1 check batch_0001 d0002
r1 status batch_0001
r1 validate-post batch_0001
echo "##### AB2: the 'fresh batch' recovery -- does the stale lock block it?"
r1 new-batch
r1 show-file app.py
quiet add-descriptor batch_0002 --op replace_range --file app.py --start ${F}_l00004 --end ${F}_l00004 --payload-text 'print(new_name(999))'
r1 validate-plan batch_0002
cat .operational-platform/active_locks.json | python3 -I -c "import sys,json;print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin)))"
echo "##### AB3: remove the stale lock by hand (the documented exception), then re-plan"
python3 -I - <<'PY'
import json
p='.operational-platform/active_locks.json'
d=json.load(open(p)); d['batches'].pop('batch_0001'); json.dump(d,open(p,'w'),indent=2)
PY
r1 validate-plan batch_0002
r1 apply-all batch_0002
show app.py
r1 validate-post batch_0002
r1 status batch_0001
```

#### `sc_assembly.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
newproj assembly
printf '# Title A\nintro A\n## Install\nstep 1\nstep 2\n## Legacy\nold stuff\n' > s1.md
printf '# Title B\nintro B\n## Usage\nuse it\n' > s2.md
printf '# Combined\n\n' > out.md
F1=$(fid s1.md); F2=$(fid s2.md); FO=$(fid out.md); B=batch_0001
run new-batch --shape assembly
echo "##### gate: no inventory started"
run validate-plan $B
run add-source-range $B --file s1.md --start ${F1}_l00001 --end ${F1}_l00005
run add-source-range $B --file s1.md --start ${F1}_l00006 --end ${F1}_l00007
run add-source-range $B --file s2.md --start ${F2}_l00001 --end ${F2}_l00002
run add-source-range $B --file s2.md --start ${F2}_l00003 --end ${F2}_l00004
run inventory-next $B
echo "##### gate: ranges still pending"
run validate-plan $B
printf 'intro A\n## Install\nstep 1\nstep 2' > edited.txt
run add-descriptor $B --op insert_after --file out.md --after ${FO}_l00002 --payload-file edited.txt
run copy-across-files $B --src-file s2.md --start ${F2}_l00003 --end ${F2}_l00004 --dest-file out.md --dest-after ${FO}_l00002
run inventory-resolve $B ri0001 --disposition transferred_with_edit --descriptor-ids d0001 --note "title dropped, body kept"
run inventory-resolve $B ri0002 --disposition excluded --note "legacy section deliberately dropped"
run inventory-resolve $B ri0003 --disposition excluded --note "title+intro of the second source not needed"
run inventory-resolve $B ri0004 --disposition transferred_with_edit --descriptor-ids d0002
run inventory-status $B
run add-invariant $B --file out.md --pattern '(?m)^## ' --expected-count 2 --description "Install + Usage headings, no Legacy"
run validate-plan $B
run apply-all $B
show out.md
run validate-post $B
```

#### `sc_audit.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
newproj audit
printf 'import os\ndef Get_User(name):\n    print("debug", name)\n    return name\n' > a.py
printf 'from a import Get_User\nx = Get_User("bob")\nprint("debug", x)\n' > b.py
FA=$(fid a.py); FB=$(fid b.py); B=batch_0001
run new-batch --shape audit
echo "##### shape gate: no taxonomy yet"
run validate-plan $B
run add-category $B --code NAMING --description "identifier violates snake_case convention"
run add-category $B --code DEBUG --description "debug output left in code"
run add-category $B --code STYLE --description "formatting / import hygiene"
run add-descriptor $B --op replace_range --file a.py --start ${FA}_l00002 --end ${FA}_l00002 --payload-text 'def get_user(name):' --category NAMING --severity major --domino-hint Get_User --rule-ref "style-guide 2.1" --context 'def Get_User'
quiet add-descriptor $B --op delete_range --file a.py --start ${FA}_l00003 --end ${FA}_l00003 --category DEBUG --severity minor
run sync-domino-queue $B
echo "##### domino-next for dm0001 (hint Get_User): candidates in b.py not yet covered"
run domino-next $B
quiet add-descriptor $B --op replace_range --file b.py --start ${FB}_l00001 --end ${FB}_l00001 --payload-text 'from a import get_user' --category NAMING --severity major --provenance domino --domino-of d0001
quiet add-descriptor $B --op replace_range --file b.py --start ${FB}_l00002 --end ${FB}_l00002 --payload-text 'x = get_user("bob")' --category NAMING --severity major --provenance domino --domino-of d0001
run domino-resolve $B dm0001
run domino-next $B
run domino-resolve $B dm0002
run domino-status $B
echo "##### taxonomy gate: STYLE has neither a finding nor a closure"
run validate-plan $B
run close-category $B --code STYLE --note "checked a.py and b.py: nothing found"
echo "##### file x category matrix (opt-in)"
run set-category-scope $B --code DEBUG --files a.py,b.py
run validate-plan $B
run close-category-file $B --code DEBUG --file b.py --note "b.py print is CLI output, reviewed"
run add-invariant $B --file a.py --pattern Get_User --expected-count 0 --description "no old name in a.py" --checked-against a.py --severity major
run add-invariant $B --file b.py --pattern Get_User --expected-count 0 --description "no old name in b.py" --checked-against b.py --severity major
run add-invariant $B --file b.py --pattern 'print\(' --expected-count 0 --description "no print() left in b.py" --severity minor
run validate-plan $B
run apply-all $B
show a.py; show b.py
echo "##### validate-post (fails: one print left in b.py)"
run validate-post $B
run accept-match $B --file b.py --pattern 'print\(' --line 3 --note "legit CLI output"
echo "##### validate-post again after accept-match"
run validate-post $B
run status $B --group-by file_id,category
run report --batches $B
run checkpoint
```

#### `sc_driver.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
D=$S/scripts/driver.py; SK=$(dirname "$CLI")
drv() { echo "\$ driver.py ROOT SCRIPTS $*"; python3 -I "$D" "$P" "$SK" "$@"; echo "[exit=$?]"; echo; }
echo "##### DR1: a clean run -- plan, then apply"
newproj drv1; P=$PWD
printf 'def old_name(x):\n    return x + 1\n\nprint(old_name(1))\n' > app.py
cat > "$S/projects/plan1.json" <<'JSON'
{"files": ["app.py"],
 "descriptors": [
   {"op": "replace_range", "file": "app.py", "lines": [1, 1], "payload": "def new_name(x):"},
   {"op": "replace_range", "file": "app.py", "lines": [4, 4], "payload": "print(new_name(1))"},
   {"op": "insert_after",  "file": "app.py", "after_line": 0, "payload": "# renamed by a batch"}],
 "invariants": [{"file": "app.py", "pattern": "old_name", "expected": 0, "checked_against": "app.py"}]}
JSON
drv plan "$S/projects/plan1.json"
drv apply batch_0001
cat app.py; echo
echo "##### DR2: somebody edits the file between plan and apply -- the driver stops at the abort"
newproj drv2; P=$PWD
printf 'def old_name(x):\n    return x + 1\n\nprint(old_name(1))\n' > app.py
drv plan "$S/projects/plan1.json"
sed -i 's/old_name(1)/old_name(999)/' app.py
drv apply batch_0001
echo "##### DR3: an invariant that does not hold -- validate-post fails and the driver says so"
newproj drv3; P=$PWD
printf 'def old_name(x):\n    return x + 1\n\nprint(old_name(1))\n' > app.py
cat > "$S/projects/plan3.json" <<'JSON'
{"files": ["app.py"],
 "descriptors": [{"op": "replace_range", "file": "app.py", "lines": [1, 1], "payload": "def new_name(x):"}],
 "invariants": [{"file": "app.py", "pattern": "old_name", "expected": 0, "checked_against": "app.py"}]}
JSON
drv plan "$S/projects/plan3.json"
drv apply batch_0001
echo "##### DR4: refusals -- a typo'd path and an inverted range"
newproj drv4; P=$PWD
printf 'a\nb\nc\n' > app.py
echo '{"files": ["apps.py"], "descriptors": []}' > "$S/projects/plan4a.json"
drv plan "$S/projects/plan4a.json"
newproj drv4b; P=$PWD; printf 'a\nb\nc\n' > app.py
echo '{"files": ["app.py"], "descriptors": [{"op": "delete_range", "file": "app.py", "lines": [3, 1]}]}' > "$S/projects/plan4b.json"
drv plan "$S/projects/plan4b.json"
```

#### `sc_final.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
r1() { echo "\$ cli.py $*"; python3 -I "$CLI" "$@" 2>&1 | python3 -I -c "import sys,json;print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin),ensure_ascii=False))" 2>/dev/null || true; }
flat() { tr '\n' ' ' < "$1"; echo; }

echo "##### U2: undo of each op type"
for op in replace delete insert copy move; do
  newproj u_$op; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\nL4\nL5\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
  case $op in
    replace) quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00003 --payload-text $'X\nY\nZ';;
    delete)  quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op delete_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00003;;
    insert)  quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op insert_after --file f.txt --after ${F}_l00002 --payload-text $'N1\nN2';;
    copy)    quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op copy_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00002 --dest ${F}_l00004;;
    move)    quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op move_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00003 --dest ${F}_l00005;;
  esac
  quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001
  echo "$op: applied -> $(flat f.txt)"
  python3 -I "$CLI" undo-descriptor batch_0001 d0001 | python3 -I -c "import sys,json;print('   undo ->',json.load(sys.stdin))"
  echo "   after undo -> $(flat f.txt)"
  python3 -I -c 'import json;r=json.load(open(".operational-platform/registry.json"));f=list(r["files"].values())[0];print("   registry:",{k[-6:]:v for k,v in f["lines"].items()},"next_seq",f["next_seq"])'
done

echo; echo "##### U3: undo-order hazard: undo an EARLIER descriptor while a LATER one built on it"
newproj u_order; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text 'TWO'
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op insert_after --file f.txt --after ${F}_l00001 --payload-text 'after-one'
quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001; echo "applied -> $(flat f.txt)"
r1 undo-descriptor batch_0001 d0001
echo "after undo d0001 -> $(flat f.txt)"
r1 validate-post batch_0001

echo; echo "##### U4: undo of an unapplied descriptor / double undo"
newproj u_dbl; printf 'L1\nL2\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text 'A'
r1 undo-descriptor batch_0001 d0001
quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001; quiet undo-descriptor batch_0001 d0001
r1 undo-descriptor batch_0001 d0001

echo; echo "##### J1: javascript syntax check (node present)"
newproj js1; printf 'const a = 1;\nconst b = 2;\n' > x.js; F=$(fid x.js); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file x.js --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text 'const b = ;'
quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001
python3 -I "$CLI" validate-post batch_0001 | python3 -I -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d["result"],{k.split("/")[-1]:v for k,v in d["syntax"].items()})'

echo; echo "##### PC: project-level constraint inheritance (SEC closed so the taxonomy gate passes)"
newproj pc; printf 'a\nb\nc\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch; quiet new-batch
quiet add-constraint batch_0001 --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --reason "project-wide freeze" --project
quiet add-descriptor batch_0002 --op delete_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003
r1 validate-plan batch_0002

echo; echo "##### AS: assembly, corrected flow (dependency orders the stacked inserts) + dry-run"
newproj asm; printf '# Title A\nintro A\n## Install\nstep 1\nstep 2\n## Legacy\nold stuff\n' > s1.md
printf '# Title B\nintro B\n## Usage\nuse it\n' > s2.md; printf '# Combined\n\n' > out.md
F1=$(fid s1.md); F2=$(fid s2.md); FO=$(fid out.md); B=batch_0001
quiet new-batch --shape assembly
quiet add-source-range $B --file s1.md --start ${F1}_l00001 --end ${F1}_l00005
quiet add-source-range $B --file s1.md --start ${F1}_l00006 --end ${F1}_l00007
quiet add-source-range $B --file s2.md --start ${F2}_l00001 --end ${F2}_l00002
quiet add-source-range $B --file s2.md --start ${F2}_l00003 --end ${F2}_l00004
printf 'intro A\n## Install\nstep 1\nstep 2' > edited.txt
quiet copy-across-files $B --src-file s2.md --start ${F2}_l00003 --end ${F2}_l00004 --dest-file out.md --dest-after ${FO}_l00002
quiet add-descriptor $B --op insert_after --file out.md --after ${FO}_l00002 --payload-file edited.txt --depends-on d0001
quiet inventory-resolve $B ri0001 --disposition transferred_with_edit --descriptor-ids d0002 --note "title dropped"
quiet inventory-resolve $B ri0002 --disposition excluded --note "legacy section dropped"
quiet inventory-resolve $B ri0003 --disposition excluded --note "title+intro of 2nd source not needed"
quiet inventory-resolve $B ri0004 --disposition transferred_verbatim --descriptor-ids d0001 --note "copied as-is"
quiet add-invariant $B --file out.md --pattern '(?m)^## ' --expected-count 2 --description "Install + Usage headings, no Legacy"
r1 validate-plan $B
run dry-run $B --file out.md
quiet apply-all $B; show out.md
r1 validate-post $B
```

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
G=$S/scripts/asm_guard.py; SK=$(dirname "$CLI")
newproj guard; mkdir sub; printf 'alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n' > a.txt; P=$PWD
g() { echo "\$ asm_guard -- $*"; python3 -I "$G" "$P" "$SK" -- "$@"; echo "[exit=$?]"; echo; }
echo "##### GD1: a normal flow, with the guard's remarks (stderr lines start with '# guard:')"
g register a.txt
F=$(fid a.txt)
g new-batch
g add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text BETA
g add-invariant batch_0001 --file a.txt --pattern '^BETA' --expected-count 1
g validate-plan batch_0001
g apply-all batch_0001
g undo-descriptor batch_0001 d0001
g apply-next batch_0001
echo "##### GD2: refusals"
g status ../../probe
g register ./a.txt
g register /etc/hostname
g register ../outside.txt
g register sub/
g add-descriptor-template batch_0001 --find '' --replace X
g add-invariant batch_0001 --file a.txt --pattern 'a(' --expected-count 1
g add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text X --depends-on 'd0001, d0002'
g add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-file /etc/hostname
g report --batches batch_0001,../x
g import-batch whatever.tar.gz
echo "##### GD2b: the strict parser -- abbreviations, unknown options, argument counts"
g add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-f ../outside.txt
g add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --fil ../outside.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text X
g add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text -X
g add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-file=/etc/hostname
g status batch_0001 extra
g status
g frobnicate batch_0001
g register a.txt --force=yes
g add-invariant batch_0001 --file a.txt --pattern=^x --expected-count 1 --excl
echo "-- and the same line spelled correctly, with the = form for a value that starts with a dash:"
g add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --payload-text=-X
echo "-- nothing was created outside the state directory:"; ls -A "$P"
echo; echo "##### GD3: the lock -- another command holds it"
python3 -I - "$P" <<'PY' &
import fcntl, hashlib, sys, tempfile, time
from pathlib import Path
root = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
f = open(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / ("asm-guard-" + hashlib.sha256(str(root).encode()).hexdigest()[:12] + ".lock"), "w")
fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX); time.sleep(3)
PY
sleep 0.5
echo "\$ asm_guard --lock-timeout 1 -- status batch_0001"; python3 -I "$G" --lock-timeout 1 "$P" "$SK" -- status batch_0001; echo "[exit=$?]"
wait
g status batch_0001
echo; echo "##### GD4: a root inside another project -- the walk upward would find the wrong state (S8)"
mkdir -p "$P/sub/inner"
echo "\$ asm_guard PROJECT_ROOT=<project>/sub/inner -- status batch_0001"; python3 -I "$G" "$P/sub/inner" "$SK" -- status batch_0001; echo "[exit=$?]"
echo "-- nothing was created there:"; ls -A "$P/sub/inner" | wc -l
echo "-- the same command with the real root works (exit status only):"; python3 -I "$G" "$P" "$SK" -- status batch_0001 >/dev/null; echo "[exit=$?]"
echo; echo "##### GD5: the timeout (a read-only command and a timeout of one millisecond)"
echo "\$ asm_guard --timeout 0.001 -- status batch_0001"; python3 -I "$G" --timeout 0.001 "$P" "$SK" -- status batch_0001; echo "[exit=$?]"
```

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

echo "##### A: re-validate after a partial apply when a pending descriptor depends on an applied one"
newproj i_a; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op insert_after --file f.txt --after ${F}_l00001 --payload-text X
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --payload-text Z --depends-on d0001
run validate-plan batch_0001
run apply-next batch_0001
run validate-plan batch_0001
run status batch_0001
show f.txt

echo; echo "##### A2: same for domino_of pointing at an already-applied descriptor"
newproj i_a2; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text A
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text B --provenance domino --domino-of d0001
run validate-plan batch_0001
run apply-next batch_0001
run validate-plan batch_0001

echo; echo "##### B: add-descriptor-template with an empty --find"
newproj i_b; printf 'ab\ncd\n' > f.txt; quiet register f.txt; quiet new-batch
run add-descriptor-template batch_0001 --find '' --replace X
run explain batch_0001 d0001

echo; echo "##### C: undo of delete when an earlier-applied insert sits between the anchor and the block"
newproj i_c; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\nL4\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op insert_after --file f.txt --after ${F}_l00001 --payload-text X
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op delete_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00003
run validate-plan batch_0001
run apply-all batch_0001
show f.txt
run undo-descriptor batch_0001 d0002
show f.txt

echo; echo "##### D: a REFUSED undo still writes undo_start to the WAL"
newproj i_d; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text NEW
quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001
sed -i 's/^NEW$/CHANGED/' f.txt
run undo-descriptor batch_0001 d0001
tail -3 .operational-platform/wal.jsonl

echo; echo "##### E: --depends-on with a space after the comma"
newproj i_e; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text A
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text B
run add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --payload-text C --depends-on 'd0001, d0002'
run validate-plan batch_0001

echo; echo "##### F: rule_ref normalisation"
newproj i_f; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\nL4\nL5\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text A --rule-ref '1.11'
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text B --rule-ref '11.1'
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --payload-text C --rule-ref 'Section 7.1'
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00004 --end ${F}_l00004 --payload-text D --rule-ref '7.1'
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00005 --end ${F}_l00005 --payload-text E --rule-ref '§7.1'
run validate-plan batch_0001

echo; echo "##### G: inventory-resolve on an already-resolved range"
newproj i_g; printf 'a\nb\n' > s.txt; F=$(fid s.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-source-range batch_0001 --file s.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00002
run inventory-resolve batch_0001 ri0001 --disposition excluded --note first
run inventory-resolve batch_0001 ri0001 --disposition transferred_verbatim --note second
cat .operational-platform/batches/batch_0001/region_inventory.json

echo; echo "##### H: a read-only command in a directory with no state dir"
rm -rf "$S/projects/i_h"; mkdir -p "$S/projects/i_h"; cd "$S/projects/i_h"
ls -A
run checkpoint
ls -A; ls -A .operational-platform

echo; echo "##### I: apply-all when a later descriptor raises an uncaught exception"
newproj i_i; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text A
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op copy_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --dest START
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --payload-text C
run validate-plan batch_0001
run apply-all batch_0001
run status batch_0001
show f.txt

echo; echo "##### K: check does not tell whether an insert was already applied"
newproj i_k; printf 'L1\nL2\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op insert_after --file f.txt --after ${F}_l00001 --payload-text X
quiet validate-plan batch_0001
run check batch_0001 d0001
quiet apply-all batch_0001
run check batch_0001 d0001

echo; echo "##### L: dependency_cycle lists everything left, including descriptors downstream of the cycle"
newproj i_l; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text A --depends-on d0002
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text B --depends-on d0001
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --payload-text C --depends-on d0001
run validate-plan batch_0001
```

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
J() { python3 -I -c "$1"; }

echo "##### L9: a domino-provenance descriptor is not queued for its own trace"
newproj l9; printf 'a foo\nb\nc foo\n' > a.txt; F=$(fid a.txt); quiet new-batch --shape rename

run add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --payload-text 'c bar' --provenance domino --domino-of d0001
run sync-domino-queue batch_0001
run domino-status batch_0001

python3 -I "$CLI" validate-post batch_0001 | J "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);i=d['invariants'][0];print('result:',d['result'],'| actual:',i['actual'],'| listed matches:',len(i['matches']),'| matches_truncated:',i.get('matches_truncated'))"

quiet add-invariant batch_0001 --file a.txt --pattern old_name --expected-count 0 --exclude-comments
quiet validate-plan batch_0001
python3 -I "$CLI" validate-post batch_0001 | J "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);i=d['invariants'][0];print('actual:',i['actual'],'raw_matches_before_exceptions:',i['raw_matches_before_exceptions']);print('still counted:',[m['text'] for m in i['matches']])"

quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op delete_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --payload-text 'foo -- brand new, never reviewed'
quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001
run validate-post batch_0001
show a.txt

echo; echo "##### L17: --checked-against is matched by exact path string, and registering counts as evidence"

quiet add-invariant batch_0001 --file t.txt --pattern old --expected-count 0 --checked-against ./spec.md

quiet new-batch

echo "-- spec.md was registered but never shown or read by any command; WAL events:"
```

#### `sc_lockorder.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
# M15: the order in which active_locks.json lists the IDs of a claimed range differs from process to process
echo "##### M15: the same plan validated in six fresh projects -- the order of the IDs that active_locks.json stores"
ORDERS=""
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  newproj lockorder; printf 'one\ntwo\nthree\nfour\nfive\n' > f.txt
  F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
  quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00004 --payload-text 'X'
  quiet validate-plan batch_0001
  O=$(python3 -I -c 'import json;ids=json.load(open(".operational-platform/active_locks.json"))["batches"]["batch_0001"][0]["ids"];print(" ".join(x.split("_l")[1] for x in ids))')
  echo "run $i: $O"
  ORDERS="$ORDERS$O;"
done
python3 -I -c '
import sys
o = sys.argv[1].strip(";").split(";")
print("every run wrote the same four IDs:", all(sorted(x.split()) == ["00001", "00002", "00003", "00004"] for x in o))
print("all six runs wrote the same order:", len(set(o)) == 1)' "$ORDERS"
```
