#### `sc_more.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
jq_() { python3 -I -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(json.dumps(d,indent=None,ensure_ascii=False))"; }
r1() { echo "\$ cli.py $*"; python3 -I "$CLI" "$@" 2>&1 | jq_ 2>/dev/null || true; }   # compact one-line JSON

echo; echo "##### 1: inverted range at validate-plan"
newproj k1; printf 'a\nb\nc\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text z
run validate-plan batch_0001

echo "##### 2: register --force after the file changed outside, with an open descriptor"
newproj k2; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\nL4\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --payload-text 'L3-new'
printf 'NEWTOP\nL1\nL2\nL3\nL4\n' > f.txt
r1 register f.txt --force
r1 validate-plan batch_0001
r1 apply-next batch_0001
show f.txt

echo "##### 3: invariants: multiple matches per line, ^ anchoring, comments, balanced_pairs"
newproj k3; printf '# foo foo\nx = foo(1) + foo(2)\ny = (a[1]\n' > f.py; F=$(fid f.py); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.py --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --payload-text 'y = (a[1])'
quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001
r1 add-invariant batch_0001 --file f.py --pattern 'foo' --expected-count 0
r1 add-invariant batch_0001 --file f.py --pattern 'foo' --expected-count 0 --exclude-comments --description "excluding whole-line comments"
r1 add-invariant batch_0001 --file f.py --pattern '^x' --expected-count 1 --description "anchored without (?m)"
r1 add-invariant batch_0001 --file f.py --pattern '(?m)^[xy]' --expected-count 2 --description "anchored with (?m)"
r1 add-invariant batch_0001 --file f.py --pattern '()[]{}' --type balanced_pairs --expected-count 0 --description "brackets balance"
python3 -I "$CLI" validate-post batch_0001 | python3 -I -c '
import sys,json
d=json.load(sys.stdin); print("result:",d["result"]); print("syntax:",list(d["syntax"].values()))
for i in d["invariants"]: print({k:i[k] for k in i if k in ("type","pattern","expected","actual","raw_matches_before_exceptions","result","detail","description")}, "matches:", i.get("matches"))'

echo; echo "##### 4: python syntax failure and unknown extension in validate-post"
newproj k4; printf 'x = 1\ny = 2\n' > ok.py; printf 'a\nb\n' > notes.md; F=$(fid ok.py); G=$(fid notes.md); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file ok.py --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text 'y = = 2'
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file notes.md --start ${G}_l00001 --end ${G}_l00001 --payload-text 'A'
quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001
python3 -I "$CLI" validate-post batch_0001 | python3 -I -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(json.dumps({"result":d["result"],"syntax":{k.split("/")[-1]:v for k,v in d["syntax"].items()}},indent=1))'
r1 status batch_0001

echo "##### 5: require-file gate"
newproj k5; printf 'a\n' > f.txt; quiet register f.txt; quiet new-batch
r1 require-file batch_0001 spec/the-standard.md
r1 validate-plan batch_0001
mkdir spec; printf 'the standard\n' > spec/the-standard.md; quiet register spec/the-standard.md
r1 validate-plan batch_0001

echo "##### 6: project-level category / constraint inheritance"
newproj k6; printf 'a\nb\nc\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch; quiet new-batch
r1 add-category batch_0001 --code SEC --description "security finding" --project
quiet add-descriptor batch_0002 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text 'A' --category SEC
r1 validate-plan batch_0002
quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0003 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text 'B'
r1 validate-plan batch_0003
r1 add-constraint batch_0003 --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003 --reason "project-wide freeze" --project
quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0004 --op delete_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003
r1 validate-plan batch_0004
cat .operational-platform/project_taxonomy.json .operational-platform/project_constraints.json | python3 -I -c 'import sys;print(sys.stdin.read().replace("\n","")[:400])'

echo; echo "##### 7: other shape gates"
newproj k7; printf 'a\n' > f.txt; quiet register f.txt
quiet new-batch --shape transition; r1 validate-plan batch_0001
quiet new-batch --shape rename;     r1 validate-plan batch_0002
quiet new-batch --shape conformance; r1 validate-plan batch_0003
r1 sync-domino-queue batch_0002
r1 validate-plan batch_0002
r1 new-batch --shape bogus

echo; echo "##### 8: template: two hits per line, two files, --file filter"
newproj k8; printf 'foo foo bar\n  indented foo\nnothing\n' > a.txt; printf 'foo\n' > b.txt; quiet register a.txt; quiet register b.txt; quiet new-batch
r1 add-descriptor-template batch_0001 --find foo --replace BAZ --file a.txt
quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001; show a.txt; show b.txt

echo "##### 9: domino hint is a REGEX; short lines are ignored"
newproj k9; printf 'x = f(1)\n}\nend\nlonger line here\n' > a.txt; printf 'f(1)\n}\nend\nlonger line here\n' > b.txt
FA=$(fid a.txt); quiet register b.txt; quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${FA}_l00001 --end ${FA}_l00001 --payload-text 'x = g(1)' --domino-hint 'f('
quiet sync-domino-queue batch_0001
r1 domino-next batch_0001
newproj k9b; printf '}\nend\nlonger line here\n' > a.txt; printf '}\nend\nlonger line here\n' > b.txt
FA=$(fid a.txt); quiet register b.txt; quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op delete_range --file a.txt --start ${FA}_l00001 --end ${FA}_l00003
quiet sync-domino-queue batch_0001
r1 domino-next batch_0001

echo; echo "##### 10: resume in each state"
newproj k10; printf 'a\nb\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text 'A'
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text 'B'
r1 resume
quiet validate-plan batch_0001;  r1 resume
quiet apply-next batch_0001;     r1 resume
r1 checkpoint
quiet apply-next batch_0001;     r1 resume
r1 apply-next batch_0001
quiet validate-post batch_0001;  r1 resume
```

#### `sc_movedest.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
r1() { echo "\$ cli.py $*"; python3 -I "$CLI" "$@" 2>&1 | python3 -I -c "import sys,json;print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin),ensure_ascii=False))" 2>/dev/null || true; }
reg() { python3 -I - <<PY
import json
r=json.load(open('.operational-platform/registry.json'))
for fid,e in r['files'].items():
    live=sorted((p,l.split('_')[-1]) for l,p in e['lines'].items() if p is not None)
    print('  registry:', [(p,l) for p,l in live], 'next_seq', e['next_seq'])
PY
}
for CASE in "dest=start:2:2:2" "dest=end:2:3:3" "dest=inside:2:4:3"; do
  NAME=${CASE%%:*}; REST=${CASE#*:}; S_=${REST%%:*}; REST=${REST#*:}; E_=${REST%%:*}; D_=${REST#*:}
  echo "##### MD: move_range L${S_}..L${E_} with dest L${D_} ($NAME)"
  newproj md_$NAME; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\nL4\nL5\n' > f.txt; F=$(fid f.txt); quiet new-batch
  quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op move_range --file f.txt --start ${F}_l0000${S_} --end ${F}_l0000${E_} --dest ${F}_l0000${D_}
  r1 validate-plan batch_0001
  r1 apply-next batch_0001
  echo "  file now: $(tr '\n' ' ' < f.txt)"
  reg
  r1 status batch_0001
  r1 validate-plan batch_0001
  r1 check batch_0001 d0001
  tail -2 .operational-platform/wal.jsonl
  echo
done
```

#### `sc_moves.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
mk() { newproj "$1"; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\nL4\nL5\nL6\n' > list.txt; F=$(fid list.txt); B=batch_0001; quiet new-batch; }
ad() { quiet add-descriptor $B --file list.txt "$@"; }
go() { quiet validate-plan $B; python3 -I "$CLI" apply-all $B | python3 -I -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print([r["result"] for r in d["applied"]])'; echo "result:"; tr '\n' ' ' < list.txt; echo; echo; }

mk m1; echo "##### move_range L2..L3 after L5 (later in file)"
ad --op move_range --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00003 --dest ${F}_l00005; go
run show-file list.txt | python3 -I -c 'import sys,json
t=sys.stdin.read(); j=t[t.index("{"):t.rindex("}")+1]; d=json.loads(j)
print([(l["line_id"][-6:], l["pos"], l["text"]) for l in d["lines"]])'

mk m2; echo "##### move_range L5..L6 after L1 (earlier in file)"
ad --op move_range --start ${F}_l00005 --end ${F}_l00006 --dest ${F}_l00001; go

mk m3; echo "##### move_range L3..L4 to START"
ad --op move_range --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00004 --dest START; go

mk m4; echo "##### copy_range L1..L2 after L4"
ad --op copy_range --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00002 --dest ${F}_l00004; go

mk m5; echo "##### delete_range L2..L3"
ad --op delete_range --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00003; go

mk m6; echo "##### insert_after START (2 lines) and after last line"
ad --op insert_after --after START --payload-text $'top1\ntop2'
ad --op insert_after --after ${F}_l00006 --payload-text 'bottom'
go

mk m7; echo "##### two inserts at START (no conflict flagged?) in insertion order"
ad --op insert_after --after START --payload-text 'first-added'
ad --op insert_after --after START --payload-text 'second-added'
run validate-plan $B | head -12
python3 -I "$CLI" apply-all $B >/dev/null; tr '\n' ' ' < list.txt; echo; echo

mk m8; echo "##### two inserts after the SAME anchor, ordered with depends-on"
ad --op insert_after --after ${F}_l00003 --payload-text 'ins-A'
ad --op insert_after --after ${F}_l00003 --payload-text 'ins-B' --depends-on d0001
run validate-plan $B | head -12
python3 -I "$CLI" apply-all $B >/dev/null; tr '\n' ' ' < list.txt; echo; echo

mk m9; echo "##### move into a protected zone (dest is not checked)?"
quiet add-constraint $B --file list.txt --start ${F}_l00004 --end ${F}_l00005 --reason "protected L4..L5"
ad --op move_range --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --dest ${F}_l00004
run validate-plan $B | head -12
python3 -I "$CLI" apply-all $B >/dev/null; tr '\n' ' ' < list.txt; echo; echo

mk m10; echo "##### delete L3 and move L1 after L3 in the same batch (dest not conflict-checked)"
ad --op delete_range --start ${F}_l00003 --end ${F}_l00003
ad --op move_range --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --dest ${F}_l00003
run validate-plan $B | head -12
run apply-all $B
tr '\n' ' ' < list.txt; echo
```

#### `sc_release_lock.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
RL=$S/scripts/release_lock.py; AU=$S/scripts/state_audit.py
r1() { echo "\$ cli.py $*"; python3 -I "$CLI" "$@" 2>&1 | python3 -I -c "import sys,json;print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin),ensure_ascii=False))" 2>/dev/null || true; echo "[exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}]"; }
rl() { echo "\$ release_lock.py $*"; python3 -I "$RL" "$P" "$@"; echo "[exit=$?]"; echo; }
au() { echo "\$ state_audit.py"; python3 -I "$AU" "$P" | cut -c1-260; echo "[exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}]"; echo; }
newproj release; P=$PWD
printf 'def old_name(x):\n    return x + 1\n\nprint(old_name(1))\n' > app.py
F=$(fid app.py); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file app.py --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-text 'def new_name(x):'
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file app.py --start ${F}_l00004 --end ${F}_l00004 --payload-text 'print(new_name(1))'
quiet validate-plan batch_0001
quiet apply-next batch_0001
sed -i 's/old_name(1)/old_name(999)/' app.py        # somebody edits line 4 outside the tool
r1 apply-next batch_0001
echo "##### RL1: the state before the release"
au
quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0002 --op replace_range --file app.py --start ${F}_l00004 --end ${F}_l00004 --payload-text 'print(new_name(999))'
r1 validate-plan batch_0002
echo "##### RL2: refusals and a report"
rl batch_0009
rl ../x
rl batch_0001
rm -rf "$S/projects/release_before"; cp -a "$P" "$S/projects/release_before"       # snapshot for the auditor samples
echo "##### RL3: release, then re-plan"
rl batch_0001 --yes
cat .operational-platform/active_locks.json | python3 -I -c "import sys,json;print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin)))"
r1 validate-plan batch_0002
r1 apply-all batch_0002
r1 validate-post batch_0002
echo "##### RL4: the state afterwards"
au
cat app.py
```

#### `sc_rename.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
r1() { echo "\$ cli.py $*"; python3 -I "$CLI" "$@" 2>&1 | python3 -I -c "import sys,json;print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin),ensure_ascii=False))" 2>/dev/null || true; echo "[exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}]"; }
newproj rename
printf 'def old_name(x):\n    return x + 1\n\nprint(old_name(1))\n' > app.py
printf 'from app import old_name\ny = old_name(5)\n' > util.py
echo "##### R0: the two files"; show app.py; show util.py
echo "##### R1: register"
r1 register app.py
r1 register util.py
echo "##### R2: show-file"

echo "##### R3: open a rename-shaped batch; one descriptor per matching line"

r1 add-descriptor-template batch_0001 --find old_name --replace new_name
echo "##### R4: validate-plan BEFORE any tracing (shape gate)"

echo "##### R5: queue the findings and try again (domino gate)"
r1 sync-domino-queue batch_0001
r1 validate-plan batch_0001
echo "##### R6: trace each finding"

python3 -I "$CLI" dry-run batch_0001 --file app.py; echo "[exit=$?]"
r1 apply-next batch_0001
r1 resume
r1 apply-all batch_0001
echo "##### R9: result on disk"; show app.py; show util.py
r1 validate-post batch_0001
r1 status batch_0001
r1 report --batches batch_0001
```

#### `sc_tour.sh`

```bash

lid() { python3 -I "$CLI" show-file "$1" | python3 -I -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print([l["line_id"] for l in d["lines"] if l["pos"]=='"$2"'][0])'; }

newproj tour

import os

def old_name(x):

print(old_name(1))
PY
cat > notes.md <<'MD'
# Notes
Call old_name() to compute.
## Usage
Use old_name(2) in loops.
## Legacy
old_name was introduced in v1.
MD

echo "################ BATCH 1: a rename (shape rename), exercising categories, constraints, domino, invariants"
run register app.py
run register notes.md
run show-file app.py
A=$(fid app.py); N=$(fid notes.md)
run new-batch --shape rename
run add-category batch_0001 --code NAMING --description "identifier renames"
run add-category batch_0001 --code STYLE --description "style findings"
run add-category batch_0001 --code DOCS --description "documentation mentions" --project
run close-category batch_0001 --code STYLE --note "no style findings in scope"
run set-category-scope batch_0001 --code DOCS --files notes.md,app.py
run close-category-file batch_0001 --code DOCS --file app.py --note "no docs inside code"
run require-file batch_0001 notes.md
run add-constraint batch_0001 --file app.py --start ${A}_l00001 --end ${A}_l00001 --reason "imports frozen"
run add-constraint batch_0001 --file notes.md --start ${N}_l00005 --end ${N}_l00006 --reason "legacy section frozen" --project

run add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file app.py --start ${A}_l00003 --end ${A}_l00003 --payload-text 'def new_name(x):' --category NAMING --severity major --context 'old_name' --rule-ref 'S3.1' --domino-hint old_name
run validate-plan batch_0001
run sync-domino-queue batch_0001
run domino-status batch_0001
run domino-next batch_0001
run add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file app.py --start ${A}_l00006 --end ${A}_l00006 --payload-text 'print(new_name(1))' --category NAMING --severity major --provenance domino --domino-of d0001
run add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file notes.md --start ${N}_l00002 --end ${N}_l00002 --payload-text 'Call new_name() to compute.' --category DOCS --severity minor --provenance domino --domino-of d0001
run add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file notes.md --start ${N}_l00004 --end ${N}_l00004 --payload-text 'Use new_name(2) in loops.' --category DOCS --severity minor --provenance domino --domino-of d0001
run domino-resolve batch_0001 dm0001
run domino-status batch_0001

run add-invariant batch_0001 --file app.py --pattern old_name --expected-count 0 --description "no old name in code" --checked-against app.py --severity critical
run add-invariant batch_0001 --file app.py --pattern '()' --expected-count 0 --type balanced_pairs --description "parentheses balanced"
run add-invariant batch_0001 --file notes.md --pattern old_name --expected-count 0 --description "only the frozen legacy line may keep it" --checked-against notes.md --severity minor

run validate-plan batch_0001
run check batch_0001 d0001
run explain batch_0001 d0001
run dry-run batch_0001 --file notes.md
run find-pattern --pattern old_name
run status batch_0001 --group-by file_id,category
run apply-next batch_0001
run apply-all batch_0001
run validate-post batch_0001
run accept-match batch_0001 --file notes.md --pattern old_name --line 6 --note "frozen legacy line"
run validate-post batch_0001
run status batch_0001
run report --batches batch_0001
run checkpoint
run resume

echo "################ BATCH 2: an assembly (shape assembly), inventory, cross-file copy, undo"
printf '# Combined\n\n' > out.md
run register out.md
run new-batch --shape assembly
run add-source-range batch_0002 --file notes.md --start $(lid notes.md 1) --end $(lid notes.md 2)
run add-source-range batch_0002 --file notes.md --start $(lid notes.md 3) --end $(lid notes.md 4)
run add-source-range batch_0002 --file notes.md --start $(lid notes.md 5) --end $(lid notes.md 6)
run inventory-status batch_0002
run inventory-next batch_0002
run copy-across-files batch_0002 --src-file notes.md --start $(lid notes.md 3) --end $(lid notes.md 4) --dest-file out.md --dest-after $(lid out.md 2)
run inventory-resolve batch_0002 ri0001 --disposition excluded --note "title and intro not needed"
run inventory-resolve batch_0002 ri0002 --disposition transferred_verbatim --descriptor-ids d0001 --note "copied as is"
run inventory-resolve batch_0002 ri0003 --disposition excluded --note "legacy section dropped"
run inventory-status batch_0002
run validate-plan batch_0002
run close-category batch_0002 --code DOCS --note "documentation category does not apply to an assembly"
run validate-plan batch_0002
run apply-all batch_0002
run validate-post batch_0002
show out.md
run undo-descriptor batch_0002 d0001
show out.md
run status batch_0002

echo "################ BATCH 3: the other ops, template, cross-file move; then export/import"
printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\nL4\nL5\nL6\nL7\nL8\n' > list.txt
printf 'X1\nX2\n' > other.txt
run register list.txt
run register other.txt
rm -rf "$S/projects/tour_dest" "$S/projects/tour_dest2"; cp -r "$S/projects/tour" "$S/projects/tour_dest"; cp -r "$S/projects/tour" "$S/projects/tour_dest2"
run new-batch
run add-descriptor batch_0003 --op move_range --file list.txt --start $(lid list.txt 2) --end $(lid list.txt 3) --dest $(lid list.txt 5)
run add-descriptor batch_0003 --op copy_range --file list.txt --start $(lid list.txt 1) --end $(lid list.txt 1) --dest $(lid list.txt 6)
run add-descriptor batch_0003 --op delete_range --file list.txt --start $(lid list.txt 4) --end $(lid list.txt 4)
run add-descriptor batch_0003 --op insert_after --file list.txt --after START --payload-text top
run add-descriptor-template batch_0003 --find X1 --replace Y1 --file other.txt
run move-across-files batch_0003 --src-file list.txt --start $(lid list.txt 8) --end $(lid list.txt 8) --dest-file other.txt --dest-after $(lid other.txt 2)
run validate-plan batch_0003
run close-category batch_0003 --code DOCS --note "not relevant here"
run validate-plan batch_0003
run export-batch batch_0003 --out "$S/projects/tour_exp_unapplied.tar.gz"
run dry-run batch_0003 --file list.txt
run apply-all batch_0003
run validate-post batch_0003
show list.txt
show other.txt
run export-batch batch_0003 --out "$S/projects/tour_exp_applied.tar.gz"

echo "################ destination 1: import the export made BEFORE applying, then apply there"
cd "$S/projects/tour_dest"
run import-batch "$S/projects/tour_exp_unapplied.tar.gz"
run status batch_0003
run validate-plan batch_0003
run apply-all batch_0003
run validate-post batch_0003
show list.txt
show other.txt

echo "################ destination 2: import the export made AFTER applying"
cd "$S/projects/tour_dest2"
run import-batch "$S/projects/tour_exp_applied.tar.gz"
run status batch_0003
run validate-plan batch_0003
show list.txt
show other.txt
```

#### `sc_trust.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
echo "##### T1: batch id is used as a path component, unvalidated"
newproj t1; printf 'a\n' > a.txt; quiet register a.txt
mkdir -p sub
echo "-- project root before:"; ls -A
run status ../../probe1
echo "-- project root after (probe1 is a sibling of .operational-platform, i.e. OUTSIDE the state directory):"; ls -A
run add-invariant ../../probe2 --file a.txt --pattern x --expected-count 1
echo "-- what was written outside the state dir:"; ls -A probe2; echo
echo "##### T2: a managed path outside the project root"
newproj t2; mkdir -p ../t2_outside; printf 'x\ny\n' > ../t2_outside/o.txt
run register ../t2_outside/o.txt
run register "$S/projects/t2_outside/o.txt"
echo "##### T3: --payload-file reads any path the user can read"
newproj t3; printf 'a\nb\n' > a.txt; F=$(fid a.txt); quiet new-batch
printf 'from-elsewhere\n' > ../t3_payload.txt
run add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${F}_l00001 --end ${F}_l00001 --payload-file ../t3_payload.txt
```

#### `sc_undo.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
newproj undo
printf 'alpha\nbeta\ngamma\ndelta\nepsilon\n' > notes.txt
F=$(fid notes.txt); B=batch_0001
run new-batch
run add-descriptor $B --op replace_range --file notes.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text 'BETA'
run validate-plan $B
run apply-next $B
show notes.txt
run undo-descriptor $B d0001
show notes.txt
run status $B
echo "##### documented 'redo': apply-next after undo"
run apply-next $B
show notes.txt
run status $B
run validate-post $B
```

#### `sc_undo2.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
r1() { echo "\$ cli.py $*"; python3 -I "$CLI" "$@" 2>&1 | python3 -I -c "import sys,json;print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin),ensure_ascii=False))" 2>/dev/null || true; }
echo "##### UP: what happens to validate-plan after undoing a replace_range?"
newproj undo_plan; printf 'alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n' > n.txt; F=$(fid n.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file n.txt --start ${F}_l00002 --end ${F}_l00002 --payload-text 'BETA'
quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001; quiet undo-descriptor batch_0001 d0001
r1 validate-plan batch_0001
echo "-- add a NEW descriptor against the restored line's NEW id, then validate again"
r1 show-file n.txt
```

```bash
quiet require-file batch_0001 nosuch.txt

quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001
```

#### `sc_v20.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
echo "##### A: descriptor added AFTER the last sync-domino-queue is not gated"
newproj v20a; printf 'alpha foo\nbeta\ngamma foo\n' > a.txt; printf 'zzz foo zzz\n' > b.txt
FA=$(fid a.txt); FB=$(fid b.txt); quiet new-batch --shape rename
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${FA}_l00001 --end ${FA}_l00001 --payload-text 'alpha bar' --domino-hint foo
run sync-domino-queue batch_0001
run domino-next batch_0001
run domino-resolve batch_0001 dm0001
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${FA}_l00003 --end ${FA}_l00003 --payload-text 'gamma bar' --domino-hint foo
run domino-status batch_0001
run validate-plan batch_0001
run status batch_0001

echo; echo "##### B: invalid regex in --domino-hint: can the finding still be resolved?"
newproj v20b; printf 'call foo(1)\nother\n' > a.txt; FA=$(fid a.txt); quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file a.txt --start ${FA}_l00001 --end ${FA}_l00001 --payload-text 'call bar(1)' --domino-hint 'foo('
run sync-domino-queue batch_0001
run domino-next batch_0001
run domino-resolve batch_0001 dm0001
run domino-status batch_0001
run validate-plan batch_0001

echo; echo "##### C: copy_range with --dest START"
newproj v20c; printf 'L1\nL2\nL3\n' > a.txt; FA=$(fid a.txt); quiet new-batch
run add-descriptor batch_0001 --op copy_range --file a.txt --start ${FA}_l00002 --end ${FA}_l00002 --dest START
run validate-plan batch_0001
run apply-next batch_0001
show a.txt
run status batch_0001
cat .operational-platform/wal.jsonl | tail -3

echo; echo "##### D: unknown / mistyped batch id creates a phantom directory"
newproj v20d; printf 'x\n' > a.txt; quiet register a.txt; quiet new-batch
ls .operational-platform/batches
run status batch_0007
ls .operational-platform/batches
run new-batch
ls .operational-platform/batches

echo; echo "##### E: an empty batch passes both validations and is committed"
newproj v20e; printf 'x\n' > a.txt; quiet register a.txt; quiet new-batch
run validate-plan batch_0001
run apply-all batch_0001
run apply-next batch_0001
run validate-post batch_0001
run status batch_0001
run resume

echo; echo "##### F: check on unknown descriptor id; explain on unknown"
run check batch_0001 d0042
run explain batch_0001 d0042
```

#### `sc_v3b.sh`

```bash
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
echo "##### V3b: a stale second registration lets an insert land one line early when anchor texts coincide"
newproj v3b; printf 'x\n}\n}\ny\n' > app.py
A=$(fid app.py); B=$(fid ./app.py)
echo "A=$A  B=$B"
quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0001 --op replace_range --file app.py --start ${A}_l00001 --end ${A}_l00001 --payload-text $'x1\nx2'
quiet validate-plan batch_0001; quiet apply-all batch_0001
show app.py
echo "-- now a second batch through the OTHER spelling: insert after the SECOND '}' (./app.py line 3)"
quiet new-batch
quiet add-descriptor batch_0002 --op insert_after --file ./app.py --after ${B}_l00003 --payload-text 'AFTER-SECOND-BRACE'
run validate-plan batch_0002
run apply-all batch_0002
show app.py
```

### D.12 The reference tour

The complete transcript of `sc_tour.sh` — the run from which the samples of [Part VII](#part-vii--state-file-formats) and of several worked examples were taken. Three batches over five small files: a rename, an assembly with an undo, and a mixed batch of the other operations; then the export of a batch and its import into two projects, one before and one after the batch was applied. Paths are shortened as everywhere in this guide; the line `[exit=N]` after each command is the real exit status.

## Appendix E — Glossary

The words of this guide in alphabetical order, each with the section that explains it. A term in *italics* inside a definition has its own entry. The reference labels used throughout — V1, S1, L1, BP1 and the rest — are explained at the end.

| Term | Meaning | See |
|---|---|---|
| **abort** | The result that `apply-next` and `apply-all` print when the live text matches neither the *expect_hash* of the descriptor nor a plausible post-state, or when its target no longer exists. The file is untouched by that call, the exit status is 1, and the right response is not a retry but a new *batch*. | [§50.22](#5022-apply-next-and-apply-all), [§59.3](#593-abandoning-a-batch) |
| **accepted match** | A surviving match of an *invariant* that a reviewer has declared legitimate with `accept-match`. Kept by line number with a note; subtracted from the invariant's actual count at `validate-post`, yet still listed there, marked `accepted`. | [§29.4](#294-reviewed-exceptions-accept-match) |
| **anchor** | The line that an `insert_after` descriptor inserts after (`--after`). The *expect_hash* of an insert covers only the anchor's text. `START` is the anchor for "the top of the file". | [§24.2](#242-the-five-operations) |
| **apply order** | `apply_order`: the list of descriptor IDs that a passing `validate-plan` writes into the batch — a topological order of the declared dependencies, ties broken by severity and then by insertion order. Only descriptors that were **not applied** at that moment are in it. | [§45.5](#455-the-topological-order) |
| **audit trail** | The three records the tool keeps of what it did: the *WAL*, the validation log and the *checkpoint*. None is tamper-evident, and none is `fsync`ed. | [§34](#34-the-audit-trail-wal-validation-log-and-checkpoint) |
| **batch** | A numbered set of related edits (`batch_0001` …) with its own directory of state files, a status (*planning*, *validated*, *committed*, *failed*) and, optionally, a *shape*. The unit of planning, validation and locking. | [§26](#26-batches-and-their-lifecycle) |
| **blob** | A *payload* stored as a file named by the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its text. Identical texts share one blob; blobs are never deleted and never re-hashed on read. | [§25.2](#252-payload-storage), [§53.2](#532-payloadshashblob) |
| **candidate** | A line that the domino search found still holding the old content (or matching the `--domino-hint`) and that no descriptor covers yet. A search result, not a verdict: a dependency that shares no text with the old content never shows up. | [§30.4](#304-how-the-candidate-search-works) |
| **category** | A code in the *taxonomy* under which a descriptor is classified. It must be declared before a descriptor can use it, and every declared category must be used or closed before the plan passes. | [§27](#27-taxonomy-categories-and-severity) |
| **census** | The program `schema_census.py`: it reads every state file of every *fixture* and checks each record against the schema of Part VII and reports the required keys that are missing, the keys that no list names, the optional keys that are present, and the values that are outside the documented vocabulary. | [D.7](#d7-mechanical-checks) |
| **checkpoint** | `checkpoint.json`: one small object saying where the last change of phase stood — active batch, counts, the cause of the last interruption. Read by `resume`; it follows the last batch that *changed phase*, not the last one opened (V15). | [§34.3](#343-the-checkpoint) |
| **committed** | The status that a passing `validate-post` gives a batch: every descriptor applied, syntax and invariants hold, locks released. Not terminal — a later `validate-plan` can return the batch to *validated*. | [§26.2](#262-states) |
| **compare-and-swap** | The check before every write: the hash of the live text of the target must equal the descriptor's *expect_hash*, or nothing is written. Strong for replace, delete and move; for an insert it covers only the *anchor*. | [§25.3](#253-the-compare-and-swap-at-apply-time) |
| **conflict** | Two descriptors of one batch that claim overlapping lines with no declared order between them. `validate-plan` fails with `conflicts`; `--depends-on` states the order, and a declared order is obeyed, not judged. | [§39.2](#392-conflicts--and-why-a-declared-order-is-obeyed-not-judged) |
| **constraint** | A *protected range*: lines, given as two line IDs, that no descriptor may target. Declared per batch or — permanently — per project. | [§28](#28-constraints-and-protected-zones) |
| **context** | The optional `--context` of a descriptor: at most 120 characters that must be a substring of the live text at the target. Checked once, at add time; its purpose is to catch an ID that points at the wrong line (BP18). | [§24.5](#245-what-is-checked-and-when) |
| **contract** | In Part IX: the rule that says, for every command, what to read in the reply, when the caller may go on and when it must stop. | [§60.2](#602-the-contract-what-to-parse-when-to-continue-when-to-stop) |
| **crash window** | One of three points inside a single apply where a process can die: **A** — the file is written, the registry is not saved; **B** — the registry is saved, the WAL record `op_applied` is not; **C** — the WAL record is written, the status is not. | [§48.2](#482-the-crash-harness), [§48.3](#483-the-verified-results) |
| **descriptor** | One planned edit: an operation, its target as line IDs, the text, the hash it expects, and optionally category, severity, dependencies and *provenance*. Append-only — no command edits or removes one. | [§24](#24-descriptors-the-five-operations) |
| **direct / domino** | The two values of *provenance*. A `direct` descriptor comes from the analysis itself; a `domino` descriptor was found *because* of another finding and names it in `domino_of`. | [§24.3](#243-the-three-provenance-related-fields) |
| **disposition** | What became of a declared source range in the *inventory*: `transferred_verbatim`, `transferred_with_edit` or `excluded`. | [§31](#31-the-region-inventory) |
| **domino** | The cascade search. For every direct finding: look for other places that depend on the same text, add a descriptor for each real one, and close the finding. Implemented by the domino queue (`sync-domino-queue`, `domino-next`, `domino-resolve`, `domino-status`). | [§30](#30-the-domino-queue) |
| **expect_hash** | The 12-hex-digit hash of the text a descriptor was planned against — for an insert its *anchor line*, for a copy the source range. The left-hand side of the *compare-and-swap*. | [§25.1](#251-the-two-hashes) |
| **failed** | The status that a `validate-post` gives a batch when a syntax check or an invariant does not pass. The locks are released all the same, and a later `validate-post` can still make the batch *committed*. | [§26.2](#262-states) |
| **file ID** | `f_` + 10 hex digits: the SHA-256 of the path **as typed** at registration. The permanent identity of a *managed file* — and the reason `./a.py` and `a.py` are two files (V3). | [§22.1](#221-file-identity) |
| **finding** | In the domino queue, one entry (`dm0001` …) for a direct descriptor that has to be traced; in the methodology, anything the analysis found that needs a change. | [§30.2](#302-queue-entries) |
| **fixture** | A throwaway project that a *scenario script* or the crash harness leaves behind, with its state directory, so that the *census* and the auditor's sweep can read it. | [D.3](#d3-the-scenarios) |
| **gate** | A check of `validate-plan` that fails the plan unless a mechanism that was declared — a taxonomy, a domino queue, an inventory, required materials, a shape — was used. Eleven in all, run in a fixed order, stopping at the first failure. | [§32.2](#322-all-gates-in-the-order-validate-plan-runs-them) |
| **guard** | `asm_guard.py`, the wrapper written for this guide: it serializes the calls on a project and refuses command lines that the tool would accept and regret. | [§60.3](#603-the-guard-wrapper) |
| **idempotency key** | The WAL record by which a repeated command recognizes that its work was done: `op_applied` for `apply-*`, `domino_traced` for `domino-resolve`. | [§53.13](#5313-waljsonl), [§48.4](#484-what-recovered-proves--and-what-it-does-not) |
| **inventory** | The region inventory: declared source ranges (`ri0001` …), each of which must be given a *disposition* before the plan can pass. The mechanism of the `assembly` *shape*. | [§31](#31-the-region-inventory) |
| **invariant** | A post-condition checked at `validate-post`, independent of the descriptors: a regular expression whose count over a file's **whole text** must equal `expected_count`, or a check that bracket pairs balance. | [§29](#29-invariants-and-accepted-matches) |
| **line** | Whatever `str.splitlines()` finds in the UTF-8 text of a file. A file is rewritten as its lines joined with one line ending, plus a final one (V7). | [§22.5](#225-what-a-line-is) |
| **line ID** | `<file ID>_l` + 5 digits: the permanent identity of one line, minted at registration or by an insert, replace or copy, and never reused. | [§22.2](#222-line-identity) |
| **lock** | An entry of `active_locks.json`: the line IDs that a *validated*, unfinished batch claims. A batch whose plan overlaps them fails with `cross_batch_conflicts`. Released only by `validate-post`; an abandoned batch keeps its lock (V21). | [§33](#33-cross-batch-locks) |
| **managed file** | A file under the project root that has been registered and that the tool may rewrite. Its bytes change only through `apply-next`, `apply-all` and `undo-descriptor`. | [§22](#22-files-and-lines-identity-that-never-changes) |
| **methodology** | The six-phase method of the Operational Platform — context loading, analysis, task map, execution plan, execution, validation — of which `operational-platform` is an implementation for one domain. | [Part II](#part-ii--the-methodology) |
| **negative control** | A check that a test *can* fail. For an invariant with `expected_count 0`: a pattern that does match in the pre-state, so that a regex which never matches is noticed (BP21). | [§29.5](#295-the-independence-warnings) |
| **normalized** | In the *reproduction check*: a text in which the values that differ from run to run by design — the root directory, the time stamps that the tool writes, the dates of `ls -l` — have been replaced by a fixed word, so that two runs can be compared. | [D.3](#d3-the-scenarios) |
| **payload** | The new text of an insert or replace — or the snapshot of the source of a copy — stored as a *blob* and referenced by `payload_ref`. | [§24.4](#244-payload-text-and-newlines) |
| **phantom** | Something empty that the tool creates without being asked: a `batches/<id>/` directory for a batch ID that does not exist (V13), or the registration of a path that does not exist (V19). | [§56](#56-verified-behaviors-and-deviations-from-the-documentation) |
| **planning** | The status of a batch that has not passed `validate-plan`. Descriptors may be added; nothing is claimed; nothing may be applied. | [§26.2](#262-states) |
| **project root** | The directory that holds `.operational-platform/`, found by walking up from the current directory; if there is none, the current directory becomes the root. | [§43.1](#431-root-discovery-and-the-state-directory) |
| **protected range** | See *constraint*. | [§28](#28-constraints-and-protected-zones) |
| **provenance** | `direct` or `domino`; see *direct / domino*. | [§24.3](#243-the-three-provenance-related-fields) |
| **recovered** | The result of `apply-*` (and of `domino-resolve`) that means "the log, or the live content, says this was already done, and the bookkeeping has been brought up to date". After a crash it is usually true; after an `undo` it is false (V1). This guide's contract says: stop and look. | [§48.4](#484-what-recovered-proves--and-what-it-does-not) |
| **registry** | `registry.json`: the map from line IDs to positions for every registered file, with `next_seq` and the line ending. | [§23](#23-the-registry) |
| **reproduction check** | `repro_check.py`: it runs every *scenario script* again, in a new directory, and compares what each prints with the *transcript* that this guide quotes, after the values that differ by design have been *normalized*. | [D.3](#d3-the-scenarios) |
| **rule_ref** | An optional free-text pointer from a descriptor to the clause that governs it. Used only by a noisy spelling-drift warning (V28). | [§24.1](#241-anatomy) |
| **scenario** | One numbered experiment on the tool, announced in a *transcript* by a line `##### CODE: title` (`C1`, `GD3`, `V20` …). The code is the label that the guide uses to refer to it. | [D.3](#d3-the-scenarios) |
| **scenario script** | A shell script (`sc_NAME.sh`) that sets up a *fixture*, runs the tool's commands and prints the replies; it holds one or more *scenarios*. All 42 are printed in full. | [D.11](#d11-the-scenario-scripts) |
| **severity** | The optional `critical` > `major` > `minor` > `cosmetic` on a descriptor or an invariant. Changes tie-breaking in the *apply order* and the counts of `report`, nothing else. | [§27.4](#274-severity) |
| **shape** | One of five declared kinds of job — `conformance`, `audit`, `transition`, `rename`, `assembly` — that commits a batch to using the mechanism it cannot responsibly skip. | [§32.1](#321-declaring-a-shape) |
| **skill** | The packaging of `operational-platform` as an installable Claude skill: `SKILL.md`, reference documents and the scripts. | [§2](#2-what-is-in-the-archive) |
| **START** | The literal anchor meaning "the top of the file": valid for `--after` and for the `--dest` of a move. Never hash-checked, never claimed by the plan (V17). | [§24.2](#242-the-five-operations) |
| **state directory** | `.operational-platform/`: everything the tool knows, as JSON files, JSON-lines files and text blobs. | [§52](#52-the-state-directory) |
| **syntax check** | Part of `validate-post`: `.py` files are compiled, `.js` files go through `node --check` if Node.js is installed (V10). | [§45.9](#459-validate_post) |
| **taxonomy** | The categories declared for a batch together with those of the project; the batch entry wins on a clash. | [§27](#27-taxonomy-categories-and-severity) |
| **tombstone** | A `null` position in `registry.json`: the line was deleted or replaced; its ID stays in the registry and can never be addressed again. | [§22.3](#223-how-ids-and-positions-change) |
| **transcript** | What a *scenario script* prints — standard output and standard error together. The console blocks of this guide are transcripts, with the root directory shortened. | [D.3](#d3-the-scenarios) |
| **undo** | `undo-descriptor`: reverses one applied descriptor through its inverse and marks it `undone`. A new edit, not a rollback — and a command with sharp edges (V1, V12, V23, V24). | [§44.6](#446-undo_descriptor) |
| **validated** | The status of a batch after a passing `validate-plan`: `apply_order` is fixed and the batch holds its locks. | [§26.2](#262-states) |
| **WAL** | `wal.jsonl`, the write-ahead log: an append-only record of what began and what finished, one JSON object per line. | [§34.1](#341-the-write-ahead-log) |

### The reference labels

| Label | Stands for | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **V1 … V31** | the register of behavior verified to differ from the documentation, or never mentioned in it | [§56](#56-verified-behaviors-and-deviations-from-the-documentation) |
| **S1 … S10** | trust and security findings | [§57](#57-trust-model-and-security-notes) |
| **L1 … L23** | the limitations that the tool's own documentation states, each re-tested | [§55](#55-stated-limitations-and-their-verification-status) |
| **m1 … m15** | minor findings | [§56.9](#569-minor-findings) |
| **G1 … G12** | the guarantees of the tool | [§54.1](#541-the-guarantees) |
| **BP1 … BP52** | best-practice rules | [§58](#58-best-practices) |
| **E1 … E10** | the text edge cases of the scenarios (there is no E8) | [D.4](#d4-text-edge-cases) |
| **R1 … R6, DS1 … DS4, BL1, LK1, CP1, WL1** | the rules a healthy state satisfies | [B.5](#b5-what-a-healthy-state-satisfies) |
| **A … C** (crash windows), **GD1 … GD5**, **DR1 … DR4**, **RL1 … RL4**, **LINT-A … LINT-D**, **AB-A**, **AB-B** | scenario codes: the crash windows, and the tests of the guide's own programs — the guard, the driver, the lock release, the plan lint and the abbreviation test | [D.5](#d5-the-crash-harness), [D.8](#d8-tests-of-the-programs-of-part-ix) |
